Toggling system settings for titlebar and window accent color should be reflected without having to restart the application

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')

function createWindow () {
  const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    frame: false,
    titleBarOverlay: true,
  })

  mainWindow.loadFile('index.html')
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  createWindow()
})

app.on('window-all-closed', function () {

* Disable the system setting

author: alexhaugland
title: long-animation-frame events don't contain script attribution
body:
### Preflight Checklist

macOS

### Operating System Version

Sequoia 15.5

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

n/a

### Expected Behavior

Long animation frames (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/long-animation-frames) should come with script attribution, making it easy to figure out which scripts are contributing to hitches in your application. If I take [this fiddle](https://gist.github.com/alexhaugland/498d878b7fff5a578c0ca6da03d836f8) and serve the index.html from python (`python3 -m http.server 9911` or similar) then I get nice console logs like this:
```json
obs1 {
    "name": "long-animation-frame",
    "entryType": "long-animation-frame",
    "startTime": 905.7000000476837,
    "duration": 250.964,
    "renderStart": 0,
    "styleAndLayoutStart": 0,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 0,
    "blockingDuration": 200.964,
    "scripts": [
        {
            "name": "script",
            "entryType": "script",
            "startTime": 905.8999998569489,
            "duration": 250,
            "invoker": "DOMWindow.onkeydown",
            "invokerType": "event-listener",
            "windowAttribution": "self",
            "executionStart": 905.8999998569489,
            "forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration": 0,
            "pauseDuration": 0,
            "sourceURL": "http://localhost:9911/",
            "sourceFunctionName": "block",
            "sourceCharPosition": 19
        }
    ]
}
```

The script attribution here makes it easy to figure out which script is causing the stuttering. The specific code in the fiddle was adopted from https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals/blob/8a54167b8a455128bd5ae0f3729c3e81ea146f62/test/views/inp.njk. 

### Actual Behavior

When loading the [above fiddle](https://gist.github.com/alexhaugland/498d878b7fff5a578c0ca6da03d836f8) I do not observe the same behavior. The events look more like:
```json
obs1 {
    "name": "long-animation-frame",
    "entryType": "long-animation-frame",
    "startTime": 2289.7000000476837,
    "duration": 151.39999985694885,
    "renderStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "styleAndLayoutStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 2287.7999999523163,
    "blockingDuration": 101.355,
    "scripts": []
}

obs2 {
    "name": "long-animation-frame",
    "entryType": "long-animation-frame",
    "startTime": 2289.7000000476837,
    "duration": 151.39999985694885,
    "renderStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "styleAndLayoutStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 2287.7999999523163,
    "blockingDuration": 101.355,
    "scripts": []
} 
```
and contain no script attribution at all. I see similar behavior if I load the `index.html` as a `file://` url which could be related.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/alexhaugland/498d878b7fff5a578c0ca6da03d836f8

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: kriskowal
title: Node.js child_process.fork recurses on arvg[1] and not given module path in packaged application
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Darwin  23.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0: Thu Mar  6 21:58:03 PST 2025; root:xnu-10063.141.1.704.6~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Given a fresh Electron application generated from the default template, and using `child_process.fork` in the main process, Electron should spawn the corresponding Helper as Node.js and execute the specified module both during development `npm run start` and in the generated application with `npm run make`.

The linked repository isolates the observed behavior:
https://github.com/kriskowal/electron-isolate-fork-defect/

```js
if (process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) {
  console.error('unexpected');
  console.error(__filename);
  console.error(process.argv);
  console.error(process.env);
  return;
}
const { fork } = require('node:child_process');
const path = require('node:path');
fork(path.join(__dirname, 'child.js'), [], {});
```

For this program, I expect `npm run start` to behave the same as `npm run make && out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork`. They should print out `expected` (as evidence that `child.js` executed).

### Actual Behavior

Running `npm run start` works as expected.

Running `npm run make && out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork`, the application logs `unexpected` with the diagnostic information indicating that `fork` enters `main.js` instead of `child.js`.

```
unexpected
/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/src/index.js
[
  '/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Frameworks/isolate-fork Helper.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork Helper',
  '/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/src/child.js'
]
{
  ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1',
.
.
.
```

https://github.com/kriskowal/electron-isolate-fork-defect/blob/main/src/index.js

### Problem Description

I want to show my electron app on a specific monitor that the user chooses. This should persist even after system restarts or unplugging and plugging them again in a different order. 



### Proposed Solution

Add the serial number of the monitor or the PnP device ID to the Display properties. This way we can easily identify the right monitor in any circumstance.

### Alternatives Considered

Currently, Display object in Electron has no properties that can be used for this. Screen sizes can be the same, screen position can be rearranged and id is unique but not persistent across system reboots.

x64

34.0.0

### Expected Behavior

Electron apps should start normally and the [Steam overlay](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/overlay) should function without issue.

### Actual Behavior

The Steam overlay briefly flashes and then disappears entirely. It remains disabled until a full system reboot.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Notes:**
I realize this may be a niche use case, so I understand if support is limited. However, I'd appreciate any guidance on what might be causing the issue. I'm happy to assist in tracking it down (I am a developer), though I'm not familiar with the Electron codebase. Are there any command-line flags I could try that might help? I'm open to testing and looking for any direction.

**Is this a Steam issue?**
That was my initial assumption. However, there were no Steam updates when the problem began. The issue started immediately after updating from Electron 34 to 35. Reverting to Electron 34 resolves it, and upgrading again reintroduces the bug.

**Relevance:**
Steam is a major platform, and many apps built with Electron integrate with it, so maintaining overlay compatibility could benefit a lot of developers.

author: jking-realyze
title: shell.openPath is blocking on Linux when it should be non-blocking
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

shell.openPath should not be a blocking call.

### Actual Behavior

On Linux shell.openPath _is_ a blocking call.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Here is the linux implementation of shell.openPath (`shell/common/platform_util_linux.cc:349`)
```
void OpenPath(const base::FilePath& full_path, OpenCallback callback) {
  // This is async, so we don't care about the return value.
  XDGOpen(full_path.DirName(), full_path.value(), true, std::move(callback));
}
```
The third argument to `XDGOpen` is `true`. That argument is named `wait_for_exit` and causes the call to `XDGOpen` to be synchronous when true. (`XDGOpen` is defined on line 276 of the same file.)

That `true` should be `false`.

author: himself65
title: support `electron` conditional exports
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

This spec if from WInterCG https://runtime-keys.proposal.wintercg.org/ (https://github.com/WinterTC55/runtime-keys) initial proposal from https://github.com/WinterTC55/runtime-keys/pull/2 by @Ethan-Arrowood.

I thought electron really take care of this key but actually it's not :(

```diff
"exports": {
+ "electron": "./fake-module.electron.js",
  "node": "./fake-module.node.js",
  "default": "./fake-module.js"
},
```

I think this is super useful, since electron main thread runtime has some specific feature, like `require('electron')` does exist, and tons of API inside.

### Proposed Solution

support this feature

### Alternatives Considered

add `--condition electron` on startup?

### Additional Information

reproduce: https://github.com/himself65/electron-conditional-exports

title: Passing transferrable objects (OffscreenCanvas, VideoFrame) between OOP iframe and window doesn't work
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

No errors when drawing on transferred canvas

VideoFrame transfer works


### Actual Behavior

Iframe crashes as blank grey, when tryng to write to transferred canvas

VideoFrame transfers as null

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I trying to stream canvas content from iframe to main window. But none of the effective methods of transferring image data works. In Chrome this example works well.

Main window:
```
const offscreenCanvas = document.querySelector('canvas').transferControlToOffscreen();
document.querySelector('iframe').contentWindow.postMessage({ offscreenCanvas }, '*', [offscreenCanvas])
```

IFrame:
```
window.addEventListener('message', (ev) => ev.data.offscreenCanvas.getContext('2d').clearRect(0, 0, 100, 100))
```

I also tried transfer VideoFrame and ArrayBuffer. VideoFrame transfers as null, ArrayBuffer transfers successfuly but it looks like it transfers data copy, not the reference, so it makes huge load on GC trying to stream 60fps.



Is there any fundamental issues in cross process object transfer in electron, or maybe some flags that could make it work?

body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows Server 2025 24H2, Windows 10 22H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

35.0.0-nightly.20241104

### Expected Behavior

WebAssembly should not run slower in newer versions of Electron.

### Actual Behavior

WebAssembly runs up to twice as slow in versions of electron after version 35.0.0-nightly.20241104, starting from 35.0.0-nightly.20241107. Stable Electron 34 is also affected after 34.0.0-alpha.7.

Chromium is also affected by this issue.

Here is a comparison between Electron 33 (performs the same as 35.0.0-nightly.20241104), Chrome (Brave) 138, and Firefox 141: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a818948f-4a19-46dd-a9f4-5529dbb992d0

The test cases can be accessed via the gist url or on https://permille.io/WasmPerformanceRegression/

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/c3defad16b251ddcddde5e8de3814536

### Additional Information

This is the electron fiddle for 35.0.0-nightly.20241107, the nightly version immediately after the performance regression: https://gist.github.com/5a4d6e7d013b970a0c4394a594551f1e

These tests were run on an Intel i7 7700k cpu.

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro, version 22H2 (OS Build 19045.4412)

### What arch are you using?

ia32

### Last Known Working Electron version

34.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The file "ffmpeg-v36.1.0-win32-ia32.zip" should contain a 32-bit (x86) ffmpeg.dll, compatible with 32-bit Windows systems and builds.

### Actual Behavior

The file "ffmpeg-v36.1.0-win32-ia32.zip" incorrectly contains a 64-bit (x64) ffmpeg.dll, even though the file name indicates it is for 32-bit systems.

This breaks:

32-bit app builds

Tools like electron-packager-plugin-non-proprietary-codecs-ffmpeg

Electron apps targeting ia32 platforms

### Testcase Gist URL

This issue doesn't require a runtime repro, as it's strictly related to release asset content.

### Additional Information

Steps to Reproduce:

Download the asset:
ffmpeg-v36.1.0-win32-ia32.zip from "https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v36.1.0/ffmpeg-v36.1.0-win32-ia32.zip"

Extract the file and locate ffmpeg.dll.

Run Sysinternals Sigcheck(https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sigcheck) or any binary inspector:

sigcheck.exe ffmpeg.dll


Output:
MachineType: 64-bit



This issue starts from Electron v34.1.0 and continues in v36.1.0.

The ffmpeg.dll included in the win32-ia32 ZIP package is not actually 32-bit, which breaks compatibility and leads to runtime crashes on 32-bit systems.

The issue was confirmed using sigcheck and comparing the DLL against earlier versions.

Please repackage the correct ffmpeg.dll (32-bit) for win32-ia32 and update the affected release assets.

author: kaovilai
title: Feature Request: desktopCapturer.getSources() should return actual monitor names instead of generic "Screen 1", "Screen 2"
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, when using `desktopCapturer.getSources()` to get available screens for screen sharing, Electron returns generic names like "Screen 1", "Screen 2", "Screen 3" for multiple monitors. This makes it difficult for users to identify which physical monitor they want to share, especially when they have multiple monitors of the same resolution.

This issue has been raised by users of applications like Deskreen (see https://github.com/pavlobu/deskreen/issues/283) where the lack of descriptive monitor names creates a poor user experience.

### Proposed Solution

Enhance the `desktopCapturer.getSources()` API to return actual monitor model names that help users identify their displays. For example:
- "LG 27UK850" instead of "Screen 1"
- "Dell U2720Q" instead of "Screen 2"
- "MacBook Pro Built-in Display" instead of "Screen 3"

### Implementation Approach

The implementation would require platform-specific code to query display information:

**macOS**: Use Core Graphics API
```cpp
CFStringRef displayName = CGDisplayCopyDisplayName(displayID);
```

**Windows**: Use Windows Display Configuration API
```cpp
DISPLAYCONFIG_TARGET_DEVICE_NAME targetName;
DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo(&targetName);
```

**Linux**: Use X11/XRandR or Wayland protocols (implementation varies by display server)

The display names would be mapped to the existing display IDs returned by `desktopCapturer.getSources()`.

### Alternatives Considered

1. **Adding a new API**: Create a separate API like `screen.getDisplayNames()` that returns a mapping of display IDs to friendly names. However, this would require developers to manually correlate the data.

2. **Optional parameter**: Add an optional parameter to `getSources()` to request detailed display information. This maintains backward compatibility while providing the feature when needed.

### Additional Information

- This feature would significantly improve user experience in screen sharing scenarios
- The implementation complexity varies by platform, with Linux being the most fragmented due to different display servers
- This enhancement would benefit all Electron applications that use screen sharing functionality
- Similar functionality exists in native applications on all major platforms

Would the Electron team be open to a PR implementing this feature? I'd be happy to work on the implementation if this aligns with the project's goals.

author: G0rocks
title: Add Icelandic spell check support
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

When I type in Icelandic in [obsidian](https://obsidian.md/) then I get a lot of red squiggly error lines below the words since obsidian doesn't support Icelandic for spell checking.
According to [this post](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/icelandic-spellcheck/39062/2) on the obsidian forums from 2022 then "We use the spellchecker provided by electron which in turn uses chrome or macos’ spellchecker. IF they have it, we have it, If they don’t we don’t. Nothing we can do about it." which is why I post this here.

The only other issue I found about this by searching "icelandic" was [this one](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/586) but it is very different.

### Proposed Solution

I have 2 ideas for a solution but all of them are to add Icelandic as a spell check languages.

1. Find a language pack online and add it. I found these potential sources:
     - From Árnastofnun: http://www.bin.arnastofnun.is (They have a CC BY-SA 4.0 license)
     - From Microsoft: https://www.microsoft.com/is-is/download/details.aspx?id=51200 (Unsure about licensing but microsoft points to [this page](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/terms-of-use))
     - From Aspell: http://aspell.net/ which I learned about from [here](https://harabanar.com/2010/02/09/villuleit-a-islensku-i-wordpress/) About the license, I didn't see which one they use but they do say it is "Free and Open Source"
     - From libreoffice: https://extensions.libreoffice.org/en/extensions/show/hunspell-is-the-icelandic-spelling-dictionary-project Which I learned about from [here](https://github.com/recette-lemon/vim-spell-is) which seems to use [CC-BY](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) license

2. Make a new language pack by having people add it to the language pack directly through obsidian. This sounds like a lot more work but is a real solution.

I lean most towards using idea 1.

### Alternatives Considered

I have considered and currently am using the method of adding every single Icelandic word and inflection of each word to the english dictionary that is already in use in obsidian.
This is very tedious and quite boring but it does work.

### Additional Information

Obsidian version 1.8.10

author: aesopov
title: Introduce the window.beginDrag() function to trigger native window dragging
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Modern browsers such as Chrome allow users to drag tabs out of the main window to create new ones, providing a seamless, OS-integrated window dragging experience. In Electron, replicating this behavior is currently not possible using native APIs.

When implementing a similar feature (dragging a tab to create a new window), developers must simulate dragging by:

- Listening to mouse events in the original window.
- Creating a new BrowserWindow.
- Manually updating its position based on mouse movements.

This approach is:

**Non-performant** on low-end systems or virtual machines.
**Incompatible with OS-native behaviors** like window snapping, drag previews, or aero shake.
**Complex** to implement and maintain.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce a `window.beginDrag()` (or similar) method on BaseWindow that programmatically initiates native window dragging behavior, as if the user clicked and dragged the title bar.

**Example usage:**

```typescript
const newWin = new BaseWindow({ /* options */ });
newWin.beginDrag(); // Starts native drag immediately
```

This API should:

- Begin an OS-native drag for the given window.
- Respect platform-specific behaviors (snapping, animations, etc.).
- Optionally accept mouse position offsets.

### Alternatives Considered

**Alternatives Considered**
- **Manual window repositioning** using `win.setBounds()` or `win.setPosition()`:
Works but lacks OS integration and performs poorly on some environments.

- `Transparent windows with drag regions`:
Fragile and limited; doesn't cover the use case where a new window is created and dragged.

- `Simulating drag using drag-and-drop APIs`:
Not intended for window control; only handles DOM elements.

### Additional Information

**Prior Art**
- Neutralino.js introduced this functionality in its latest release with window.startDrag(), improving UX for lightweight desktop apps.
- Chrome and other browsers have long supported native tab detaching with drag behaviors.

author: samuelmaddock
title: Refactor APIs to use frame tokens
body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I am a [maintainer](https://github.com/orgs/electron/people) of the Electron project. (If not, please create a [different issue type](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/).)

### Description

Frame routing IDs were recently removed from the renderer process upstream. We should refactor frame-related APIs to use frame tokens instead.

Related:
- https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47616
- https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47717
- https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47850

## WebContents

- [ ] 'did-fail-load' event
- [ ] 'did-fail-provisional-load' event
- [ ] 'did-frame-finish-load' event
- [ ] 'did-frame-navigate' event
- [ ] 'did-navigate-in-page' event

Events which pass in `frameProcessId` and `frameRoutingId` as a parameters should be redesigned to set them as properties on the `Event` object. See past work in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/37085

Where possible, a `WebFrameMain` instance as a `frame` property should be preferred over individual frame identifier properties.

## Webview

- [ ] 'will-frame-navigate' event
- [ ] 'did-start-navigation' event
- [ ] 'did-redirect-navigation' event
- [ ] 'did-frame-navigate' event

These use `frameRoutingId` as a parameter. If we are to replace this parameter, it will need to go through a breaking change in a major release.

title: The size of temporary file created by Electron always increase when loading images
body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 37.2.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When Electron app launches, it creates a `{uuid}.tmp` file in the `C:\Users\{username}\AppData\Local\Temp ` folder. If the Electron app does not contain any images, the size of this file is always 0 byte. If the Electron app displays multiple images, the size of this file increases proportionally to the images size. The size of this `tmp` file can grow unbounded to 10GB for some of our users. Expected behavior: the file size should not grow unbounded and cause the hard disk to run out of space. ### Actual Behavior The size of the `tmp` file increases and can cause hard disk to run out of space. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/thomasdao/74f9d9996ce7dea50dd86c72bfc0f2bf ### Additional Information In File Explorer, it's easier to sort the files in Temp folder by "Date modified" descending, so the `uuid`.tmp file created by this sample appears on top. You need to press "Delete" key to try to delete the file, then the system will show a warning this file is being used by Electron, and show the most updated size of the file. Please note that due to system caching, you may need to wait for up to 30 seconds and try deleting a few times for the real size to be shown in the warning dialog.

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 15.6

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

27.3.11

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`<video>` tag should work with any video, also 10-bit HEVC.

To reproduce: https://github.com/mifi/electron-mas-video-bug

It should show a video player that allows playing back the video, this expected behaviour can be seen by simply running the unsigned app:
```
npx electron main.js
```


### Actual Behavior

Since Electron 27.3.11, the bug appears:

With the [example](https://github.com/mifi/electron-mas-video-bug), observe that the window goes completely blank (background color is still visible). It's sometimes flashing if you move your mouse around in the window. Not only the `<video>` goes blank but the whole rendering of the window content blanks out, even chrome dev tools stops working. Once the video is hidden or removed from the DOM, the rendering recovers and all content re-appears. It does not crash the app in any way, the app is still interactive, even the UI that is not being rendered is still interactive, and the video can be played back (with audio). Once the `<video>` element is removed, or the `src` is set to a different video, the rendering instantly recovers.

- Downgrading Electron to 27.3.11 works (no bug).
- Electron version from 28.0.0 until 28.1.1 app hard crashes on launch (even non-signed)
- Electron versions from 28.1.2 until 37.2.5 shows the bug

author: rcombs
title: [Feature] Expose NSMenuItem.alternate in Menu API
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The NSMenuItem class on macOS supports an "[alternate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsmenuitem/isalternate?language=objc)" property, allowing a pair of adjacent sibling menu items to be joined together into what the user perceives as a single visible item that changes its title, key-equivalent, and behavior depending on what modifier keys are held.

For instance, in the File menu, Chrome's "Close All" item is an alternate of the preceding "Close Tab", available when holding the alt/option key. Safari similarly has "Close Other Tabs" as an alternate of "Close Tab".

This functionality is useful, but is not currently exposed by Electron.

### Proposed Solution

It should be fairly straightforward to add a `base::flat_map<int, bool> alternateFlags_;` to `ElectronMenuModel`, expose it to C++ and JS, and do something like this in `electron_menu_controller.mm `:
```objective-c++
    if (model->IsAlternateAt(index))
      [item setAlternate:YES];
```

Note that it would also be useful to support alternate pairs that *don't* have accelerators (but do have modifier masks). This is done by calling `setKeyEquivalentModifierMask` without `setKeyEquivalent` (or by calling `setKeyEquivalent` with an empty string). This is used in Chrome for eg "Tab -> Duplicate Selected Tab", which is an alternate of `Tab -> Duplicate Tab` with a modifier mask of `Option`. This could probably be implemented by skipping the `setKeyEquivalent` call if `character <= 0`, though I'm not sure if there are other API/parser issues there.

### Alternatives Considered

Apps can already update their menus (and behavior) manually in response to key events, but this is clunky for the developer, and doesn't offer the full functionality that the alternate flag does. With the alternate flag, the user is able to rebind the keyboard shortcut for either or both of the menu items in System Settings, with the UI automatically updating accordingly.

Apps can also simply add all actions to their menus without setting the alternate flag, but this can result in an excessively-cluttered menu.

### Additional Information

This was previously proposed in #20902, but it was closed out as "completed" by the filer despite not actually being implemented.

author: benbucksch
title: `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` must handle exceptions and user cancellation
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

any

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

any

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

### Problem

How can the app callback signal to the `getDisplayMedia()` caller that it wants to abort the window selection and deny the screen share?

### Reproduction

1. Some page JS calls `await navigator.getDisplayMedia()`. For the page, the call stalls here.
2. On the web, this would call the browser UI to select a window to share. In Electron, this calls the app handler that was passed to `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()`.
3. The app handler then brings up a UI dialog to allow the user to select the window to share
4. The user aborts the selection, by clicking [Cancel], because he changed his mind and doesn't want to share the screen.
5. To signal the abort, the UI dialog throws an exception into the handler.
(There is no other way to tell electron `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` and the waiting `getDisplayMedia()` that the selection was aborted.)

### Expected result
1. `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` catches the exception
2. It throws the same exception into the caller of `getDisplayMedia()`.
3. This terminates the screen share in a defined way.
4. The UI that called `getDisplayMedia()` catches the exception and handles it.


### Actual Behavior

1. `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` doesn't catch the exception
2. This triggers an `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning`.
3. The screen sharing now hangs.
4. Starting another screen sharing will cause `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` or `desktopCapturer.getSources()` (?) to throw, causing another `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning`.
5. In some cases, the problem persists even after an app restart. This suggests that something goes badly wrong.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: clavin
title: Deprecate & remove `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT` env var
body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I am a [maintainer](https://github.com/orgs/electron/people) of the Electron project. (If not, please create a [different issue type](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/).)

### Description

## Timeline

* **Deprecation**: Electron 38
* **Removal**: Electron 39

## Background

While working on the [main upgrade roll](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47983) for Electron 39, [this change](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6819616) that removes the `--ozone-platform-hint` flag was causing an error. After tracking it back to a change, I discovered the flag was being removed because [the default value became `auto`](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6775426). That change landed in [Chromium 140](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/3cf2a1826b002326a2d2994a489e98eebc340054) which is part of Electron 38.

Curious about our env var's intended behavior, I searched through the history of it. I learned it was [added](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/39792) to make it simple for users to tell Electron apps to automatically detect Wayland.[^1] Since the `auto` behavior is now the default, `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`'s purpose is equivalent to `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` and we can remove it without losing any convenience for those Wayland users.

I plan to do that removal in Electron 39, allowing app users to anticipate the removal. The removal will be backwards-compatible, so users running apps with Electron 38 and below will continue to accept the `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT` and Electron 39 and above will safely ignore it.

[^1]: It can also be set to `wayland` to force Wayland instead of potentially falling back to X11; however, `auto` works by inspecting the `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` env var, meaning ours now acts like an alias for that one.

On mobile view, the "Use the tools you love" section should display tool icons in a compact and responsive layout that doesn't consume excessive vertical space. The gallery section should have hover interactions, and the site should offer installability via PWA features.


### Actual Behavior

- After toggling to light mode, the hero section and navbar remain black instead of turning white.
- On mobile, the "Use the tools you love" logos are stacked vertically, making it look cluttered and take up a lot of screen space.
- The gallery section is static with no hover effects or animations.
- The site doesn’t support PWA installation or offline access.


### Testcase Gist URL

Not applicable – this issue is related to the website UI (https://www.electronjs.org), not Electron’s runtime or API.

### Additional Information

- Dark mode UI inconsistency was observed on desktop (Chrome, Brave browsers).
- Mobile responsiveness issue tested on Chrome Android and responsive view in DevTools.
- Suggest adding PWA support to enable offline documentation access and installability.
- Happy to help with a PR if any of these enhancements are accepted by the team.

title: NodeJS module-sync target support
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

## Introduction
I know this is a high traffic issue so i will justify that i know what i say.
I am aware of the ESM Support electron dlopen and i am v8 engineer i am aware of intrinsic and embedding node inside chrome. i know all Electron ESM issues i understand that some settings need to get exported Sync before the embedding gets used.

### Feature Use Case

There is a new import condition for NodeJS called 'module-sync' it is the missing block to require ESScripts see: module-sync in https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#conditional-exports

"module-sync" - matches no matter the package is loaded via import, import() or require(). The format is expected to be ES modules that does not contain top-level await in its module graph - if it does, ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE will be thrown when the module is require()-ed.

so it is able to be seen as ideal forward migration for all existing CJS code that does not depend on complex nativ embedded behavior when nodejs is used as embedded runtime. 

### Proposed Solution

Electron can default and exclusiv use the ModuleSync target.

## Bonus.
good solution to detect it:

--experimental-print-required-tla[#](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--experimental-print-required-tla)
Added in: v22.0.0, v20.17.0
If the ES module being require()'d contains top-level await, this flag allows Node.js to evaluate the module, try to locate the top-level awaits, and print their location to help users find them.

--experimental-require-module

### Alternatives Considered

all alternatives are in the old ESM issues you know them start with .cjs then use import or use esm npm package which is a sync ESM loader Implemented in CJS .............

author: devmanbr
title: more video formats
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I have a use case where I need to "natively" play MKV, AVI, FLV, and other video formats that are usually unsupported by browsers, with support for audio tracks and subtitles. Due to the way Electron.js is built, and from what I have found over several days of research, I know that there is no native support for such formats and features. However, I believe this can be added more effectively than if it were done by a developer with less technical capability (like myself).

although I am looking at this from my own case, I believe that having this capability could be enriching, even for other types of projects.

### Proposed Solution

implementing support for the mentioned video formats (and others) through a more "native" approach that does not create much additional processing overhead, while being able to leverage hardware resources that, at best, Electron.js is better equipped to utilize.

### Alternatives Considered

integration with players like VLC and real-time transcoding. Both possibilities have been considered and attempted, but since I am not the most experienced developer for this type of process, I encountered significant performance issues (as I need to cater to PCs with modest configurations) and some security gaps.

### Additional Information

electron.js has been great for addressing various use cases over the years, and I believe that adding this native support will open up many possibilities for many developers. please consider this! thank you!

Yes

### Expected Behavior

The file picker (`<input type=file>`, `showOpenFilePicker`) should not allow selecting directories, only files.

### Actual Behavior

The file picker allows selecting directories if they match some of the given file extensions. The directory is exposed to JS as a File / FileSystemFileHandle, but fails to be read.

For example, the following code:

```
window.showOpenFilePicker({
    multiple: true,
    types: [
      {
        accept: {
          "application/octet-stream": [".foobar"],
        },
      },
    ],
  });
```

allows choosing directories named with ".foobar" even though they are not files.

### Additional Information

I have also filed an issue upstream with Chrome at https://issues.chromium.org/issues/438779953

### Expected Behavior

Description: 
We are evaluating the use of Electron v35.2.0 (downloaded from https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v35.2.0/electron-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip) 
Then download ffmpeg.dll (downloaded from https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v35.2.0/ffmpeg-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip)
To replace the same file from Electron v35.2.0 for ensuring under LGPL-2.0.
Our legal and compliance team has specific requirements regarding FFmpeg usage:

- If FFmpeg is used, it must be entirely under an LGPL license (no GPL components).
- FFmpeg must not include any Audio or Video Codecs; all codec functionality must be implemented by underlying Hardware or OS (e.g., GPU or Windows Media Foundation).

The prebuilt `ffmpeg.dll` in the v35.2.0 ZIP includes a `LICENSES.chromium.html` file stating FFmpeg is under LGPL-2.1+, which aligns with the LGPL requirement. However, we need confirmation on the following:
1. Does the FFmpeg in v35.2.0 use `ffmpeg_branding = "Chrome"` and `proprietary_codecs = false` as per the default build? build/args/ffmpeg.gn
2. Are there any software-implemented Audio or Video Codecs (e.g., H.264, AAC) included in the prebuilt `ffmpeg.dll`?
3. If software codecs are included, can we disable them in the prebuilt version, or must we rebuild ffmpeg from source to exclude them?

Steps to Reproduce
1. Download `electron-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip` from the release page.
2. Extract and inspect `ffmpeg.dll` and `LICENSES.chromium.html`.
3. Download `ffmpeg-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip` from the release page.
4. To replace the same file from Electron v35.2.0 for ensuring under LGPL-2.0.

Expected Behavior
- FFmpeg should be LGPL-2.1+ compliant with no GPL components.
- No software-implemented Audio or Video Codecs should be present; codec support should rely solely on Hardware/OS.

### Additional Information
- Electron version: v35.2.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)
- Compliance deadline: September 1, 2025

author: Sep29th
title: Playwright browser launched inside utilityProcess has no Internet connectivity
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

When attempting to launch a Playwright-controlled browser inside an Electron utilityProcess, the browser cannot access the Internet.

The same Playwright code works correctly when run in the main process or in a regular Node.js child process before packaging.

However, after packaging the Electron application, using child_process.fork() becomes very problematic (due to ASAR restrictions, lack of proper Node runtime, etc.).

utilityProcess seems like a good replacement for child_process.fork() because it works after packaging, but when running Playwright in it, the launched browser has no network access.

This makes it impossible to run Playwright in a packaged Electron app.

### Proposed Solution

Allow utilityProcess to support full networking capabilities so that processes launched from it can open TCP/UDP sockets and child processes (like Playwright browsers) without restrictions.

Ideally, provide an explicit option (similar to allowNetworking or equivalent) when calling utilityProcess.fork().

Ensure that browsers or other processes launched from inside utilityProcess inherit the necessary permissions to access the Internet.

### Alternatives Considered

...

### Additional Information

Electron version: [37.2.3]

Playwright version: [1.54.2]

OS: [Windows]

Expected behavior: Playwright browser launched inside utilityProcess should have Internet connectivity like it does in main process.

### Problem Description

Chromium bundles FFmpeg, so it is shipped in Electron as well.

It would be great to have Electron expose a module with bindings to this bundled FFmpeg.

### Proposed Solution

Create a module that exposes bindings to FFmpeg from the main process.

### Alternatives Considered

Installing a third-party node bindings module dependency, but it is not as reliable as binding directly to the bundled FFmpeg from Electron. There may be incompatibilities caused by the FFmpeg version, and the binary may not be found at the expected locations. By bundling directly to Electron, both problems can be avoided, and the exposed bindings can match the FFmpeg API exactly.

author: andersk
title: [24.1.0 regression] Unsandboxed preload is restricted by Content-Security-Policy, but only after `readyState` becomes `interactive`
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

NixOS 25.11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

24.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

For a given preload script execution, runtime code generation via `eval` and `new Function(…)` should be consistently allowed, or consistently disallowed, depending on the Content-Security-Policy.

### Actual Behavior

As of #37756 (22.3.6, 23.2.3, 24.1.0), Electron enforces the Content-Security-Policy `script-src` for preload scripts with `sandbox: false`. However, it does so incompletely: even in the presence of a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, code generation is still allowed until `document.readyState` becomes `interactive`, at which point it becomes disallowed.

This breaks CSP detection techniques used by libraries like Zod. The first time any object schema is declared, Zod uses `try { new Function("") }` to detect whether code generation is allowed, and caches the result forever ([source](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/v4.1.5/packages/zod/src/v4/core/util.ts#L362-L375)). That should be a reasonable thing to do, but when Electron unexpectedly disallows code generation after execution has already begun, Zod starts crashing with `Uncaught EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/andersk/40e446d2932d0656821d179a8735dc72

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: 12joan
title: Accelerators such as `CmdOrCtrl+B` do not work while `contenteditable` elements are focused
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. The developer defines an accelerator for `CmdOrCtrl+B` in the application menu
2. The user focuses a `contenteditable` element inside the Electron app
3. The user presses `command+b` or `ctrl+b`
4. The menu item with the `CmdOrCtrl+B` accelerator is activated

### Actual Behavior

When the user presses `command+b` inside the `contenteditable` element, Chromium intercepts this and fires a `beforeinput` event with an input type of `formatBold`. Editors that support this (including default `contenteditable` elements) will apply the bold formatting as a result.

However, the keyboard shortcut is never handled by Electron, and the menu item is never activated.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/12joan/92d28dc884dd25103eb51e3ebb83ccee

### Additional Information

This causes problems when the intended behaviour of the menu item differs from what Chromium assumes. For example, the editor might not support bold formatting, and the developer might want `command+b` to open the user's bookmarks instead.

> Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

This is presumably an intentional behaviour of Chromium to prevent browser keyboard shortcuts from colliding with the default `contenteditable` shortcuts. However, this behaviour is unlikely to be useful in Electron. If the developer defines an accelerator, it should take precedence over Chromium's default behaviour.

I wasn't able to find any way of overriding this behaviour. Calling `preventDefault` on the `beforeinput` event prevents Chromium's native behaviour of toggling bold, but Electron still isn't able to handle the keyboard shortcut itself.

In addition to `command+b`, the same thing applies to `command+i` and `command+u`, and possibly other keyboard shortcuts that I haven't encountered yet.

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When using goForward() to navigate to any page, navigationHistory.canGoBack() and canGoForward() should maintain accurate state regardless of page content.

### Actual Behavior

When using goForward() to navigate to a page containing iframes, the navigationHistory gets corrupted:

- History length suddenly decreases
- canGoBack() and canGoForward() return false when they should return true
- Navigation state becomes inconsistent

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a WebContentsView with navigationHistory tracking
2. Navigate through several pages to build up history (e.g., 6+ entries)
3. Use goBack() multiple times to go to earlier pages
4. Use goForward() to navigate to a page that contains iframes
5. Observe that navigationHistory suddenly becomes corrupted

### Code Example
```typescript
// Navigation event tracking
tab.webContentsView.webContents.on("did-navigate-in-page", (_, navigationUrl, isMainFrame) => {
  if (isMainFrame) {
    const history = tab.webContentsView.webContents.navigationHistory;
    console.log(
      `🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: ${history.canGoBack()}/${history.canGoForward()} == ${history.getActiveIndex()}/${history.length()}`
    );
  }
});

// goForward
webContentsView.webContents.navigationHistory.goForward();
```

### console output
```text
// Normal navigation - working correctly
🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: true/true == 2/11

// goForward() to page with iframe - navigationHistory corrupted
🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: false/false == 3/4  ← History corrupted: length changed from 11 to 4
```

author: RastislavKish
title: Accessibility: Hidden windows present themselves as active to Linux screenreaders
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Tested on Electron 35+, probably affects older releases, too

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

openSUSE Tumbleweed 20250904

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When calling the .hide() method on a BrowserWindow instance, the window disappears from the screen, and should also fire a window deactivate accessibility event to screenreaders through at-spi. When queried for its state by a running screenreader, the window should report itself as inactive until it's shown again. These mechanisms allow the screenreaders to determine which window is currently focused, and provide the user with appropriate feedback and various navigation tools.

### Actual Behavior

After calling the .hide() method, the window disappears, but the deactivation a11y event is not fired and when queried by the assistive tech, the window presents itself as active despite it's hidden.

This is a quite severe problem for Linux screenreaders. The user may be running various popular Electron apps like Signal, Element or Discord in the background, but these all report themselves as active to the screenreader, which afterwards often reads a completely different window to the user from the one they actually want to use, because it's unable to determine which of them is really focused.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/RastislavKish/c9ec92351be7c9e77d965e601465f4c9

### Additional Information

Reproduction steps

Detecting the status of windows with a screenreader directly is complicated, because Orca, the Linux screenreader, applies some mitigations against this problem, and so the results can be somewhat unpredictable. But there is an official Orca script which prints plain at-spi window activations and deactivations to the terminal, as well as a list of windows claiming to be active. This python script only requires at-spi2-core-dev libraries and the gobject introspection libraries, which are both included in the repositories of all major distributions.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Clone the official Orca repository and cd into the tools directory:

```sh
git clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/orca.git
cd orca/tools
```

2. Turn on Orca, so we can be sure the Electron a11y stack starts properly.
3. Start Electron fiddle, and load the attached gist. This gist is the standard hello world app, which after 5 seconds upon launch calls mainWindow.hide()
4. Return to the terminal, and launch:

```sh
python3 dump-window-events.py
```

5. Switch the window, either by mouse or by using Alt+Tab, back to the Electron fiddle and hit F5 to run the gist.
6. Wait until the Hello world app launches, stays for 5 seconds and disappears.
7. Switch the window, either by mouse or pressing Alt+Tab, back to the terminal with the running script. The script should notice the terminal has been focused and exit automatically. Check the output.

In the output, you should see the Hello world app fires the activation event when it first appears on the screen, but then does not fire the deactivation event when it hides, and when switching windows, it keeps reporting itself as being active, even though only one window should always be active at once.

I'm attaching the output of the command captured on my machine running GNOME 48.4 Wayland. Ignore everything from mutter-x11-frames, what matters for Orca are the events from the real apps.

Note: If you don't see *any* accessibility events from the electron apps, i.e. electron-fiddle and the Hello world app, it may be necessary to set the ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED environment variable to 1, and if it doesn't help, also use --force-renderer-accessibility flag with the Hello world app. Neither of these should be necessary by default when Orca is turned on, but there are certain setups where the AT auto-detection mechanism fails for various reasons.

[dump-window-events-output.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22191937/dump-window-events-output.log)

No

### Expected Behavior

According to the [documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/window-open), `window.open` allows a subset of the web preferences options, including `preload`. That said, calling `window.open("google.com", "_blank", "contextIsolation=no,preload=/path/to/preload.js")` should be able to open a window with the preload script executed when there is no hook defined in the main process.

> A subset of [WebPreferences](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/web-preferences) can be set directly, unnested, from the features string: zoomFactor, nodeIntegration, preload, javascript, contextIsolation, and webviewTag

### Actual Behavior

Calling `window.open("google.com", "_blank", "contextIsolation=no,preload=/path/to/preload.js")` in a window without any main-process hook cannot load the specified preload script in the new window.

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown; reproduces back to v36 at least

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Calling:
```js
app.relaunch()
app.quit()
```
should restart the app, regardless of how it's launched.

### Actual Behavior

If the application is launched by double-clicking on the executable within the built app, it restarts correctly.

If however, the built application is launched by running the executable from the command line, using a `.desktop` file; or the app is run unbuilt via `electron .`, the `relaunch()` call appears to have no effect, and the app simply quits and does not restart.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/ExodusMovement/electron-ubuntu-restart-minimal-repro

### Additional Information

Worth noting that due to https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/42510, it is necessary to `chown root` and `chmod 4755` the `chrome-sandbox` file before running from the command line. Oddly, a built application that has not had anything done to `chrome-sandbox` can be run by double-clicking the binary (in which case restarting also works); not sure if there's some connection there.

title: Accelerator null on predefined menu roles
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.

### Electron Version

38.1.0 and below

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When getting the menu via Menu.getApplicationMenu(), the accelerators should not be null for the predefined menu roles such as copy, paste, etc.

### Actual Behavior

Any menu items with a user-defined accelerator correctly returns the accelerator, but any of the predefined menu roles such as undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, etc. return null for the accelerator, despite those accelerators being registered and working.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/johnbwoodruff/725227db5ae734f73de6efd3af2a7960

### Additional Information

I had previously opened an issue for this, #34705, but it was closed due to no activity.

The accelerators are definitely defined for these predefined roles. The hotkeys work correctly, and they're displayed when the native menu is rendered. However, if you want to render your own custom menu, you won't know those accelerators as they are returned as `null`.

You can see in https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/5af6b898d92432369ce9495e75d75b02af651531/lib/browser/api/menu-item-roles.ts#L36-L41, for example, that all of these roles have accelerators properly defined. (hence why they work when you use them) So those accelerators should come through on the menu when using `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

I believe the fix should be here: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/api/menu-item.ts#L28

Specifically like so:

```this.overrideReadOnlyProperty('accelerator', roles.getDefaultAccelerator(this.role));```

I was going to submit a PR for this fix but I wasn't able to get the build environment working on my laptop so I couldn't properly validate the fix and I didn't want to submit a spam PR that hasn't followed the contribution guidelines.

author: tealsnow
title: Expose `xdg_toplevel::state` information on Wayland
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

[xdg_toplevel::state](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:enum:state) is an enum of different states a window/toplevel can be in exposed as an array in [xdg_toplevel::configure](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:event:configure).



### Proposed Solution

Specifically, I'd like access to the `tiled_*` information. `suspended` and `constrained_*` are not too useful for UI code, and are newer in the spec, so I don't expect those to be exposed.

Expose this information along the lines of `{ tiled: { left: boolean, right: boolean, etc. } }` on the window object through a (possibly Wayland only) API.

### Alternatives Considered

I believe native plugins are a thing. I'd consider using one of those if it is infeasible to expose in Electron directly.

### Additional Information

The `tiled_*` information is most useful when rendering rounded corners. If say the left side is tiled (an example of when is if the window was dragged to the left side of the monitor) knowing this in the application can conditionally apply window rounding for the sides that are not tiled.

I apologize if this information is already exposed. I wouldn't be surprised if similar information is exposed on Windows or OSX, and thus it is exposed under a different name. I only know the Wayland terminology.

author: leeyuchang
title: [Feature Request] Support tag and renotify from the Web Notification API in new Notification() (Electron)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

### **Summary**
Add tag and renotify options to Electron.Notification so apps can replace/coalesce notifications (by tag) and optionally re-alert the user when a tagged notification is updated—matching the Web Notification API semantics. See Electron’s current Notification docs and tutorial.

### **Motivation & Use Cases**

- Chat/Collab apps: keep only the latest per-thread/DM toast instead of spamming users; bump attention on important updates (renotify: true).
- Status summaries: “5 → 8 unread” replaces the same card by tag without adding a second toast.
- Cross-platform parity with Web: devs expect Web Notification API behavior in Electron renderers/main.

Pain today:
- No built-in way to replace the same logical notification.
- Apps must do OS-specific workarounds → inconsistent UX & more code.


### Proposed Solution

### **Proposed API**
interface NotificationConstructorOptions {
  // existing fields…
  tag?: string;       // Identifier to replace an existing notification with the same tag
  renotify?: boolean; // If replacing, re-alert user (sound/attention) when supported
}

### **Behavior**
- If tag is set and a visible (or Action Center/Notification Center) notification with the same tag exists, the new one replaces it.
- If renotify === true, replacement should re-alert where supported. If not supported, still replace (no-op on alert).



### Alternatives Considered

- App-level maps with manual .close() + .show(): works but error-prone and diverges per OS.
- Full custom toastXml on Windows only: loses cross-platform parity and adds platform branches.

### Additional Information

### **References**
[renotify](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notification/renotify)
[tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notification/tag)

author: mitchchn
title: Wayland app_id should be normalized to match wm_class
body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 38 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Fedora 42 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Apps should have the same wm_class (X11) and app_id (Wayland) by default. This allows desktop environments to look up the correct icons on both X11 and Wayland, based on a single .desktop file. e.g.., an app with `productName: "1Password"` should have its wm_class and app_id both normalized to "1password" to correspond with a "1password.desktop" file. It might also be a good idea to let developers specify the app_id and/or wm_class at runtime instead of relying on hard-to-understand semantics from fields in package.json. ### Actual Behavior Electron sets a lowercase wm_class and an uppercase app_id, both derived from the same fields in package.json (`productName`, `name`). If the source value isn't already lowercase, this causes some icons not loading properly on Wayland in certain environments, e.g. KDE. See 1Password, which shows its icon in the taskbar icon but is unable to show it in the Alt-Tab switcher or window corner: - productName: "1Password" - derived wm_class: `1password` - derived app_id: `1Password` - desktop file: `1password.desktop` ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information xdg documentation: https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:request:set_app_id

author: nmggithub
title: Utilize the macOS Keychain for ASAR Integrity
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While ASAR Integrity is a great feature, on macOS is uses the `Info.plist` file to store the expected hash. This works, I see two potential issues with it:
1. While, theoretically, `.app` packages are sealed on macOS, depending on certain configurations, the `Info.plist` can be editable by an outside app. Secondarily, it seems macOS does not check the integrity of `.app` package files on every launch, so an attacker could just find a way to modify the `app.asar` *and* the `Info.plist` and negate the ASAR Integrity check.
2. This could limit some custom auto-update solutions. While many auto-update solutions I have seen on Electron do work at the package level (meaning a new `.app` for each version), I have seen some that seem to mostly switch out JS files behind the scenes.

### Proposed Solution

I believe a better candidate for storage of the hash (at least on macOS) is the Keychain. By default, keychain items made by an app are only accessible by that app (unless the user explicitly changes an ACL). This would thwart most bad actors' attempts at changing the hash after compromising the `.asar` archive. While not totally foolproof (an attacker could socially engineer the user into giving up access to the keychain item containing the hash), I believe its better than the `Info.plist` method. Additionally, the macOS Keychain is already uses as part of [the safeStorage API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/safe-storage), so I don't believe using it for ASAR integrity would be that difficult.

### Alternatives Considered

N/A

### Additional Information

I'm a security researcher, first and foremost. While I do have fairly good software engineering experience, there may be certain blockers or quirks of Electron that make my proposed solution difficult to implement. I am open and willing to collaboratively discuss and adjust this feature request as needed.

title: Add support for macOS 26 .icon format in app.dock.setIcon()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

### Problem Description

macOS 26 introduced the new layered .icon format (supports tinted variants). Electron’s nativeImage / app.dock.setIcon() can’t load .icon, forcing developers to ship pre-rendered images and lose system-driven variants.

### Proposed Solution

Add .icon support to nativeImage and allow app.dock.setIcon() to accept a .icon path or nativeImage created from .icon. Preserve variant selection automatically.

### Alternatives Considered

Pre-render variant PNGs and switch at runtime with dock.setIcon() loses dynamic system rendering and increases asset maintenance.

### Additional Information

electron-builder will support new format https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/pull/9279

author: Stepnicka012
title: Support type="module" for <webview> to allow native ES Modules
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, the `<webview>` tag in Electron does not support native ES Modules. This forces developers using pure ESM projects to:
* Create additional preload scripts to import modules,
* Use `require()` (CommonJS), or
* Use `webview.executeJavaScript('import(...)')`, which is less clean and error-prone.
This creates inconsistencies in modern projects that adopt ESM in **renderer**, **main**, and **webview**, making migration and maintenance more difficult.

### Proposed Solution

Add support for a `type="module"` attribute on `<webview>`, similar to `<script type="module">`. Example usage:
```html
<webview
  src="https://example.com/app.js"
  type="module"
  nodeintegration="false"
  preload="./preload.mjs"
></webview>
```

Benefits:
1. Allows importing ES Modules directly inside the `<webview>` without workarounds.
2. Simplifies integration with modern frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte) using ESM.
3. Improves consistency between `BrowserWindow` and `<webview>`.
4. Reduces complexity of preload scripts and module management.

Technical consideration:
* Should be optional to avoid breaking CommonJS projects.
* Must respect existing sandbox and contextIsolation restrictions.
* Ideally compatible with both static and dynamic `import()` statements.

### Alternatives Considered

* Using preload scripts as modules (`.mjs`) and manually importing everything.
* Executing `import()` dynamically via `webview.executeJavaScript()`.
* Mixing CommonJS (`require()`) with ESM using Node’s `createRequire`.

All of these are workarounds and introduce complexity or potential errors, especially in fully ESM-based projects.

### Additional Information

This feature would make `<webview>` more aligned with the modern JavaScript ecosystem and significantly improve developer experience for Electron apps built entirely with ES Modules.

title: Add support for LanguageDetector and Translator APIs
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

In Electron at the moment, the [`LanguageDetector`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/language-detection) and [`Translator`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/translator-api) APIs appear to be present, but if called the language detector rejects with `UnknownError: Model not available`, and the `Translator` APIs never resolve the promise.

### Proposed Solution

Are the models for these in Chrome open/available for use in Electron? If so, it would be great if these could be made available. Given they're downloaded on demand in Chrome, I can see that would introduce a complication; being able to self-host the downloads would be good, but fine if they're just always downloaded from Google.

### Alternatives Considered

On Mac we could add a custom integration with the system translate APIs, but a built-in solution would be preferable due to easier maintenance and cross-platform compatibility. We could call out to an external service, but especially for language detection isn't suitable for our purposes; we want it to happen on device.

author: xushengfeng
title: Export supported web APIs
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The TypeScript team's policy mandates that Web API types only get included after being implemented in at least two browser engines. However, this constraint doesn't align with Electron's reality where we have a single Chrome-based runtime.

A concrete example is `navigator.bluetooth` - while functionally available in Electron, it triggers TypeScript type errors due to its exclusion from the official lib.d.ts definitions.

### Proposed Solution

It would be beneficial to have a type definition such as `import { type webapi } from "electron"` to enable `bluetooth` injection into the `navigator` object. This type should be automatically maintained to align with the Chrome versions supported by Electron.

### Alternatives Considered

write by developer self
```ts
declare global {
    interface navigator {
        bluetooth: ...
    }
}
```
