author: mitchchn
title: Windows shrink the first time they lose focus on Wayland
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

An 800x600 window should be able to keep consistent dimensions after creation, including when it loses focus. 

### Actual Behavior

An 800x600 window goes on a journey after you create it, first growing to its proper size after creation and then shrinking to about 785x580 (client size) if you click out of it to lose focus.

Logs from the Fiddle:

```
Main window bounds at creation: { x: 645, y: 172, width: 800, height: 600 }
Main window bounds after 1s: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 844, height: 644 }
Main window bounds after blur (assuming you manually de-focused it): { x: 0, y: 0, width: 822, height: 625 }
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mitchchn/7487efc43b208a3624ba464cb156860d

### Additional Information

Some context to help diagnose the root cause: on Wayland (and in GNOME specifically), Electron draws all window decorations using CSD, including titlebars, borderes, and shadows.

This means that an 800x600 BrowserWindow actually sits inside a larger 844x644 transparent frame into which the active shadows are drawn. When the window goes inactive, the shadows are drawn thinner, so the transparent frame shrinks.

This incorrectly causes the client area of the window to shrink as well, because it is still using the insets/padding to accommodate the thicker active shadows. (But for some reason everything works fine after the first time the window loses focus.)

author: mitchchn
title: BrowserWindow.getBounds() includes transparent space taken up by shadows on Wayland
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.2.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`BrowserWindow.getBounds()` should show the bounds of the visible, physical window (contentBounds + titlebar). It should not include the transparent area which surrounds the window to support shadows + resize handle hit targets.

### Actual Behavior

This window will report bounds of 800x600 immediately after creation, but soon reports larger bounds of 844x822, even though the visible window is still 800x600.

```  
const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js')
    }
  })

  // Will be 844x822
  setTimeout(() => {
    console.log("Main window bounds after 1s:", mainWindow.getBounds());
  }, 1000);
```
The larger bounds  are given because the window is surrounded by a transparent client-drawn frame to support shadows + hit targets, but this is an implementation detail. This is an issue because if an app implements window bounds saving/restoration, windows will grow a little more each time they are created. (This bug may have been filed already.)

## Isn't this what BrowserWindow.getContentBounds() is for?

No. `BrowserWindow.getContentBounds()` returns the web content bounds only, i.e. it subtracts the titlebar. For an 800x600 window, the bounds are:

- Total absolute bounds including transparent region; 844x822
- Window bounds: 800x600
- Client bounds: 800x532

That second value is the one which needs to be consistently respected by `BrowserWindow.getBounds()`, since it is related to the one which is set (correctly) on window creation. The total bounds including external decorations aren't relevant to app creators or users.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/7487efc43b208a3624ba464cb156860d

### Additional Information

Related to: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48588.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

**The Problem**
On [Line 115 - status destructure](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L115)
 the install spawn only destructures status but not signal .
Then on [Line 122 - signal check](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L122) , the code checks signal which refers to the [Line 103 - build process signal](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L103)  not the install process signal.



**Expected Behavior(2 cases  here )**

_Scenario 1_: Install process killed by signal (e.g: SIGTERM, SIGINT)
when: User presses Ctrl+C during yarn install, or CI timeout kills the process

Expected:

1. Install process exits with _installSatus=null_  and   ``` installSignal = 'SIGTERM' ```
2. Error check detects the signal termination
3. Script exits with error message: "Failed to install nan node_modules"
4. Exit code reflects the signal termination

_Scenario 2_: Build killed but install succeeds

when: Build process was terminated by signal but install completes successfully

Expected:

1. Build process fails and script exits (already handled correctly) 
2. If build somehow continues, install process completes with installStatus=0, ``` installSignal = null ```
3. Install validation passes
4. Script continues to next step

### Actual Behavior

### Actual Behavior
Scenario 1: Install process killed by signal
What actually happens:

1. Install process exits with _installSatus=null_  and signal = 'SIGTERM'
2. Error check evaluates: ``` if (installStatus !== 0 || signal != null) ```
3. signal refers to the build signal from line 103, which is null (build succeeded)
4. Check fails to detect the install termination 
5. Script continues as if install succeeded, leading to downstream failures

Scenario 2: Build killed but install succeeds
What actually happens:


1. Build fails with signal (correctly exits early - this scenario won't happen)
2. But hypothetically, if build signal was set and install succeeded:
     -   Check evaluates: ```  if (0 !== 0 || 'SIGTERM' != null) ```
     -   Incorrectly reports install failure 
     -   Exits with wrong error message

title: Local Network Access plans and default behavior
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Chrome 142 is introducing a local network access permissions check and has plans to make it on by default in a future version: [https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access)

This feature is important for security, but having it on could interfere with legitimate use cases site to connect to resources on localhost or a private network.

When testing Electron 39.0.0 beta, this had no effect and I could not get a permissions prompt or query local network access permissions even when adding flags to the command line in Electron.

### Proposed Solution

Include an option for local network access for navigator.permissions.query to allow applications to define their own local network access behavior, and define/document the default behavior for local network access checks.

### Alternatives Considered

Make no changes, but document the default behavior, especially as Chrome/Chromium pushes to make local network access checks always on.

As of testing Electron 39.0.0 beta, local network access checks did not block any localhost communication, so not doing anything is a viable solution.

### Additional Information

_No response_

Calling reload() immediately after calling this method will force the reload to occur in a new process.

author: georgedorn
title: On Linux, Accelerators revert to QWERTY layout randomly
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.2.1 and many others

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Manjaro, up-to-date

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Accelerators (shortcuts) should respect my keyboard layout.  That is, the shortcut for "paste" should be ^V, using my layout's definition of 'V' according.

(I'm using Dvorak, and 'V' is where '>.' is located for QWERTY).

### Actual Behavior

Accelerators revert to QWERTY layout - after a while, the shortcut to "paste" becomes ^K (in Dvorak) which is ^V in QWERTY.  Non-shortcuts, e.g. typing normal text in a Signal message or code in a VSCodium window, correctly uses the specified layout, only the accelerators are wrong.  Non-electron apps are unaffected.

Re-running `setxkbmap -layout us -variant dvorak` fixes it, for a while.  Sometimes days, sometimes hours.  As it is random, I haven't worked out a reliable way to trigger it.  My guess is that it may be related to sleeping or coming back from it?

Note:  I did not "install" QWERTY on this system; it's not in the layout selection menu in xfce4's applet, or in the keyboard layout control panel.  Obviously, it's available to `setxkbmap` if I force it, in a terminal.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

As I don't have reliable repro steps, I will add more notes when it next happens.  Applications it has affected in the last couple weeks:
- Signal-desktop
- Delta Chat
- VSCodium
- Chromium

It likely affect many other versions; I recall having the issue going back a year, maybe more.

author: RareScrap
title: Allow passing CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

It's crucial for apps with background behavior (no window, tray icon only) to update themselves seamlessly without interrupting the user and resume work after update as soon as possible. Nobody likes having their work interrupted when an application they aren't using suddenly restarts and displays its window on top of others. The resulting frustration may be so severe that it even prompt the user to completely abandon the application and uninstall it immediately.

Developers need a way to customize the startup behavior of the updated version. The most common requirement for a seamless background update is to prevent the updated application from spawning a new window if no windows were open before the update. The best way to achieve this is to pass CLI arguments to the updated application and handle them in the new process.

The problem is that `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` does not provide this capability

### Proposed Solution

Implement the ability to pass CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() via an optional Options object.

### Alternatives Considered

1) **Using the `app.relaunch()`**: Ultimately, this method could be used to launch any executable following the main process termination. And it also allows for the passing of CLI arguments. The main disadvantage of this workaround is that it does not respect the new version prepared by the `autoUpdater`, which results in two application instances being launched: the old one and the updated one. You could fix this by manually providing the execPath to the Squirrel.Windows main executable. However, **this isn't a proper solution because app.relaunch() isn't intended for this responsibility**. Communicating with the underlying updating framework is solely the responsibility of the autoUpdater.
2) **Using a temp file**: While transferring data via a temporary file is possible, its main drawback is extremely low performance. This method introduces an additional delay in application window initialization, especially when checking a flag to determine if the window should be created at startup.

An API function  `Menu.getContextMenu()` as a counterpart to `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

author: Kilian
title: Configurable type for webContents
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`webContents` gets assigned a `type` on creation. For `BrowserWindow` and `BrowserView` this type is `window` or `browserView`. Webviews always get the type `webview` (this is a hardcoded string: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/guest-view-manager.ts#L102C5-L102C20 )

Because of that `webview` type, `webContents` for webviews are excluded when getting the list of pages through Puppeteer: https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.browser.pages which will only list the `page` type webContents, which it seems both `window` and `browserView` resolve to.

I encountered this issue when trying to set up [chrome-devtools-mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/) to work with [Polypane](https://polypane.app). In Polypane, webviews are conceptually pages but since they are excluded from Puppeteers `browser.pages()` call, they do not show up in the MCP. Having more control over the types of webContents would allow my app to work with this tooling.

### Proposed Solution

It would be nice if there was some way to set the type of a `webview` to (resolve to) `page` rather than `webview`. I'm not too concerned with how, but here are a few options:

- `webContent`s already have a [getType()](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents#contentsgettype) method, add a setter.
- Extend the webview tag with a new `type` attribute that can be set to `page` that in turn overwrites the type on the guestView when specified.

These could both either be set as strings, or a number that refers to a pre-specified value (backgroundPage = 0, window = 1 etc). 

An alternative would be a boolean attribute or method to set the type of a webview to `page` when specified or `webview` when not.

### Alternatives Considered

chrome-devtools-mcp can also be updated to show webview types along page types. This means circumventing the `puppeteer.browser.pages()` api and using the CDP JSON endpoint to build up the list of webContents to include both types, and using that instead.

Over in Chrome land, both the `background_page` and `webview` types are not a concern anymore so they might prefer to not make this change.

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: App freezes when trying to send a Notification without a notification daemon running
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 37.2.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Arch Linux (all distros are affected) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior The notification should simply fail to send ### Actual Behavior The app freezes for 1 minute ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/Vendicated/6f8d74229835950e1aeb5f43b74e1f92 ### Additional Information The root issue seems to be that `notify-send hi` will fail and get stuck until it times out after 1 minute. So the suggested fix is to make sure that notify-send is called asynchronously instead of waiting for it to exit. This issue doesn't happen on Chromium. This issue was already reported in the past but got automatically closed due to the tested Electron version no longer being supported: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/21912 This is a widespread issue that affects every Electron app. See for example: - https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop/issues/2567 - https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Discord#Discord_freezes_after_getting_pinged_or_messaged Reproducing this is a bit inconsistent. For example I can't reproduce on Hyprland with no Notification daemon, but can reproduce on KDE Plasma with Notifications disabled. ## Reproduction Steps (KDE Plasma) 1. Install and run KDE Plasma 2. Right click the little Tray caret and click "Configure System Tray" 3. In "Entries", set "Notifications" to Disabled 4. Log out and back in 5. Run the attached Fiddle and click the Show Notification button 6. Observe that the App becomes unresponsive 7. Run `notify-send hi` in a terminal 8. Observe that it freezes until it times out

body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description In macOS Tahoe, menu items for context menus, tray icon menus, application menus, etc. can have icons next to them. Here are Apple's design docs for the feature: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/menus#Icons It would be great if it was possible to show SF Symbol icons there in the right size and with the right settings in one line of code. Based on my experimentation, I can replicate the native look by saving symbols from the [SF Symbols app](https://developer.apple.com/sf-symbols/) with the following settings: - Font: SF Pro - Font weight: Semibold - Rendering mode: Monochrome - Color: Black (100%) - Background: Default - Point size: 13 - Symbol scale: Small (Right-click the icon, select "Copy Image As…", then select PNG) Then I load them using `nativeImage.createFromPath()`. This replicates the native look. ### Proposed Solution It would be great if there was a one-line solution to load an SF Symbol with the correct settings (see above) so that we can set it as `menuItem.icon`. This work could build on https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48203. It would need to extend that logic to load semibold icons. ### Alternatives Considered Alternatively, developers will need to save every image manually. This doesn't make sense. ### Additional Information _No response_

author: aral-matrix
title: safeStorage does not seem to work without DBUS enabled - incomatible with proper secure sandboxing of applications
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Originating issue: Element Desktop https://github.com/element-hq/element-desktop/issues/2689 

I was forwarded to upstream as this appears an Electron issue: About 1 1/2 years ago, I noticed that I could no longer launch Element Desktop with my tried & tested firejail configuration. While it launched, it failed to read the configuration / authentication data from the jail.
It turned out that for this to work, I was no longer able to block DBUS (`env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=none firejail [..]`)

I consider this a security risk because: When DBUS is available, applications that launch other applications (in my case: Element Desktop launching a web browser for authentication to homeservers) will launch them outside the jailed context, giving them full access to the user home directory. In the case of a web browser, this exposes the user space to security flaws exploited by any website that is opened from an unjailed browser.

When DBUS is disabled, applications are launched within the same jailed context, and this security risk goes away / becomes acceptable.

In the referenced issue, I was informed that this likely results from the use of electron's safeStorage, and sure enough, as soon as I used the option to disable safeStorage (`~/.config/Element/electron-config.json`, setting: `safeStorageBackend: "plaintext"`), I could again launch the application in a jailed configuration with DBUS disabled.


### Proposed Solution

I would like to kindly request that the electron team investigates whether it is possible to make safeStorage work *without* DBUS available in a sandbox (e.g. firejail), thereby enabling both safeStorage *and* keeping further applications launched from a jailed application inside that same jail.

### Alternatives Considered

Currently working: disable DBUS but accept that safeStorage is not available.

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: manusa
title: Electron 39.2.0 crashes with SIGTRAP when launched via Playwright inspector
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

  Fedora 42 (Linux 6.17.7)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.1.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron application via Playwright's electron.launch() API (which uses the inspector protocol with --inspect=0 flag), the application should start successfully and remain running for automated testing.


### Actual Behavior

The Electron process crashes immediately with SIGTRAP signal after the debugger attaches:

```
  <launched> pid=366007
  [err] Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] For help, see: https://nodejs.org/en/docs/inspector
  <ws connecting> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  <ws connected> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] Debugger attached.
  <ws disconnected> code=1006 reason=
  <kill>
  <will force kill>
  <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGTRAP>
```

This causes all Playwright-based E2E tests to fail.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

#### Steps To Reproduce

  1. Create a minimal Electron application
  2. Install Playwright: npm install --save-dev playwright@1.56.1
  3. Create a test file that launches Electron via Playwright:

     ```javascript
     const { _electron: electron } = require('playwright');
     const path = require('path');
     
     async function test() {
       const electronApp = await electron.launch({
         args: [
           path.join(__dirname, 'main.js'),
           '--no-sandbox',
           '--disable-gpu'
         ]
       });
   
       // Process crashes before reaching here
       await electronApp.close();
     }
   
     test();
     ```

  4. Run with Electron 39.2.0: Process crashes with SIGTRAP
  5. Downgrade to Electron 39.1.2: Process launches successfully

#### Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be caused by PR #48703 ("Automatically focus DevTools when element is inspected or breakpoint is triggered"), which was included in 39.2.0.

When Playwright connects via the inspector protocol, the new automatic DevTools activation logic tries to activate/focus a DevTools window that doesn't exist in the Playwright test environment, causing the crash.


#### Impact

This regression breaks all Playwright-based testing for applications that upgrade to Electron 39.2.0, affecting CI/CD pipelines and automated testing workflows.

author: gdavidkov
title: Modal BrowserWindow: multiple show() calls leave parent disabled after close (refcount issue)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Version 10.0.26200.6899]

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.1.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When a modal BrowserWindow is created with a parent and modal: true:

1. The parent window should be disabled while the modal is shown.
2. After the modal is closed, the parent should become fully usable again (interactive, focusable),
3. This should hold even if show() has been called more than once on the modal (for example: once immediately, once in ready-to-show).

### Actual Behavior

If show() is called more than once on the modal window, closing the modal leaves the parent in a permanently disabled state:

- The parent cannot be interacted with (no mouse or keyboard interaction).
- It behaves as if a modal is still open and blocking it, even though the modal window is closed.

If, instead, I call hide() before close(), the parent becomes usable again. That suggests a reference-count mismatch for modal children on the parent window.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/gdavidkov/64ed0deb5c169e5a57de4e152be0e1b7

### Additional Information

Every call to Show() on a modal window increments the parent’s num_modal_children_, but the count is only decremented in Hide(). Close() does not adjust this counter.

So if show() is called multiple times on the same modal window, the parent’s num_modal_children_ can remain > 0 after the modal is closed, leaving the parent disabled.

This feels related to the changes in:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

and is similar in effect to the older issue:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Workaround

Ensure that either:

- show() is called only once on the modal, or
- Call hide() before close():
 This brings the parent back to a usable state.

author: ssh-peppe
title: Clarify default Linux dependencies
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

My company is building a couple of Electron apps, packaged with electron-builder, targeting multiple platforms, among them Linux. The apps  install (from both deb and rpm) and work fine on multiple Linux distros. When testing on RHEL10, however, we noticed that we get an error during installation of the rpm:

```
Error: 
 Problem: conflicting requests
  - nothing provides libXScrnSaver needed by XXX from @commandline
```

This is caused by electron-builder defaulting the dependencies for rpm to include libXScrnSaver, which is no longer installed by default in RHEL10 and in fact is not even available anymore.

Redefining the dependencies to be the ones listed in electron-builder docs as default, minus libXScrnSaver, seem to work fine. The rpm now installs and the app runs, and even `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`, which I understood to be the reason for why libXScrnSaver is required, seems to be working. There does not appear to be any `libXss.so.*` anywhere in the system either so it really does seem like this library is not needed.

Further, checking what libs are needed using readelf -d shows a bunch of libraries, but not `libXss.so.*`.

This begs the question, is libXScrnSaver actually needed anymore? And what are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux? I was trying to find this information, but was unable to.

Asking this in the electron-builder project I got this answer:

> This might be a better question to ask in upstream electron project.
> 
> Happy to update the default config used in electron-builder, but I'm guessing it'll require semver checks on the electronVersion as to what libs are deprecated or no longer required. So getting that clarity upfront will make any changes here more streamlined of a discussion

So I am now asking here: What are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux?

### Proposed Solution

Please provide a list of dependencies needed for Electron apps on Linux.

### Alternatives Considered

Went with the defaults of electron-builder, but this results in the application not being able to install on RHEL10.

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: pavelai
title: Decide TypeScript support in preloads since v40
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Node.js has enabled TypeScript type stripping by default in v24 of the runtime and mark it as stable in v25.2. It means that Electron v40 would support this feature by default too. But as soon as Electron has custom loader for preload scripts which has partial Node.js (CommonJS) semantic it should be decided whether enable type stripping in preloads or not. In my opinion not having TypeScript enabled could lead to unwanted inconsistency in the code, which is run on Electron's side. Today there are three modifications of JS which developers should use in Electron: 1. Node.js (CommonJS, ESModules), 2. Electron's Preload Scripts 3. Chromium's JS (in webpages and extensions). With partial TypeScript support the difference between them would grow further

In my opinion it could be confusing for developers too as soon as they see `require` in preload scripts and decide it is a Node.js/CommonJS module, which has TypeScript support

Another problem is that it would lead to unexpected behavior when `webPreferences.nodeIntegration` is turned on and node integration would work differently

Also it would make users to keep using builder for preloads (when it's not needed for main code), what looks excessive

### Proposed Solution

TypeScript stripping should be enabled in preload scripts. It should be done in the same way it realized in Node.js to reduce inconsistencies in bahavior. It also would reduce the amount of software needed to run Electron with TypeScript

### Alternatives Considered

Leave TypeScript enabled in main code and use preloads in its current view

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: headstrongpete
title: Electron Module Initialization Failure on macOS 15.6.1
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.2 (also tested with 28.3.3, 33.0.0)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15.6.1 (24G90) - Sequoia

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown (issue appears to be macOS-specific)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron application, the `require('electron')` statement should return the Electron API object with properties such as `app`, `BrowserWindow`, etc. The `process.type` property should be set to either `'browser'` or `'renderer'` depending on the process context.

### Actual Behavior

On macOS 15.6.1, Electron's JavaScript bootstrap layer fails to initialize. This results in:

1. `process.type` returning `undefined` instead of `'browser'` or `'renderer'`
2. `require('electron')` returning a string (file path) instead of the Electron API object
3. All Electron applications failing to launch with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`

## To Reproduce

### Minimal Reproduction

**Step 1:** Create a minimal test file (`test-electron-minimal.js`):

```javascript
// Absolute minimal Electron test
console.log('=== Electron Module Load Test ===');
console.log('process.type:', process.type);
console.log('process.versions.electron:', process.versions.electron);

try {
  const electron = require('electron');
  console.log('require("electron") type:', typeof electron);
  console.log('require("electron") value:', electron);

  if (typeof electron === 'object' && electron !== null) {
    console.log('Keys:', Object.keys(electron).slice(0, 10));
    console.log('app exists:', 'app' in electron);
    console.log('BrowserWindow exists:', 'BrowserWindow' in electron);
  }
} catch (error) {
  console.error('ERROR loading electron:', error);
}

console.log('=== Test Complete ===');

// If we're in an Electron context, try to use the app
if (typeof require('electron').app === 'object') {
  const { app } = require('electron');
  app.whenReady().then(() => {
    console.log('SUCCESS: App is ready!');
    app.quit();
  });
} else {
  console.log('FAILED: Electron API not available');
  process.exit(1);
}
```

**Step 2:** Run with Electron:

```bash
npx electron test-electron-minimal.js
```

**Expected Output:**

```
=== Electron Module Load Test ===
process.type: browser
process.versions.electron: 39.2.2
require("electron") type: object
Keys: [ 'app', 'BrowserWindow', ... ]
app exists: true
BrowserWindow exists: true
=== Test Complete ===
SUCCESS: App is ready!
```

**Actual Output (macOS 15.6.1):**

```
=== Electron Module Load Test ===
process.type: undefined
process.versions.electron: 39.2.2
require("electron") type: string
require("electron") value: /path/to/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
=== Test Complete ===
FAILED: Electron API not available
```

### Reproduction with Official Sample

The issue also reproduces with the official `electron-quick-start` repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/electron/electron-quick-start
cd electron-quick-start
npm install
npm start
```

**Result:** Same failure - application does not launch.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Additional Information

### Diagnostic Evidence

#### 1. Electron Framework Loads Successfully

Using `DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES=1`, we confirmed the Electron Framework binary loads correctly:

```
dyld[12345]: <...> /path/to/Electron.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Electron Framework
```

#### 2. Electron Version Detected

The `process.versions.electron` property correctly shows `"39.2.2"`, indicating the Electron runtime is partially initialized.

#### 3. Module Resolution Returns Path String

The npm wrapper at `node_modules/electron/index.js` correctly exports the Electron binary path. However, Electron's require hook system (which should replace this path with the API object) never executes.

#### 4. Environment Variables

- `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is **not set** (ruling out issue #8200)
- No IDE-specific environment variables present (ruling out issue #27135)
- Clean terminal execution with no special environment

### System Configuration

```bash
$ sw_vers
ProductName:            macOS
ProductVersion:         15.6.1
BuildVersion:           24G90

$ uname -m
arm64

$ node --version
v20.11.0

$ npm --version
10.2.4
```

### Attempted Fixes (All Failed)

We systematically attempted all standard Electron troubleshooting steps:

1. **Removed quarantine flags:**

   ```bash
   xattr -cr node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   ```

   Result: No effect

2. **Re-signed application bundle:**

   ```bash
   codesign --remove-signature node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   codesign -s - --deep --force node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   ```

   Result: No effect

3. **Purged Electron caches:**

   ```bash
   rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.github.Electron
   rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Electron
   ```

   Result: No effect

4. **Tested multiple Electron versions:**

   - Electron 28.3.3: Failed
   - Electron 33.0.0: Failed
   - Electron 39.2.2: Failed
     Result: All versions fail identically

5. **Tested official samples:**

   - electron-quick-start: Failed
     Result: Official repository also affected

6. **Direct binary execution:**

   ```bash
   ./node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron test-electron-minimal.js
   ```

   Result: Same failure

7. **Launched from Terminal (bypass LaunchServices):**
   Result: No effect

### Root Cause Analysis

The evidence points to a system-level issue in macOS 15.6.1 that prevents Electron's JavaScript bootstrap from executing:

1. **Framework loads:** The Electron Framework dylib loads successfully
2. **Native layer initializes:** `process.versions.electron` is set by native code
3. **Bootstrap fails:** The JavaScript layer that installs the `require('electron')` hook never executes
4. **Result:** `require('electron')` returns the npm wrapper's path string instead of the API object

This suggests macOS 15.6.1's dynamic linker (dyld) or security policy is preventing Electron's embedded Node.js from completing its initialization sequence.

title: Electron Bug Report: `require('electron')` Returns Executable Path Instead of API Objects on Windows
body:

### Electron Version

31.7.7 and 32.2.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Under development. This is the first version

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Se report under additional Information

### Actual Behavior

Se report under additional Information

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

# Electron Bug Report: `require('electron')` Returns Executable Path Instead of API Objects on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, when running Electron applications, `require('electron')` incorrectly resolves to the npm package's `node_modules/electron/index.js` which exports the path to the executable (`electron.exe`), instead of being intercepted by Electron's internal module loader to provide the Electron API objects (`app`, `BrowserWindow`, etc.).

This causes a critical failure where all Electron applications fail to start with:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
```

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10/11
- **Node.js**: v20.18.0 and v22.18.0 (tested both)
- **npm**: 10.9.3
- **Electron**: v31.7.7 and v39.2.2 (both affected)
- **Package Manager**: npm (also tested with bun v1.3.1, same issue)

## Expected Behavior

When `require('electron')` is called from within an Electron main process:

1. Electron's internal module loader (`c._load` in `node:electron/js2c/node_init`) should intercept the require call
2. Return the Electron API object containing `{ app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain, dialog, ... }`
3. Allow the application to start normally

## Actual Behavior

1. `require('electron')` resolves to `node_modules/electron/index.js`
2. That file returns the string path: `"C:\\path\\to\\node_modules\\electron\\dist\\electron.exe"`
3. Destructuring `const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')` results in `undefined` values
4. Application crashes when trying to call `app.whenReady()`

## Reproduction

### Minimal Reproduction Repository

Project structure:
```
project/
├── package.json
├── electron/
│   └── main.cjs
└── node_modules/
    └── electron/
```

### Step 1: Create package.json
```json
{
  "name": "electron-bug-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "electron/main.cjs",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": "^31.7.7"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Create electron/main.cjs
```javascript
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

console.log('Type of require("electron"):', typeof require('electron'));
console.log('Value:', require('electron'));
console.log('app:', app);
console.log('BrowserWindow:', BrowserWindow);

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  console.log('Electron started successfully');
});
```

### Step 3: Install and Run
```bash
npm install
npm start
```

### Expected Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): object
Value: [object Object]
app: [Function: app]
BrowserWindow: [Function: BrowserWindow]
Electron started successfully
```

### Actual Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): string
Value: C:\path\to\node_modules\electron\dist\electron.exe
app: undefined
BrowserWindow: undefined

C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7
app.whenReady().then(() => {
    ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
    at Object.<anonymous> (C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7:5)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1484:14)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1564:10)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1295:32)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1111:12)
    at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)
    at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:189:12)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:28:49
```

## Analysis

### What We Discovered

1. **Electron's Internal Loader DOES Fire**: The stack trace shows `at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)`, confirming that Electron's module interception system is being invoked.

2. **But It Doesn't Provide the Module**: Instead of providing the Electron APIs, the internal loader falls back to Node's standard module resolution, which finds `node_modules/electron/index.js`.

3. **The npm Package Returns the Path**: The `node_modules/electron/index.js` file by design exports the executable path (for CLI usage), not the API objects:
```javascript
// From node_modules/electron/index.js
module.exports = getElectronPath(); // Returns string path to electron.exe
```

### What We Tested

#### Test 1: Renaming node_modules/electron
When we temporarily renamed `node_modules/electron` to `node_modules/.electron-hidden`:

**Result**:
```
Error: Cannot find module 'electron'
Require stack:
- c:\path\to\electron\main.cjs
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1232:15)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1058:27)
    at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)  ← Electron loader fires!
```

This proves Electron's `c._load` IS being called, but it throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` instead of providing the internal APIs.

#### Test 2: Custom Module Resolution Override
We attempted to override `Module._resolveFilename` to force MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the electron package:

```javascript
const Module = require('module');
const originalResolveFilename = Module._resolveFilename;

Module._resolveFilename = function(request, parent, isMain, options) {
  if (request === 'electron') {
    const error = new Error(`Cannot find module 'electron'`);
    error.code = 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND';
    throw error;
  }
  return originalResolveFilename.call(this, request, parent, isMain, options);
};

const electron = require('electron'); // Still returns string!
```

**Result**: Same issue - returns the executable path string.

#### Test 3: Downgrading Node.js
- **Node v20.18.0**: Same issue
- **Node v22.18.0**: Same issue

#### Test 4: Different Electron Versions
- **Electron v31.7.7**: Affected
- **Electron v39.2.2**: Affected

## Root Cause Hypothesis

Based on our testing, we believe the issue is:

1. Electron's internal module loader (`c._load`) is properly hooked into Node's module system
2. However, it's not registering `'electron'` as an internal module that it should provide
3. When the lookup fails internally, it falls back to standard Node.js module resolution
4. Node finds `node_modules/electron/index.js` and returns its export (the path string)

This suggests that **Electron's internal module registration is not working correctly** on this Windows configuration.

## Attempted Workarounds

### Workaround 1: Custom Electron Loader Module ❌
Created a wrapper module that attempts to force Electron's internal loader. Failed because the internal loader doesn't provide the module.

### Workaround 2: Runtime Directory Renaming ❌
Attempted to temporarily rename `node_modules/electron` at runtime to force MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Failed due to:
- File permissions (EPERM errors)
- Electron's loader still doesn't provide APIs even when npm package is missing

### Workaround 3: Module Cache Manipulation ❌
Tried deleting from `require.cache` and various resolution overrides. None successful.

## System-Specific Details

This bug appears to be **Windows-specific** and possibly related to:
- Node.js internal module loading changes in v20+
- Windows file system casing or path resolution
- Electron's module bootstrap sequence on Windows
- Interaction between Electron's ASAR handling and module resolution

## Impact

This is a **critical blocker** that prevents:
- Any Electron application from starting on affected systems
- Development of Electron applications
- Using any npm packages that depend on Electron APIs

## Additional Information

### Debug Output from Working System (Expected)
On systems where this works correctly:
```javascript
console.log(typeof require('electron')); // "object"
console.log(require('electron').app);    // [Function: app]
```

### Debug Output from Affected System (Actual)
```javascript
console.log(typeof require('electron')); // "string"
console.log(require('electron'));        // "C:\\...\\electron.exe"
console.log(require('electron').app);    // undefined
```

### Environment Variables
No unusual environment variables are set:
- `NODE_PATH`: Not set
- `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`: Not set
- `ELECTRON_NO_ASAR`: Not set (also tested with it set to '1', same issue)

## Request for Help

We've exhausted all known workarounds. This appears to be a fundamental issue with how Electron's internal module system is initialized or registered on Windows.

**Questions for Electron Team:**
1. Is there a known issue with Electron's internal module loader on Windows + Node v20+?
2. Are there any environment variables or configuration that affects module registration?
3. Could this be related to how Electron detects it's running in Electron vs Node mode?
4. Is there diagnostic output we can enable to see what Electron's internal loader is doing?

## Files for Reference

### node_modules/electron/index.js
```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const pathFile = path.join(__dirname, 'path.txt');

function getElectronPath () {
  let executablePath;
  if (fs.existsSync(pathFile)) {
    executablePath = fs.readFileSync(pathFile, 'utf-8');
  }
  if (process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH) {
    return path.join(process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH, executablePath || 'electron');
  }
  if (executablePath) {
    return path.join(__dirname, 'dist', executablePath);
  } else {
    throw new Error('Electron failed to install correctly, please delete node_modules/electron and try installing again');
  }
}

module.exports = getElectronPath(); // ← This is what's being returned!
```

### node_modules/electron/path.txt
```
electron.exe
```

## Related Issues

- Electron Issue #... (if similar issues exist)
- Node.js Issue #... (if related to Node module changes)

## Potential Fix Direction

Based on our analysis, a potential fix might involve:

1. Ensuring Electron's internal `ModuleWrap` or native module system properly registers the 'electron' module before Node's standard resolution kicks in
2. Investigating why `c._load` fires but doesn't provide the module on Windows
3. Possibly adding more aggressive interception of 'electron' requires before falling back to file system lookup

---

**Thank you for investigating this critical issue. Happy to provide any additional information or testing.**

**Reported by**: JEBL-Prosjekter Development Team
**Date**: 2025-11-18
**Contact**: Birger Lundgård

author: glenntws
title: Allow clicking through areas of a webContentView
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

We want to build an Electron app that offers external web content (inside a webContentView) in a section of a BaseWindow. Above that, we want to offer our custom UI that surrounds the web app content.

### Proposed Solution

There should be a mechanism inside webContentView that allows the dev to define that clicks on a certain area are pass-through to the next lower view. This way, we can keep the UI on top of everything with native performance of the actual web content.

One way to implement the check: A CSS-Class similar to "app-region: drag" that allows to define if an area of the app catches the whole event or let's the event pass through to the next layer. Alternatively (though inconsistent with existing similar functions), we could offer some function in the main process API for WebContentsView to add a "pass-through" area.

Technically, we could extend the respective functions of the Chromium "View" base class to make extra checks for these areas (and then return "no hit" if such an area is the one clicked).

### Alternatives Considered

There is no functionality in Electron to accommodate this use case. Existing hacks like forwarding mouseEvents to other webContentViews come with limitations and edge-cases, and stacking multiple windows with "setIgnoreMouseEvents" feels like the worst of all hacks.

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: coladict
title: Allow GTK settings override
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Applications sandboxed behind Flatpak or other means do not always have access to read the configuration, thus they are stuck with garbage 1990s features like "gtk-enable-primary-paste" using the middle button to paste being enabled even when it's disabled by the user through their settings.

Currently Slack and Discord cannot resolve this issue with their software, as they are limited by Electron's capabilities.

### Proposed Solution

Offer a generic solution for any GTK setting to be overridden through the metadata or programmatically at runtime. The second option would be more useful to application developers

### Alternatives Considered

A single option for toggling that particular GTK setting would be possible, but a waste of effort if app developers want access to more of the settings.

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Electron Version

39.2.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 19045.2965

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.6.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron is detected as a Chrome-based browser.

### Actual Behavior

Electron is detected as a Safari-based browser.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When changing the "ProductName" of electron.exe using [rcedit](https://github.com/electron/rcedit):
```ps1
rcedit-x64.exe electron.exe --set-version-string ProductName Foo
```

The user-agent changes from something like
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/142.0.7444.175 Electron/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```
to
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```

As you can see both the `Chrome` and `Electron` versions are removed, which means user-agent-based browser detections thinks the browser is a Safari browser (https://bowser-js.github.io/bowser-online/).

This seems to have changed from v36.6.0 to v36.7.0:
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.6.0 Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/36.6.0 Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.6.0 Safari/537.36
```

```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.7.0 Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/36.7.0 Safari/537.36
```

I think at least the `Chrome` version should be included by default.

I also found it weird that there is no mention of this in the release notes for v36.7.0, so I don't think this change was on purpose: https://releases.electronjs.org/release/v36.7.0

author: livemehere
title: Handling Relative Paths for Local File Loading via Custom Protocol after registerFileProtocol Deprecation
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I am encountering an issue when attempting to load local files, particularly an index.html file, within an <iframe> using a custom protocol registered via protocol.handle.

The context is the upcoming deprecation of protocol.registerFileProtocol(), prompting migration to protocol.handle().

Problem
When a custom scheme is handled with protocol.handle, it is treated as a network request. This behavior prevents the resolution of relative paths within the loaded file, which is crucial for handling static assets.

Example:

A custom scheme is used to load an HTML file: <iframe src="custom://contents/index.html"></iframe>

The index.html file attempts to load a resource using a relative path: <video src="./assets/sample.mp4"></video>

The Electron/Chromium networking stack resolves the resource URL incorrectly as: custom://contents/index.html/assets/sample.mp4

This resolution logic mimics a standard server hosting environment where the path is appended, which is unsuitable for local file paths where the parent directory structure should be preserved.

Current Workarounds & Concerns
Using the file:// Protocol: Loading assets directly via file:// would resolve relative paths correctly, but this often requires setting webSecurity: false in the webPreferences of the BrowserWindow.

Web Security Risk: Disabling webSecurity poses significant security risks, especially in contexts where arbitrary or untrusted content might be loaded.

Question / Feature Request
How can a custom scheme registered with protocol.handle be configured to resolve relative paths and treat the request as a local file protocol (file:// behavior) for nested resources, without compromising security by globally disabling webSecurity?

A mechanism to properly handle the base URL and relative path resolution for assets served from the local file system using protocol.handle is urgently needed before registerFileProtocol is fully deprecated.

### Proposed Solution

A parameter (e.g., type: 'network' | 'file') should be added to the handler options.

### Alternatives Considered

or other method?..

### Additional Information

_No response_

body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 37.5.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS, Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 24H2 26100.7171 (and on more other Windows systems) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 29 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? Yes ### Expected Behavior No memory leaks. ### Actual Behavior Memory leaks occur in the GPU process when calling `app.getGpuInfo()` in certain environments, affecting approximately 1% of users. However, the root cause of these leaks lies within the Vulkan driver, and the underlying code originates from Chromium upstream rather than the Electron project. WPA analysis (the ETL file is to large to upload): Fiddle code with only one `main.js` file: ``` js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') const path = require('node:path') function createWindow () { const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) } app.whenReady().then(() => { createWindow() app.on('activate', function () { if (BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length === 0) createWindow() }) setInterval(async () => { const result = await app.getGPUInfo('complete') console.log(result) }, 1000) }) app.on('window-all-closed', function () { if (process.platform !== 'darwin') app.quit() }) ``` Output: ``` { auxAttributes: { amdSwitchable: false, canSupportThreadedTextureMailbox: false, directMLFeatureLevel: '5.0', displayType: 'ANGLE_D3D11', dx12FeatureLevel: 'D3D 12.2', glExtensions: 'GL_AMD_performance_monitor GL_ANGLE_base_vertex_base_instance_shader_builtin GL_ANGLE_blob_cache GL_ANGLE_client_arrays ### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.4

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home Single  Lanuage

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The Entire screen should be shared.

### Actual Behavior

The screen share is failing with  NotReadableError: Could not start video 

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/chalapathi-ct/bcb989f1b942ba3844157383cf512913

### Additional Information

A significant number of users have reported issues with screen sharing, specifically on devices running Windows 11.
To debug the issue, we tested it on multiple systems, and it occurred on a few of them. All permissions were set right. 

1. When I try to share the entire screen, the screen share fails. However, when I try to share only a specific window, the screen share succeeds.
```session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler((request, callback) => {
        desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['screen'] }).then((sources) => {
            // For simplicity, automatically select the first screen
            // In a production app, you'd show a UI to let users choose
            const primaryScreen = sources[0];
            if (primaryScreen) {
                callback({ video: primaryScreen });
            } else {
                callback({});
            }
        }); - not working
session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler((request, callback) => {
        desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['window'] }).then((sources) => {
            // For simplicity, automatically select the first screen
            // In a production app, you'd show a UI to let users choose
            const primaryScreen = sources[0];
            if (primaryScreen) {
                callback({ video: primaryScreen });
            } else {
                callback({});
            }
        });```- working

2.  To check whether the issue was related to Chromium, I downloaded the exact Chromium version and tested it. Full screen sharing worked on the same system where the Electron app’s screen sharing failed..

3. To investigate further, I collected both Chromium logs and Electron app logs

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

We're developing an Electron app for MacOS App Store. When updating our app through TestFlight, TestFlight prompts "Close This App to Update", and when I click "Continue" our app would be "Terminated" for update.
Now this is where things go wrong. On MacOS 15 our app seems to be gracefully terminating (We attached it with lldb and it shows that our app returns with 0 when we click "Continue") which is fine.
However for MacOS 26 though, it seems that TestFlight just directly SIGKILLs our app (indicated by lldb), which means that all of our app's child processes are left orphaned. Even worse, our app is singleton, which means that when the app relaunches it fails, because the leftover child processes from the previously SIGKILLed session is still alive, and even if we want to kill those orphaned child processes we can't because our app is sandboxed thus cannot kill processes outside of the current sandbox.

Like MacOS 15, our app gracefully terminating

Dear Electron Team,

I am writing to formally report a series of critical issues affecting multiple Electron-based applications following the recent macOS update to version 26.1. These issues have severely impacted our business operations and productivity across the company.

Since updating to macOS Tahoe 26.1, we have consistently encountered the following problems across several widely used Electron-based applications, including Slack, Visual Studio Code, 1Password, and others:

- Frequent freezing and UI hangs, often requiring force-quitting the applications.
- Significant performance degradation, making basic tasks such as opening program windows, navigating menus, or loading workspaces slow or unresponsive.
- Malfunctions with file drag-and-drop functionality, including an inability to drag files into application windows and inconsistent behavior in different areas of the interface.
- Application launch failures, where applications either fail to start or crash immediately upon launch.
- General instability, which includes unexpected shutdowns, unresponsive interface components, and rendering issues.

I want to inform you that these issues are not new. We began experiencing similar issues after the previous macOS Tahoe update, and the release of version 26.1 has not resolved them. In many cases, the problems have become more widespread.

Critically, this is not an isolated incident. These issues now affect over one thousand users within our company, indicating that the problem is systemic and widespread across our environment.

Given our heavy reliance on Electron-based applications for essential daily workflows, the ongoing instability poses a significant challenge to maintaining efficient business operations.

I respectfully request that your  team:

1. Investigate the root cause of the issues introduced by the recent macOS Tahoe updates.
2. Provide an official statement outlining known issues, temporary workarounds, or recommended mitigation steps.
3. Offer information regarding potential patches or a projected timeline for resolving these problems.

Our company is fully prepared to provide detailed technical logs, system diagnostics, reproducible examples, and an inventory of affected devices to help you in your investigation.

I appreciate you taking the time to look into this and look forward to your response.

author: maifeeulasad
title: Support for multiple user profiles
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Introduce native support for multiple user profiles within the application, similar to Chrome/Chromium profile behavior. Each profile should maintain completely isolated sessions, storage, cookies, cache, and authentication state.

Without proper profile isolation, users must frequently log in and out, risking session conflicts and data leakage.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a profile system backed by Electron’s `session` partitions:
Each user profile maps to a unique persistent partition (e.g., `persist:userId`)

Full isolation of:
 - Cookies
 - LocalStorage / IndexedDB
 - Cache
 - Authentication tokens
 - Profiles persist across application restarts
 - Everything on application layer

Ability to:
 - Create new profiles
 - Switch between profiles without restarting the app
 - Delete profiles safely

### Alternatives Considered

trying to write an application with this feature, not sure how much is possible, but I think adding it to electron source itself will be great

### Additional Information

willing to work on this one

### Additional Information

Displaying these accelerators as plain text could the best option, as it is very clear. Works well for Windows and Linux.

author: storcke64
title: **[Critical] Electron v39 Fails to Render Styled UI on Fedora/Gnome (Renderer Process Failure)**
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

last known working version could not be determined because the application failed on every tested version.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

The application is expected to launch, initialize the Chromium renderer process successfully, and display the fully styled Graphical User Interface (GUI) as designed.

The main Electron window should open and present the complete application UI, which includes the styled form fields, and correctly colored buttons (green for Save, indigo for Preview).

The application should not display a blank white screen or an unstyled, bare HTML interface.

The application's internal JavaScript logic (for generating the manifest object) and the secure IPC bridge (window.fileAPI) should initialize without error.

### Actual Behavior

When the application is launched, the following happens:

1.  The main Electron window opens successfully.
2.  The application **fails to render any styling or layout** from the fully embedded CSS.
3.  The user interface is displayed as **plain, unstyled HTML text** (white background, default black font, unstyled buttons).
4.  There is **no crash log or error message** generated; the Chromium renderer process silently fails to apply the styles, indicating a deep-seated system conflict during graphical initialization.

This behavior persists even when launching with the most permissive flags: `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity`.


Here is the diagnostic timeline section in a single markdown block, exactly as it appears in the final bug report:

```markdown
#### C. Final Electron Failure (The System Conflict)

Despite the code being proven correct and all components being embedded, the failure persists in the native Electron window.

| Step | Command Executed | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cache Clear & Relaunch** | `rm -rf ~/.config/flatpak-manifest-builder` then `npx electron . --no-sandbox` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **Final Nuclear Launch** | `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **CSS Fix** | All CSS was **embedded directly** into `index.html` to eliminate all external file access conflicts. | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## 🔗 Testcase Gist URL

**N/A (System-Level Conflict)**

A simple Electron Fiddle link cannot be provided because the application code has been confirmed to be **100% functional** and bug-free (tested working perfectly via `http-server` in Chrome and Firefox).

The failure is a **deep incompatibility** between the Chromium renderer (used by Electron v39) and the core Fedora/Gnome system libraries. **The bug cannot be reproduced in the clean, isolated context of Electron Fiddle**; it requires the specific library environment of the host system to fail.

We request attention based on the extensive diagnostic evidence provided in the "Diagnostic Timeline" section above.

title: Change to gin_converters/guid_converter broke UUID sanitation
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.9.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS Tahoe, Win11, Win10

### What arch are you using?

Other (specify below)

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.7.4

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon`  should be able to take in a guid of format `{<guid>}` in addition to `<guid>`

Root cause is in additional information

### Actual Behavior

when passing a guid into `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` of the format `{<guid>}`, it errors out with `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string`

Root cause is in additional information

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/a0d983e4b53432b236499cf76638ead4dd3d2c46 added a change where `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` takes in a base::Uuid GUID as opposed to a UUID GUID.

The gin_converter/guid_converter for UUID GUID has input sanitization that removes { & } from the outside of the GUID (Windows wraps GUIDs in braces).
```
if (!guid.empty()) {
      if (guid[0] == '{' && guid[guid.length() - 1] == '}') {
        guid = guid.substr(1, guid.length() - 2);
      }
    }
```

Since we switched to using a base::Uuid GUID, & its gin convert does not hav ethis input sanitization, existing electron users that take in a guid of the format `{ guid }` are met with an error `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string` because the converter returns an empty string.

Clone Electron source for 40.0.0-beta.X.

Configure GN with:

  v8_enable_sandbox = false

```
  
Build Electron (e.g. ninja -C out/Release electron).

Run my app with the newly built Electron.

body:

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Type check should pass with latest `@types/node` versions.
The following should have no errors:
```
mkdir electron-type-error
cd electron-type-error
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm i typescript electron
npx tsc --init --skipLibCheck false
echo "import electron from 'electron'; console.log(electron.shell);" > main.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

### Actual Behavior

Fails as of `@types/node@22.19.3` with:
```
node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2717: Subsequent property declarations must have the same type.  Property 'noDeprecation' must be of type 'boolean', but here has type 'boolean | undefined'.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5
    25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    'noDeprecation' was also declared here.

node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~


Found 3 errors in 2 files.

Errors  Files
     2  node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712
     1  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738

```

Seems like @types/node [added](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/74184) `noDeprecation` as an optional field, but electron defines it as required.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Not sure where the type is actually defined in electron. I see there's https://github.com/electron/typescript-definitions, but which api .json is it given?

### Additional Information

Couldn't get Fiddle to run, so here's the code:
### `package.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "electron-test",
  "main": "main.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {

### `main.js`:
```js
const {app, BrowserWindow} = require("electron")

function createWindow() {
	const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
		// frame: false // Uncomment to stop segfault from occurring
	})

	 // Not reached
	console.log("No segfault!")
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  createWindow()
})
```

Someone [on reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/electronjs/comments/1oc7qvi/crash_on_new_browserwindow/) identified that `frame: false` stops the segfault, I would never have figured that out myself
