### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When using OSR with `useSharedTexture: true`, a paint event should be fired with a properly populated texture.

### Actual Behavior

The following error is output, and the paint event does not fire:

```
[93649:1220/233451.235840:ERROR:gpu/command_buffer/service/shared_image/shared_image_representation.cc:408] Unable to initialize SkSurface
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

According to this post by @reitowo:
[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/46811#issuecomment-2859463799](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/46811#issuecomment-2859463799)

it appears that the issue does not occur on Linux environments equipped with AMD GPUs. Since AMD-based environments have had Wayland as the default for quite some time, it is assumed that this setup is also running on Wayland.

If that is the case, the only plausible difference between that environment and mine is the GPU itself. Therefore, it seems reasonable to conclude that OSR is not supported on NVIDIA + Linux + Wayland environments. There are no display issues or errors when using non-OSR windows or when rendering in Chrome/Chromium.

author: Abhijeet911max
title: Enhance Electron spawn lifecycle handling for better robustness
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

 The current Node.js script that spawns and manages the Electron process works correctly, but it can be improved for robustness, safety, and maintainability.
Some edge cases (like spawn failure or multiple event listeners) are not fully handled.

### Proposed Solution

Use child.once() instead of child.on() for lifecycle events

Handle the exit event in addition to close

Add a listener for the error event on the spawned process

Refactor signal handling to avoid repetition

### Alternatives Considered

Prevents accidental multiple event triggers

Avoids silent crashes if Electron fails to start

Improves code readability and intent

Makes the process lifecycle handling more production-safe

### Additional Information

The child process lifecycle should be handled safely and deterministically

Spawn failures should be caught and reported clearly

Event listeners should be registered only once

Signal handling should be concise and easier to extend

title: Allow Renderer's DNS cache cleanup using Session#clearHostResolverCache()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Right now `Session#clearHostResolverCache()` affects only the next calls of `Session#resolveHost()` which doesn't affect Renderer processes even if the same `Session` object was passed to `BrowserWindow`. This results in absolute lack of control over Renderer's DNS cache.

### Proposed Solution

Make `Session#clearHostResolverCache()` clear Renderer's DNS cache

### Alternatives Considered

The only alternative for the proposed solution is providing an another API for Renderer's DNS cache control which is weird since `Session` is the API designed to control the Chromium's network capabilities

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

### Summary

### Actual Behavior

### Summary
On macOS 26.2 Tahoe (latest official release), multiple Electron-based applications are being **force-terminated by the system (SIGKILL)** without generating crash reports. These terminations happen even with the latest versions of the applications and with up-to-date macOS.

This behaviour goes beyond UI lag/stutter described in other issues (e.g., #48311). In my case, apps such as VS Code, Slack, Chrome, and other Electron apps are killed by the OS abruptly without crash logs, often correlated with sustained WindowServer activity.

I have collected sysdiagnose output showing high WindowServer involvement shortly before the terminations. This appears to be a system resource / compositor rendering interaction issue rather than an app-specific crash.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Boot macOS 26.2 Tahoe on Apple Silicon (M4/Mx).
2. Open multiple Electron-based applications (VS Code, Slack, Chrome, etc.).
3. Work normally (code editing, multiple windows, no special operations).
4. After some time, one or more apps are killed by the OS without warnings or crash reports.

### Expected Behavior
Electron apps should not be abruptly terminated by the OS without crash reports. Users should be able to work without unexpected force quits.

### Actual Behavior
Apps are abruptly terminated (SIGKILL) by the system. No crash report is generated in Console for these terminations.

### Context
Related Electron compatibility discussions include performance and rendering issues on macOS 26 (e.g., #48311), but this report reflects **forced termination behaviour**, which has not been documented in existing open issues:

• Strange global lag / WindowServer issues — https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48311 :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}  
• VS Code GPU/WindowServer behaviour discussions — https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/267022 :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}  
• Community confirmation of macOS 26 + Electron compatibility problems — https://www.reddit.com/r/MacOS/comments/1nj0jb5/do_not_update_to_macos_26_if_you_use_vscode/ :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

### Additional Files / Logs
I have attached the sysdiagnose archive, including `RunningBoard` priority samples, `jetsam_priority.csv`, and `top.txt`, which show:
- WindowServer high rendering involvement
- Lack of memory pressure or crash logs
- Force terminated Electron processes

Please let me know if additional logs or a reproducible test case is needed.

author: triptu
title: Support `resign-key` and `become-key` events on `BrowserWindow` (macOS)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, Electron’s `BrowserWindow` exposes `focus` and `blur` events, but it does not expose the native macOS `NSWindow` events for `windowDidBecomeKey` and `windowDidResignKey`.

While `focus` and `blur` often correlate with key status, they are not semantically identical, especially when building floating panels, overlays, or "spotlight-like" interfaces (`NSPanel`).

### Proposed Solution

Expose the native [`windowDidBecomeKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidbecomekey(_:)) and [`windowDidResignKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidresignkey(_:)) events as `become-key` and `resign-key` (or similar) on the `BrowserWindow` instance. We noticed that `BrowserWindow::OnWindowIsKeyChanged(bool is_key)` already exists in `electron_api_browser_window.cc` ([source link](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/809ab09b6f5ede0a9f9b0fcc0e9c33ff971277f2/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc#L188)), but it does not appear to be mapped to a public-facing event that consumers can listen to.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Native Modules:** We are currently using a native module to access `NSWindowDelegate` methods directly.
- **Using `blur` event:** It does not map 1:1 with `resignKey` behavior in multi-window setups.

### Additional Information

author: cptpcrd
title: Window freezes on macOS when failing to enter fullscreen (regression)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

37.7.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. User begins swiping between virtual desktops (see #43112 for some context).
2. Electron window requests fullscreen.
3. The window fails to enter fullscreen mode (due to being halfway between two virtual desktops), but remains usable.

### Actual Behavior

Upon failing to enter fullscreen mode, the contents of the window freeze. In the attached example gist, this is visible in two distinct ways:
- The red border around the window disappears on the right and bottom sides, which I believe is due to the contents of the window being rendered as if it is fullscreened.
- The animated spinning box freezes.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/cptpcrd/bf28bf81d7cd4c4f4197367b54c708ba

### Additional Information

I have bisected this down to a regression that first appeared between v37.7.0 and v37.7.1, specifically in #47151 (and its backports).

As best as I can tell, following the failed fullscreen transition, the OS briefly reports the window as first occluded (which causes `OnWindowHide` to run), then visible (which previously caused `OnWindowShow` to run, but following #47151 now does nothing). It seems that the mismatched calls cause Chromium to think the page is hidden and thus does not need to be rendered.

This change fixes the issue for me locally (though it also means `WebContents::WasShown` runs twice back-to-back when `Show` is called, which I suspect is undesirable):

```diff
--- a/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc
+++ b/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc
@@ -280,6 +280,7 @@ v8::Local<v8::Value> BrowserWindow::GetWebContents(v8::Isolate* isolate) {
 }
 
 void BrowserWindow::OnWindowShow() {
+  web_contents()->WasShown();
   BaseWindow::OnWindowShow();
 }
 
```

title: Location #hash is being lost when request is handled via protocol.handle
body:

40

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Even when [page](https://sunvas.online/electron/) is heavily relies on data passed in `location.hash`, it still perfectly loads in browsers (pay attention to the hash in location).

### Actual Behavior

But when `protocol.handle("https",...)` is used, it causes infinite redirects due to losing `location.hash` data. And as a result [page](https://sunvas.online/electron/) cannot be loaded in `BrowserWindow`.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Code to reproduce

`index.js`
```
const {app, BrowserWindow} = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(function(){
	const
		win=new BrowserWindow({
			width: 700,
			height: 700,
			center:true,
			title:"Demo",
		}),
		{session}=win.webContents;

	session.protocol.handle("https", req=>session.fetch(req, {
		bypassCustomProtocolHandlers: true
	}));

	win.openDevTools({mode:"undocked",title:"Tools"});
	win.loadURL("https://sunvas.online/electron/");
});
```

author: matos-ed
title: Enable system default page size handling to print method
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron's `webContents.print()` diverges from Chromium's default printing behavior by hard-coding A4 (210mm × 297mm) as the media size when no explicit `pageSize` or `mediaSize` is provided. In contrast, Chromium's `window.print()` queries the printer driver to obtain native defaults.

**Impact of this divergence:**

1. **Thermal/Receipt Printers Broken**: POS systems using thermal printers (EPSON TM, Zebra, Star TSP) receive A4 print jobs instead of their configured 80mm width, causing content overflow and print failures.

2. **Regional Settings Ignored**: US-based printers configured for Letter size receive A4 documents, and vice versa in different regions.

3. **Driver Configurations Bypassed**: Custom page sizes configured in printer drivers are completely ignored.

4. **Inconsistent API Behavior**: 
   - `window.print()` → Uses printer driver defaults (works correctly)
   - `webContents.print()` → Always defaults to A4 (breaks many scenarios)

**Current Code** (shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc):
```cpp
if (options.Get("mediaSize", &media_size)) {
  settings.Set(printing::kSettingMediaSize, std::move(media_size));
} else {
  // Hard-coded A4 - diverges from Chromium behavior
  settings.Set(printing::kSettingMediaSize,
               base::Value::Dict()
                   .Set(printing::kSettingMediaSizeHeightMicrons, 297000)
                   .Set(printing::kSettingMediaSizeWidthMicrons, 210000)
                   ...);
}
```

This hard-coded default was introduced in later Electron versions after removing `GetDefaultPrinterAsync()` which previously queried driver settings (similar to Electron v8 behavior).

### Proposed Solution

**Add a `SYSTEM_DEFAULT` option to `pageSize`** that aligns `webContents.print()` with Chromium's approach by allowing printer drivers to provide their configured defaults.

### Implementation:
```typescript
// For thermal printers - use driver defaults
webContents.print({
  silent: true,
  deviceName: 'EPSON TM-T88V',
  pageSize: 'SYSTEM_DEFAULT'  // Queries printer driver like window.print()
});

// Existing behavior unchanged
webContents.print({
  silent: true,
  pageSize: 'Letter'  // Explicit size still works
});

// Backward compatible - no pageSize still defaults to A4
webContents.print({ silent: true });  // Still gets A4
```

### Mechanism:
1. When `pageSize: 'SYSTEM_DEFAULT'` is set, a flag (`useSystemDefaultMediaSize`) is passed to C++
2. C++ layer skips setting the hard-coded A4 default
3. Printer driver provides its native default configuration
4. Matches behavior of `window.print()` and Chromium's `PrintViewManagerBase`

### Alternatives Considered

### Alternative 1: Manually Set mediaSize for Each Printer
Users explicitly specify the `mediaSize` parameter with printer-specific values.

```typescript
// Detect printer type and hardcode sizes
if (printerName.includes('TM-T88')) {
  webContents.print({
    deviceName: printerName,
    mediaSize: { width_microns: 80000, height_microns: 297000 }
  });
}
```

**Rejected because:**
- Requires maintaining printer detection logic in application code
- Doesn't leverage printer driver configurations
- Breaks when printer models change or new printers are added
- Doesn't solve regional differences (still need to detect US vs EU)
- Error-prone and increases maintenance burden

### Alternative 2: Use window.print() Instead
Recommend users switch from `webContents.print()` to `window.print()` for silent printing scenarios.

**Rejected because:**
- `window.print()` doesn't support `silent: true` printing from main process
- Requires restructuring application architecture (moving print logic to renderer)
- Can't be used for headless/background printing scenarios
- Loses other `webContents.print()` features (deviceName selection, callbacks)
- Not a viable solution for POS/retail applications

### Alternative 3: Document the A4 Default Behavior
Update documentation to clearly state that A4 is the default and users should set `pageSize` explicitly.

**Rejected because:**
- Doesn't solve the problem, just documents the limitation
- Still requires users to implement printer detection logic
- Perpetuates the divergence from Chromium's behavior
- Users still can't leverage printer driver configurations
- Doesn't help with regional or custom page size scenarios


**Rejected because:**
- `getPrintersAsync()` doesn't reliably provide default page size information
- Printer capability data is often incomplete or platform-specific
- Adds complexity and async overhead before each print job
- Still requires hardcoding fallback logic
- Doesn't truly query the driver's configured default

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: DruidEdu
title: [MAS Rejection]:
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

37.0.0

### Rejection Email

## Apple's Rejection Message

```
Guideline 2.5.1 - Performance - Software Requirements

Additionally, we found your app uses or references the following non-public or deprecated APIs:

_toolbarView
_menuImpl
_removeFromGroups:
_isConsideredOpenForPersistentState
_boundsIfOpen
_resizeDirectionForMouseLocation:
NSAppendToKillRing
kCFBundleNumericVersionKey
__NSNewKillRingSequence
_CGSSetWindowCaptureExcludeShape
_CGRegionCreateWithRect
__NSInitializeKillRing
_CTFontCopyVariationAxesInternal
NSYankFromKillRing
NSSetKillRingToYankedState

The use of non-public or deprecated APIs is not permitted on the App Store, 
as they can lead to a poor user experience should these APIs change and are 
otherwise not supported on Apple platforms.
```

### Additional Information

## Investigation Results

I have verified that **these APIs are NOT in my application code**, but exist in the **Electron Framework itself**.

### Evidence 1: APIs found in Electron Framework

Using `nm` to check symbols in Electron Framework:

```bash
# Check for undefined symbols (U type) - these are external references
$ nm -arch arm64 -gU "MyApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Versions/A/Electron Framework" \
  | grep -E "(KillRing|CGSSetWindow|CTFont|toolbarView|menuImpl)"

                 U _CGSSetWindowCaptureExcludeShape
                 U _CTFontCopyVariationAxesInternal
                 U __NSAppendToKillRing
                 U __NSSetKillRingToYankedState
                 U __NSYankFromKillRing
                 U __NSNewKillRingSequence
                 U __NSInitializeKillRing
```

**Note**: The `U` type indicates "undefined" symbols that need to be imported from external libraries. This confirms these APIs are being referenced by Electron Framework.

### Evidence 2: Using `strings` to find API names

```bash
$ strings "MyApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Versions/A/Electron Framework" \
  | grep -E "(_toolbarView|_menuImpl|_removeFromGroups|_isConsideredOpenForPersistentState|_boundsIfOpen|_resizeDirectionForMouseLocation|kCFBundleNumericVersionKey|_CGRegionCreateWithRect)"

_toolbarView
_menuImpl
_removeFromGroups:
_isConsideredOpenForPersistentState
_boundsIfOpen
_resizeDirectionForMouseLocation:
kCFBundleNumericVersionKey
_CGRegionCreateWithRect
```

### Evidence 3: My application binary is clean

```bash
# Scanned my app binary
$ nm -gU "MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp" | grep -E "(KillRing|CGSSetWindow|CTFont|toolbarView|menuImpl)"
# (No results - my code doesn't use these APIs)

$ strings "MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp" | grep -E "(KillRing|CGSSetWindow|CTFont|toolbarView|menuImpl)"
# (No results)
```

### File Structure Analysis

```
MyApp.app/
├── Contents/
│   ├── Frameworks/
│   │   └── Electron Framework.framework/  ← Private APIs HERE (Chromium/Electron code)
│   ├── MacOS/
│   │   └── MyApp                          ← My app binary (clean)
│   └── Resources/
│       └── app.asar                       ← My application code (JavaScript/TypeScript)
```

## API Categories

### Text Editing APIs (Kill Ring)
These are used by Chromium's text editing engine for clipboard operations:
- `NSAppendToKillRing`, `NSYankFromKillRing`, `__NSInitializeKillRing`, `__NSNewKillRingSequence`, `NSSetKillRingToYankedState`

### Window Management APIs
- `_toolbarView`, `_menuImpl`, `_removeFromGroups:`, `_isConsideredOpenForPersistentState`, `_boundsIfOpen`, `_resizeDirectionForMouseLocation:`

### Graphics APIs
- `_CGSSetWindowCaptureExcludeShape`, `_CGRegionCreateWithRect`

### Font Rendering
- `_CTFontCopyVariationAxesInternal`

### Deprecated
- `kCFBundleNumericVersionKey` (should use CFBundleVersion/CFBundleShortVersionString)

## Build Configuration

```json
// electron-builder config
{
  "mac": {
    "target": ["mas"],
    "hardenedRuntime": false,
    "gatekeeperAssess": false,
    "entitlements": "build/entitlements.mas.plist",
    "entitlementsInherit": "build/entitlements.mas.inherit.plist"
  },
  "mas": {
    "identity": "...",
    "provisioningProfile": "...",
    "type": "distribution"
  }
}
```

## Environment

- **macOS**: 14.1 Sonoma
- **Xcode**: 15.0
- **Electron**: 28.0.0
- **electron-builder**: 26.0.12
- **Node.js**: 18.x

## Questions

1. Is this a known issue with Electron 28.0.0 (and other versions) for MAS builds?
2. Are there build flags or configuration options to disable these private APIs for MAS targets?
3. Has anyone successfully passed App Store review with these APIs present in Electron Framework?
4. Should I try a different Electron version? (I've seen reports that newer versions may have addressed some of these)
5. Are these APIs coming from Chromium itself, and if so, is there a way to configure Chromium to avoid them?

## Impact

This blocks Mac App Store distribution for any Electron app. Other Electron-based apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord) are on the MAS - how did they resolve this?

## Additional Context

- I've verified these APIs are not in my application code (checked with `nm` and `strings`)
- The APIs appear in Electron Framework binary itself
- Some APIs show as undefined symbols (`U` type in `nm` output), indicating they're being referenced but may be dynamically linked
- Some APIs only appear as strings, which could be false positives, but Apple's scanner still flags them

---

**Note**: I'm willing to provide more debugging info, test patches, or try different approaches if needed. I can also provide the full output of `nm` and `otool` commands if that would be helpful.

author: z0gSh1u
title: `setBounds` a WebContentsView will trigger `page-favicon-updated` event on some websites
body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 39.2.7 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Intuitively, `setBounds` is related to positions and has nothing to do with the favicon. So `page-favicon-updated` event should not be emitted when calling `setBounds` with a new `bounds` on a WebContentsView. ### Actual Behavior Construct a WebContentsView, listen its `page-favicon-updated` event, add it to the main window, and `loadURL` for like `https://electronjs.org`. Then call `setBounds` with a new `bounds` on the WebContentsView, `page-favicon-updated` will be triggered. This doesn't occur on all websites, but many websites have this problem, including `https://github.com`. Usually this won't lead to noticeable problems. But if the user wants to auto resize the WebContentsView when the main window resizes, `setBounds` will be frequently called and a series of `page-favicon-updated` event will be emitted, even if the favicon urls array is not changed. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/z0gSh1u/72fe6f155e1f145385461853d7ef2782 ### Additional Information Can be reproduced on macOS too.

author: danteissaias
title: Allow showing a window without foregrounding it on macOS
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I have an Electron app that auto-updates in the background. After an update is installed, the app needs to relaunch to run the newly installed version. When the user had the window open in the background, I'd like to recreate that window without focusing or foregrounding it, to avoid interrupting the user.

### Proposed Solution

I'd like an API that allows me to show a window without focusing it or bringing it to the foreground. This could either be a new window method, or a parameter on `showInactive` that disables foregrounding.

In my auto-update example, saving and restoring the exact z-index of the window would be tricky, so I think the API should simply place the new window at the back of the stack using `orderBack`.


### Alternatives Considered

`showInactive` does show the window without focusing it, but it appears to be hardcoded to always bring the window to the foreground: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/5901d8a6d8bf019bf8b535cb8ffe18860bdf3ad3/shell/browser/native_window_mac.mm#L477

title: Critical I/O Overload on macOS Intel (Ventura) – Inefficient SQLite Commit Pattern causing Kernel Panic/Disk Disconnects

### Electron Version

32.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS Ventura

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Description: I am reporting a critical performance issue with the Discord macOS client (Electron-based) that leads to system instability and I/O timeouts on Intel-based MacBooks. As an electronics engineer, I have verified this is NOT a hardware failure.

Hardware Validation:

    Storage: M.2 SATA SSD via PCIe adapter.

    Physical Layer: Double-sided gold-plating on adapter contacts (Gold-to-Gold interface) to ensure zero oxidation and minimal contact resistance.

    Power Stability: Added 3x tantalum capacitors (500uF each) on the VCC line to filter transient spikes and stabilize voltage during high I/O bursts.

    Stress Test: Passed 40GB small-file sequential and random write tests without errors.

    Conclusion: Hardware is 100% stable; failure occurs only under Discord's specific I/O pattern.

Technical Observations: The Discord client (specifically Discord Helper processes) initiates an aggressive pattern of synchronous SQLite commits and fsync calls. On systems where the I/O latency is slightly higher than native Apple NVMe (e.g., AHCI/SATA protocols over PCIe bridges), this "flooding" of the command queue leads to a driver-level timeout (AppleStorageDevice). This results in the partition table being dropped or a full Kernel Panic.

Proposed Fix:

    Implement better batching for SQLite transactions to reduce the frequency of fsync.

    Introduce a "Low I/O Mode" for older Intel Mac hardware.

    Optimize Chromium's cache management to be less aggressive on APFS metadata updates.

### Actual Behavior

Description: I am reporting a critical performance issue with the Discord macOS client (Electron-based) that leads to system instability and I/O timeouts on Intel-based MacBooks. As an electronics engineer, I have verified this is NOT a hardware failure.

Hardware Validation:

    Storage: M.2 SATA SSD via PCIe adapter.

This results in the partition table being dropped or a full Kernel Panic.

author: piotr1alien-art
title: Evidence of I/O induced service instability:
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

32.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

ventura

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

16.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Reproduction Update: I have successfully reproduced the I/O saturation using a standalone Electron Fiddle script.

Monitoring with fs_usage on macOS confirms that Electron is triggering massive amounts of fcntl <FULLFSYNC> calls. On my hardware configuration (high-quality external controller), each FULLFSYNC takes approximately 14-18ms.
Plaintext

20:12:02.301507  fcntl  F=39  <FULLFSYNC>  0.014464  Electron.2091985
20:12:02.320365  fcntl  F=39  <FULLFSYNC>  0.013900  Electron.2091985

This confirms that the issue is not specific to Discord's business logic, but rather how Electron/Chromium manages the I/O queue when multiple FULLFSYNC requests are issued in a short window. The lack of proper backpressure leads to a driver-level timeout (Kernel Panic).

### Actual Behavior

I have monitored the execution of the Fiddle reproduction script. The results are conclusive: aggressive I/O operations through Electron's fs module lead to a cascade failure of other Electron internal services.

Specifically, during the FULLFSYNC flood (latencies of 14-18ms per call), the Network Service crashes repeatedly:
Plaintext

[22262:0115/201214.919853:ERROR:content/browser/network_service_instance_impl.cc:613] Network service crashed, restarting service.

This confirms that the I/O blocking is so severe that it starves the Chromium IPC/Network stack, causing internal timeouts. This is the exact state that precedes the Kernel Panic I've been experiencing. It's not a Discord bug; it's a fundamental issue with how Electron handles I/O pressure on macOS when hardware latency deviates from standard internal SSD profiles.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49407

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: hyrious
title: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 electron --run <script> prints ◙ (Alt+10) for new lines (char code 10) in Windows Terminal
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

_This is just an interesting observation and doesn't introduce any harm. So feel free to investigate or ignore it._

When running `electron --run` in cmd.exe in Windows Terminal with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` env, it writes newlines (`\n`) as the character ◙ ([INVERSE WHITE CIRCLE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alt_code#:~:text=INVERSE%20WHITE%20CIRCLE)). For reference, `\n` is `String.fromCharCode(10)` and the white circle can be input by Alt+10 in old MS systems.

For testing this behavior, install electron to PATH, prepare a package.json and script:

```cmd
@REM node_shim.cmd
@echo off
setlocal

set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
call electron %*
```

```js
// package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "foo": "node_shim foo.js"
  }
}

// foo.js
console.log('aaa\nbbb\nccc')
```

Run `node_shim --run foo` returns:

```
aaa◙bbb◙ccc◙
```

If you replace the `node_shim` above with `node` (so do not invoke electron), the output is correct.

Environment:
- Windows 11
- Electron 40
- Node.js 25 (for correct behavior)

### Proposed Solution

Investigate what happens on `--run` with electron.

### Alternatives Considered

N/A

title: utilityProcess `exit` event reports incorrect code on Windows
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (10.0.26100 Build 26100)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The `exit` event in `utilityProcess` should include the correct exit code for the process, regardless of how it exits.

### Actual Behavior

If you clone the attached gist and run `npm install && npm run build && npm run start`, you get the following output:
```
Utility process exited with code: 18446744072635812000
```

This also happens if you use the `exit()` function from `cstdlib`, but not if you call `process.exit(0xC0000AA0)` in `utility.js` for some reason.

The correct decimal value would be `3221228192`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-/bbe5ecede1f2b10ac2bed4c46ac66509

### Additional Information

I started looking into this because of a user report about a utility process crash. The logs reported the exit code `18446744072635812000`, which seemed weirdly high and isn't documented anywhere.

I think the issue here is that [exit codes on Windows are 32-bit unsigned integers, a.k.a. `DWORD`s](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getexitcodeprocess), but [they get passed from Chromium to Electron as `int`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/patches/chromium/feat_enable_passing_exit_code_on_service_process_crash.patch) and then eventually get turned into 64-bit values by first extending the "signed" integer to 64 bits and then reinterpreting it as an unsigned value.

This works fine if the code is low enough to be interpreted as a positive `int`, but if it's interpreted as a negative `int` it gets mangled by the extension to 64 bits. Here's some Rust demonstrating this process:
```
let a: u32 = 0xC0E90002;
println!("{a:x} {a}"); // c0e90002 3236495362

let b: i32 = a as i32;
println!("{b:x} {b}"); // c0e90002 -1058471934

let c: i64 = b as i64;
println!("{c:x} {c}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 -1058471934

let d: u64 = c as u64;
println!("{d:x} {d}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 18446744072651079682
```

Then of course it gets turned into a 64-bit float by JavaScript, which loses precision since the value is so high. This is unfortunate since there are [70 different `NTSTATUS` codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55) that yield my original error code when sent through this process.

I haven't looked too closesly at the relevant code on the Electron side, but I think the fix would just be to immediately cast the `int` value we get from Chromium to a `uint` so that subsequent conversions don't misinterpret the value?

### Problem Description

as per #19429 - there currently is no way to prevent alt+space in windows from opening the system context menu 

even using webContents.on("before-input-event")... though, even if it did, its less than ideal as preventing a keyDown event means that the keyUp will never fire, as per #37336

### Proposed Solution

#19429 proposes allowing an override specifically for alt+space, but I think it might be more meaningful to have the alt+space get routed through the existing "before-input-event" event, as it is more semantically appropriate and (hopefully) should allow the actual relevant keyboard events through.

### Alternatives Considered

I feel the only viable alternative would be as #19429 suggests: have a specific option to override the alt+space keyboard combination, but I think that's less than ideal for the aforementioned reasons.

I have tried using a global hotkey and an accelerator key, but neither were able to allow the key event through to the browser window.

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Tahoe: Version 26.2 (25C56)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

There should be a way to allow package directories (like `.ufo`, `.bundle`, etc.) to be:
- Visible and selectable when matching a filter extension
- Selected via double-click (same as regular files)

### Actual Behavior

I'm building a font editor where I need to load [ufo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Font_Object) files (which are directories).

When using `dialog.showOpenDialog()` with filters that include a package directory extension (e.g., `.ufo`), there's no way to allow users to both:
1. See the package directory as selectable (not greyed out)
2. Double-click to select it (rather than navigating into it)

## Attempts and results

### 1. With filters only

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are greyed out and cannot be selected.

### 2. With `treatPackageAsDirectory`

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory", "treatPackageAsDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are selectable via single-click + Open button, but double-clicking navigates into the directory instead of selecting it.

### 3. Without filters

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` can be selected, but so can any other file type, which is not an ideal experience for a user.

author: nikwen
title: Retry tests in CI automatically when they fail
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

In CI, when tests are flaky and fail, we need to re-run them manually. This is annoying, costs time, and costs computing hours.

### Proposed Solution

Chromium has a nice solution where if a test fails, CI re-runs that single specific test automatically before reporting failure.

If we adopted that for Electron, we'd save maintainers time and we'd reduce our cloud bill. (We'd re-run just the failed test, not the whole test suite.)

### Alternatives Considered

Re-run all tests automatically as a first step. Would already be better than the current solution.

```
APP="/path/to/MyApp.app"
BIN="$APP/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Versions/A/Electron Framework"

nm -arch arm64 -g "$BIN" | grep -E "_CGSSetWindowCaptureExcludeShape|_CGRegionCreateWithRect|_CTFontCopyVariationAxesInternal"
Output (arm64):
```

text
```
                 U _CGRegionCreateWithRect
                 U _CGSSetWindowCaptureExcludeShape
                 U _CTFontCopyVariationAxesInternal``
```
2) Other previously reported private APIs are no longer present
After upgrading to Electron 40.1.0, I can no longer detect the other private APIs from #49386 (e.g. KillRing-related symbols, _toolbarView, _menuImpl, etc.). The MAS rejection is now only for the three APIs listed above.

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) - Build 25C56

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

Running an Electron app from the command line should not print code signing errors when the code signature is valid.

### Actual Behavior

When running VS Code (or any Electron app) from the CLI, the following error is printed to stderr:

```
[0204/102237.819836:ERROR:electron/shell/common/mac/codesign_util.cc:109] SecCodeCheckValidity: Error Domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain Code=-67062 "(null)" (-67062)
```

Error code -67062 = `errSecCSSignatureInvalid`

However, the code signature is actually **valid** according to macOS:

```
$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/Visual\ Studio\ Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: valid on disk
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement

$ spctl --assess --verbose /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
```

This appears to be Electron's internal `SecCodeCheckValidity` call in `codesign_util.cc` failing on macOS 26, even though the signature is valid.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

- This issue has been reported in VS Code: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/204085 (locked, tagged as upstream Electron issue)
- The error is cosmetic and doesn't affect functionality
- Fresh reinstall via Homebrew does not resolve the issue
- Occurs on macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) with Intel Mac (x86_64)

body:

### Electron Version

40.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.2

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

39

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron v40 supports macOS 12 and above. Native Node modules should also be built with support for macOS 12 and above.

### Actual Behavior

Native modules are built with support for macOS 13.5 and above.

They do not work on macOS 12–13.5.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Repro:

```bash
npx create-electron-app@latest my-app --template=webpack
cd my-app
npm i fs-xattr
npm start
otool -l node_modules/fs-xattr/build/Release/xattr.node
```

The output includes:

```
    minos 13.5
      sdk 26.2
```

Some libs work around it, e.g., [better-sqlite3](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/blob/27cb07b5926652ae0e601dc26a35714128692f18/deps/common.gypi#L59).

This happened because Node.js [increased their minimum supported macOS version](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/8b4022177750530d2c142a5a0349d98fb82f16e2) to 13.5 as part of Node.js 24.0.0.

Now native Node modules compile against that version.

We might want to lower it again in Electron for as long as we support macOS <= 13.4.

More information: https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/CB6CG54DB/p1770224778182279

author: Abhinandankaushik
title: feat: Automated Spell Check for Blog Content (Typos Detection)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, there is no automated mechanism to catch spelling mistakes specifically in blog content. As a result, typos often go unnoticed during development and code review, and eventually get merged into production. This affects the professionalism, readability, and quality of the website.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an automated spell-check step in the CI/CD pipeline that:

- Runs on every pull request that modifies files inside /blog/** (or relevant blog directory).
- Uses a tool like typos (or an equivalent spell-checker).
- Fails the CI check if critical spelling errors are detected.
- Allows a configurable ignore list (.typos.toml) for valid technical terms, names, or abbreviations.
- Provides clear, actionable error messages pointing to the exact file and line with the typo.

### Alternatives Considered

- Manual review by maintainers: Rejected because it does not scale and increases workload.
- GitHub issue templates only: Helpful but does not prevent duplicate submissions.
- Strict issue submission rules: Too restrictive and may discourage contributions.

### Additional Information

- This feature would be especially useful for large repositories with frequent contributions.
- Can be implemented using GitHub Actions with existing tools like issue similarity bots or custom scripts.
- Similar functionality is used in repositories like Kubernetes and TensorFlow.

- there many typos which have to fix and fixing all this manually takes too much time

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an automated spell-check step in the CI/CD pipeline that:

### Additional Information

- The action can be initially configured in a permissive mode (with exclusions) and tightened over time as false positives are handled.

author: nmggithub
title: `window.open()` could be documented better
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

This is inspired by #1219, and is a potential duplicate of it (but with a wider scope). Right now [our documentation on the use of `window.open` in the renderer](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.1/docs/api/window-open.md#windowopenurl-framename-features) reads as follows:
> Electron will parse [`BrowserWindowConstructorOptions`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/browser-window-options) out of this list where possible, for convenience. For full control and better ergonomics, consider using `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` to customize the BrowserWindow creation.

### Proposed Solution

The "where possible" here is a bit vague and while the push towards `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` is probably warranted, I believe the docs could be improved by more explicitly calling out [what feature strings we actually support there (which is arguably more limited than what the wording here would suggest).](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.0/lib/browser/parse-features-string.ts#L78)

### Alternatives Considered

We could also just continue to let the encouragement to use `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` do the heavy lifting for us and not bother with explaining the specific inner workings of a less-capable feature.

### Additional Information

### Problem Description

The `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` API performs noticeably slower on Linux, as compared to Windows and macOS.

This problem requires the API to be called repeatedly without caching to be visible, and can result in builds on Windows and macOS performing fine during testing, whilst Linux builds are disproportionately less performant.

Yes, this only appears if a developer doesn't cache the output of this API. I believe that makes it more important, as it becomes easier to overlook during testing.

### Proposed Solution

Document this performance disparity regarding how builds for Linux can run much slower, whilst appearing fine on Windows and macOS.

### Alternatives Considered

I did consider that Linux could cache the output of the API. I don't believe that's a good idea, and this would also require a code change.

### Additional Information

I had a look at the source code. The Linux API calls a shell command, and I think macOS and Windows use system APIs. I'm not completely sure about macOS.

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

If `useSharedTexture` is enabled, shared texture should be created with same directx texture flags for any `pixelFormat` in `OffscreenSharedTexture` object.

### Actual Behavior

Shared textures are created with different directx texture flags.

To be specific
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: bgra` is created only with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` flag as stated documentation.
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: rgbaf16` is created with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX` flags. So `IDXGIKeyedMutex` must be acquired and locked. Without this, all GPU operations, such as copying and drawing, will perform as if the texture were transparent, without any error.

### Additional Information

Shared textures should be created using same flags, or at least the differences should be clearly stated in the documentation.

author: pie6k
title: `webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(frame)` for Zero-Copy VideoFame GPU Handoff
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, high-performance video applications in Electron (e.g., those using node-av, ffmpeg, or custom C++ encoding/AI pipelines) lack a supported way to access the underlying GPU handle of a VideoFrame directly from Renderer process to send it to the main process.

It is a primary bottleneck in high-performance scenarios of encoding video frames created by the renderer process.



### Proposed Solution

Proposed API Expanding the [webUtils](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-utils)) module to provide a bridge between WebCodecs/MediaStream frames and native system handles.

```ts
  const handle = webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(videoFrame);
  
  if (handle) {
    // Zero-copy: only the handle travels over IPC
    ipcRenderer.send('process-gpu-handle', handle.iosurface); // platform specific handles, same as shared texture
  }
```

### Alternatives Considered

Moving frames from the Renderer to the Main process currently requires one of:

CPU Readback: Using copyTo() to move pixels to an ArrayBuffer. This is extremely expensive at 4K/60fps and negates the benefits of hardware decoding.

Private Hacks: Disabling the sandbox to use Node.js native addons that attempt to "guess" memory offsets of Chromium's internal media::VideoFrame objects. This is fragile across Electron versions and insecure.

Using `paint` event with shared textures. It works, but even if high fpu values on browser window, waiting for paint event often takes ~8-20ms for large textures which is quite bad considering I already have `VideoFrame` created in the renderer process, so what I need is already in GPU memory, I don't need a separate one from the paint event which is equal to the one I have already

### Additional Information

Electron's internal C++ implementation would likely unwrap the blink::VideoFrame, access its media::VideoFrame, and extract the gfx::GpuMemoryBuffer.

Security: By implementing this in webUtils, Electron maintains the security model. The Renderer never sees the raw pointer, only a system-level ID that the Main process (trusted) can resolve.

author: SharifIsmail
title: GPU process hangs on Linux when argv contains both spaces and multi-byte UTF-8 characters
body:
## Description

On Linux, when an Electron app is launched with command-line arguments containing **both** a space and a multi-byte UTF-8 character (emoji, CJK, etc.), the GPU subprocess fails to initialize and the process hangs indefinitely. This does not occur on Windows.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Works (no spaces in argument with emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello🎉world"

# Hangs indefinitely (space + emoji in same argument)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello 🎉 world"

# Works (spaces but no emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello world"
```

The GPU process logs:
```
ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:189] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization
```

Confirmed via `strace -f`: child/zygote processes hang while reading `/proc/self/cmdline`.

## Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0, Docker container with no GPU hardware)
- **Electron**: 33+ (via Obsidian 1.12.1, but reproducible with any Electron app on Linux)
- **GPU**: None (software rendering) — but the bug is in command-line parsing, not GPU initialization itself

## Root Cause Analysis

The bug is in `base/command_line.cc` in `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` and `SetProgram`:

```cpp
// Windows — Unicode-aware ✅
arg = CommandLine::StringType(TrimWhitespace(arg, TRIM_ALL));

// Linux/POSIX — ASCII-only, byte-by-byte ❌
TrimWhitespaceASCII(arg, TRIM_ALL, &arg);
```

`TrimWhitespaceASCII` operates byte-by-byte on what it assumes is an ASCII string. When arguments contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (3+ bytes, e.g., emoji `0xF0 0x9F 0x8E 0x89`), it doesn't understand character boundaries.

The chain of events:

1. CLI launches with emoji + spaces in argv
2. Zygote forks a GPU child process
3. Child calls `CommandLine::InitFromArgv()` → `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` runs `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on each argument byte-by-byte
4. `SetProcessTitleFromCommandLine` flattens all args into a single space-separated string and writes it over the original argv memory via `setproctitle`
5. `/proc/self/cmdline` now contains corrupted data
6. GPU subprocess reads corrupted command line → switches like `--type=gpu-process` are malformed → GPU initialization fails → process hangs

### Why each condition is required:

- **Without spaces**: `TrimWhitespaceASCII` has nothing to trim, multi-byte bytes (all > 0x7F) pass through unmodified
- **Without multi-byte UTF-8**: Pure ASCII, byte-level operations work correctly
- **With both**: Byte-level trimming near space + multi-byte boundaries corrupts string length calculations, which cascades through `setproctitle` into corrupted `/proc/self/cmdline`

### Why Windows is unaffected:

- Uses `TrimWhitespace` (Unicode-aware) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII`
- Does not use the zygote/fork model
- Does not have `setproctitle` or `/proc/self/cmdline`

## Suggested Fix

Use `TrimWhitespace` (or a UTF-8-aware equivalent) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on POSIX in `base/command_line.cc`. The ASCII-only assumption is incorrect on modern Linux systems where argv can contain arbitrary UTF-8.

## Real-World Impact

This affects any Electron-based CLI tool on Linux that accepts user content as arguments (e.g., note-taking apps, automation tools). Users cannot pass emoji or CJK characters with spaces in command-line arguments without the process hanging.

## Related Reports

- [Obsidian Forum: CLI command hangs with multibyte characters](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/cli-command-hangs-when-creating-notes-with-multibyte-characters-cjk-unicode/111035)
- [Chromium discussion: GPU process fails with multibyte username](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-discuss/c/4OgTFSPxP68)

### Actual Behavior

The extension loads but immediately throws multiple errors related to missing Chrome APIs. The extension's service worker fails to register and core functionality doesn't work.


### Testcase Gist URL

**Console Output:**
```
(node:27824) ExtensionLoadWarning: Warnings loading extension at /Users/david/Desktop/claude-browser/claude-extension/1.0.52_0:
```

author: nikwen
title: Fuse to disable all Node.js flags
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

For security purposes, we should have a fuse to disable all Node.js flags in production applications.

The more [Node.js flags](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/command-line-switches#nodejs-flags) we expose, the higher the risk. In production apps, you'd usually want to disable all Node.js flags anyways.

### Proposed Solution

Add a fuse to disable all Node.js flags.

Similar to the [`nodeCliInspect` fuse](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/fuses#nodecliinspect), but for _all_ handling of Node.js flags.

### Alternatives Considered

- Not adding any Node.js flags to Electron at all. However, those flags can make development easier.
- Changing the existing `nodeCliInspect` fuse.

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: Wayland: Non-BMP Unicode input truncated (U+1Fxxx → U+Fxxx) when typing via keyboard
body:

### Electron Version

Bundled with Signal 7.89.0 (see Additional info)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Linux mace.inner.sanctum 6.18.9-200.fc43.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Feb  6 21:43:09 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Typing Unicode characters outside the BMP (e.g. U+1F448 👈, U+1F91F 🤟) via keyboard input should insert the correct Unicode character, as provided by the Wayland input system (UTF-8 text).

### Actual Behavior

When typing certain non-BMP Unicode characters via keyboard input, the resulting character is incorrect and appears truncated:
        Intended: U+1F448 (👈)
        Actual: U+F448 ()
    This pattern is consistent for characters in the U+1Fxxx range, which appear to be truncated to U+Fxxx.
    The issue only occurs with direct keyboard input.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I’m using Signal Desktop 7.89.0 (Flatpak from Flathub), which bundles Electron internally, so I don’t have the exact Electron version available.
However, I have reproduced the same behavior in a standalone Chromium build (RPM, not Flatpak), so this does not appear to be specific to Signal.
---
I investigated this using wev on Wayland and confirmed that the system is producing correct UTF-8 input.

Example:

```
sym: U1F448 (16905288), utf8: '👈'
sym: U1F91F (16906527), utf8: '🤟'
```

This indicates:

- XKB is correctly configured
- libxkbcommon is producing correct Unicode
- Wayland is delivering correct UTF-8 text

Despite this, Electron-based applications appear to ignore the provided UTF-8 and instead derive characters from the keysym, resulting in incorrect truncated codepoints (e.g. U+1F448 → U+F448).

Additional observations:

- Clipboard paste produces correct characters
- Compose sequences produce correct characters
- Only direct key input is affected

This suggests a keysym-to-character conversion path that does not correctly handle non-BMP Unicode.

---
This is my first bug report ever. I hope I did this correctly. I consulted ChatGPT to help me find where and how to tell someone about this. I’m here in good faith, I care about getting this right, and I’m open to correction.

author: caniko
title: [Wayland/Ozone] Per-window input freeze — events received on socket but not dispatched to affected window
body:
### Description

When running Electron (via VSCode) on native Wayland with the COSMIC compositor, individual windows intermittently and permanently lose all mouse and keyboard input. The window continues to render normally — buffer updates are composited, animations play, terminal output scrolls — but the window accepts zero input. No recovery is possible; the affected window must be closed.

Other Electron/VSCode windows of the same process remain fully functional. The freeze is per-window, not per-process or per-session.

### Key diagnostic finding

During an active freeze, I ran `strace` on the Electron browser process (PID 12219) for 15 seconds, tracing `recvmsg`, `sendmsg`, `read`, `write`, `poll`, `ppoll`, `epoll_wait`.

**The Wayland socket (fd 48) is actively receiving events:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total strace lines (15s) | 9,746 |
| `recvmsg(48, ...)` calls | 3,272 |
| `sendmsg(48, ...)` calls | 154 |
| Dominant payload size | 28 bytes (1,169 calls) — matches `wl_pointer.motion` |
| Other payloads | 24B (146), 60B (139), 8B (132), 32B (40), 52B (4) |

The compositor IS sending Wayland events to the client's socket, and the Electron browser process IS reading them via `recvmsg()`. The browser process's main thread is in `ppoll()` (not blocked/stuck). Yet the affected window receives zero input.

This strongly suggests the bug is in the Ozone/Wayland input dispatch path — somewhere between reading the Wayland wire messages and routing them to the correct `wl_surface`/`BrowserWindow`.

### Reproduction

- **Not deterministic** — happens randomly, sometimes after minutes, sometimes after hours
- **Trigger**: Unknown. No specific action triggers it. Not correlated with drag-and-drop, focus changes, or fullscreen transitions
- **Frequency**: Multiple times per day across two different machines
- **Workaround**: `--ozone-platform=x11` (XWayland) eliminates the issue entirely

### What was ruled out

- **Not a compositor-wide issue**: Other windows (including other VSCode windows from the same process) continue to work
- **Not a GPU/rendering issue**: No dmesg errors, no GPU crashes, rendering continues in the frozen window
- **Not VSCode extensions**: No extension host crashes or errors correlated with freezes
- **Not VSCode's unresponsive detector**: `CodeWindow: detected unresponsive` does not fire because the renderer heartbeat passes (rendering works, only input is lost)
- **Not the compositor refusing events**: strace proves `recvmsg()` on the Wayland socket succeeds with meaningful payloads

### Environment

- **Electron**: 39.3.0 (bundled with VSCode 1.109.2, Chromium ~134)
- **Compositor**: COSMIC (cosmic-comp 1.0.0, Smithay-based)
- **GPU**: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (dGPU) + AMD Granite Ridge iGPU (Radeon Graphics)
- **Kernel**: 6.19.0-cachyos-lto
- **OS**: NixOS (x86_64-linux)
- **Tested on**: Two machines (atlas: Ryzen 9950X + RX 7900 XT, nomad: laptop with AMD iGPU)

### Process state during freeze

```
State: S (sleeping)
Threads: 45
Wchan: do_sys_poll
Main stack: do_sys_poll → __se_sys_ppoll → do_syscall_64
```

The main thread is in `ppoll()` waiting for events — the normal idle state. It is not deadlocked or stuck.

### strace excerpt (during active freeze, mouse moving over frozen window)

```
18:23:13.888284 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1528}, ...) = 28 <0.000012>
18:23:13.888421 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.890119 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1500}, ...) = 28 <0.000007>
18:23:13.890142 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.893148 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1472}, ...) = 28 <0.000006>
18:23:13.893167 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.895149 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1444}, ...) = 28 <0.000006>
18:23:13.895168 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.897182 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1416}, ...) = 28 <0.000009>
18:23:13.897231 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
```

Rapid stream of 28-byte messages at ~2ms intervals — consistent with wl_pointer.motion events while moving the mouse over the frozen window.

### Related issues

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/221961 — Nearly identical symptoms ("VSCode stops responding to mouse inputs after being unfocused"), closed as stale without resolution. Was assigned to `@deepak1556`.
- https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40732343 — "Wayland Ozone all window freeze at random after hours of stable operation"

body:

### Electron Version

37.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

CachyOS (Arch-based), Linux 6.19.3-2-cachyos x86_64, KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

After completing a drag and drop operation inside the application window, the app should continue working normally. I expect to still be able to click on UI elements, use keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl R, and interact with the window controls without any interruption.

### Actual Behavior

After performing a drag and drop action inside the window, the application becomes unresponsive to input. The window continues rendering and animations still play, and I can move or resize the window using the window manager. However, I can no longer click any UI elements, including the window controls, and keyboard shortcuts such as Ctrl R do not work. The process does not crash, but it must be killed manually to recover.



### Testcase Gist URL

Unable to reproduce in a minimal standalone Electron app at this time. The issue has only been observed in Discord (Electron 37.6.0) under Wayland. Logs and strace output are attached as supporting evidence.

### Additional Information

**This was observed in Discord (version 0.0.125-1), which bundles Electron 37.6.0.**

This issue only occurs when running the app natively on Wayland using `--ozone-platform=wayland`. It does not reproduce when forcing X11 via `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=x11`. I also tested Chromium under Wayland and could not reproduce similar behavior there.

The problem appears after internal drag and drop actions inside the window, such as dragging a member entry within the UI. It may not trigger on the first attempt, but after several repetitions the window stops responding to input.

The application does not crash. It continues rendering and animations remain active, and the window can still be moved or resized by the window manager. However, mouse clicks and keyboard shortcuts (for example Ctrl+R) no longer work inside the window, including the window controls. The process must be killed manually to recover.

Disabling `WaylandWindowDecorations` reduces the frequency of the issue but does not eliminate it.

A short strace taken while the window was unresponsive shows the process continuously polling the Wayland socket (epoll_wait / recvmsg loop) without blocking or deadlocking, suggesting the event loop remains active but input events are no longer being processed at the application level.

System details: CachyOS (Arch-based), KDE Plasma 6 on Wayland, kernel 6.19.3-2-cachyos, x86_64. Electron version 37.6.0.


### Attachments

* `discord-dnd-tail.txt` Electron log tail captured immediately after the freeze
* `discord-hang.strace.txt` strace capture taken while the app was unresponsive
* `inxi.txt` System information including GPU and driver details

Currently, in Electron, when multiple WebContents instances load pages from the same domain, each one creates a separate SiteInstance and renderer process. This increases memory usage and can lead to inefficiencies, especially in applications that require opening many same-origin tabs or windows. By contrast, in Chromium's window.open scenario, the new WebContents reuses the opener's SiteInstance and can share a renderer process for the same-origin case, resulting in better resource sharing.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce a feature that allows developers to explicitly create or clone a WebContents in such a way that, when loading a same-origin page, its SiteInstance and renderer process can be reused. For example, providing an API similar to webContents.clone() or a dedicated option to share SiteInstance between WebContents, so that they behave more like window.open in the browser context and can share renderer processes when appropriate.

### Alternatives Considered

No reliable way is available to achieve process reuse for same-origin cases in Electron's public API.

### Additional Information

Sharing renderer processes for same-origin WebContents can improve memory efficiency and emulate browser behaviors more closely in Electron-based applications. This could enable advanced use cases, such as tabbed browsers and collaborative editors, while keeping system resource usage controlled.

author: spkrka
title: fix: orphaned zygote enters infinite CPU spinloop on Linux (ENOTSOCK)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.4

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Linux

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.8.0-101-generic, x86_64)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

When the main Electron process exits or restarts, orphaned zygote processes should either be terminated or detect the broken IPC socket and exit cleanly.

### Actual Behavior

When an Electron app crashes or restarts on Linux, orphaned zygote processes from the previous session can survive with broken IPC file descriptors. The zygote enters an infinite CPU spinloop, burning 80%+ of a core indefinitely and spamming error logs at ~4000 lines/second.

This same bug has been reported for VS Code: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/288893 — confirmed affecting multiple users on Ubuntu 24.04 across different Electron apps.

#### Root Cause

In `content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc`, `HandleRequestFromBrowser()` at line 243-245:

```cpp
if (len == -1) {
    PLOG(ERROR) << "Error reading message from browser";
    return false;  // ← returns to main loop
}
```

When the orphaned zygote's IPC fd (fd 3) points to a regular file instead of a socket, `RecvMsg()` returns -1 with `errno == ENOTSOCK`. The code correctly exits on EOF/ECONNRESET (line 235-240) but not on ENOTSOCK. Returning `false` goes back to `ProcessRequests()`'s main loop, where `ppoll()` on a regular file returns POLLIN immediately — creating the spinloop.

The orphaned zygote's fds after restart:
```
fd 3 -> /usr/lib/slack/icudtl.dat          (should be IPC socket)
fd 4 -> /usr/lib/slack/v8_context_snapshot.bin  (should be IPC socket)
```

Strace of the spinloop (~33,000 syscalls/second, zero backoff):
```
recvmsg(3, ...) = -1 ENOTSOCK
socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0, [10, 11]) = 0
sendmsg(4, ..., cmsg_data=[11]) = -1 ENOTSOCK
write(2, "...ERROR:content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc:245] Error reading message
       from browser: Socket operation on non-socket (88)\n", 139) = 139
close(10); close(11); getpid()
# repeats immediately
```

#### Impact

- **CPU**: 83% of one core (single-threaded, R state)
- **Disk**: `~/.xsession-errors` grew to **15 GB** (111 million lines) in ~40 minutes
- **Persistent**: continues indefinitely until manually killed

#### Proposed Fix

Extend the existing exit path to cover non-recoverable socket errors:

```diff
--- a/content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc
+++ b/content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc
@@ -240,6 +240,14 @@ bool Zygote::HandleRequestFromBrowser(int fd) {
   }

   if (len == -1) {
+    // If the IPC socket fd is fundamentally invalid (not a socket, or bad fd),
+    // there is no way to recover. This happens when the zygote is orphaned
+    // after the browser process exits and restarts, leaving file descriptors
+    // pointing to non-socket files. Exit to avoid an infinite spinloop.
+    if (errno == ENOTSOCK || errno == EBADF) {
+      LOG(ERROR) << "Zygote IPC socket is invalid, exiting orphaned zygote";
+      _exit(0);
+    }
     PLOG(ERROR) << "Error reading message from browser";
     return false;
   }
```

This is a minimal, safe change: `ENOTSOCK`/`EBADF` are non-recoverable errors that indicate the fd is not a socket at all, so the zygote can never receive valid messages and should exit like it already does for EOF.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Observed in Slack 4.47.69 (Electron 39.2.4). The VS Code issue (microsoft/vscode#288893) confirms this affects the latest Electron versions as well, with VS Code 1.109.2 users reporting 70-100% CPU from orphaned zygote processes.

A full Electron patch file is also available at: https://gist.github.com/ (can be provided if helpful).

40.4.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Apps should be able to update using Squirrel.Mac without issue.

### Actual Behavior

Currently, our signed app is failing to update with the following errors:
```
Detected this as an install request
ERROR: Unrecognized attribute string flag '?' in attribute string "T@"NSString",?,R,C" for property debugDescription
ERROR: Unrecognized attribute string flag '?' in attribute string "T@"NSString",?,R,C" for property debugDescription
Installation error: Error Domain=SQRLShipItRequestErrorDomain Code=2 "Could not read update request" UserInfo={NSLocalizedDescription=Could not read update request, NSUnderlyingError=0x60000174aac0 {Error Domain=SQRLShipItRequestErrorDomain Code=1 "Missing required value" UserInfo={NSLocalizedDescription=Missing required value, NSLocalizedRecoverySuggestion="targetBundleURL" must not be set to nil.}}}
ShipIt quitting
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Ref https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/38437, which I think contains the breaking change.

My current theory is that the Mantle roll from 78d3966 → 2a8e212 changes how we're handling deserialization. One or both of the following are what I'm looking into:

1. `+propertyKeys` behavior changed: The old Mantle included all properties except readonly ones. The new Mantle delegates to `+storageBehaviorForPropertyWithKey:`, which adds `instancesRespondToSelector:` checks and recursive superclass lookups that can change which properties are included/excluded for Squirrel's SQRLShipItRequest.
2. `NSCoding` decode changed: `-decodeValueForKey:withCoder:modelVersion:` switched from NSInvocation-based dispatch to direct IMP calling, which could cause issues if method signatures don't match exactly.

The result is that targetBundleURL deserializes as nil, which is a required field, causing ShipIt to reject the update request and exit.

This was discovered while testing an Electron 40 → 41 upgrade. All Squirrel update E2E tests pass on Electron 40.4.0 and fail on 41.0.0, beginning with alpha.1.

### Expected Behavior

After the renderer process crashes and the page is recovered via webContents.reload(), calling win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true }) when the cursor is over the click-through area and win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(false) when it leaves should behave the same as before the crash: mouseenter/mouseleave fire only when the cursor actually enters or leaves the element, and the window correctly switches between click-through and normal mode. After a click in the click-through area, mouseleave should still fire when the cursor leaves, so the window can return to non–click-through state.

### Actual Behavior

After the renderer crashes and we call webContents.reload() in the render-process-gone handler:

After one click in that area while it is in click-through mode, mouseleave stops firing. The window then stays in click-through mode and never returns to normal mode, so the user can no longer interact with the window.
