author: bengotow
title: `action` and `reply` notification events never fire on non-MSIX Windows apps
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.2.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

I migrated Mailspring's notifications from custom toastXml over to the Electron Notification APIs and expected inline replies and actions to trigger `notification.on('reply')` and `notification.on('action')` but they do not.

### Actual Behavior

The action and reply events on Notification are silently dropped. The buttons and reply input render correctly in the toast, and click fires as expected, but action and reply never fire regardless of CLSID configuration. (I've added the new CLSID setter and verified a stable CLSID in the shortcut)

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/codebytere/toast-actions-msix-sample/blob/main/src/main.ts, just without MSIX packaging

### Additional Information

In windows_toast_notification.cc, ToastEventHandler::Invoke handles the WinRT Activated event for all toast interactions. For structured arguments (action/reply), it returns early without dispatching:

```
bool structured = arguments_w.find(L"&tag=") != std::wstring::npos ||
                  arguments_w.find(L"type=action") != std::wstring::npos ||
                  arguments_w.find(L"type=reply") != std::wstring::npos;
if (structured)
  return S_OK;  // drops the event, waiting for COM callback
```

This design expects the COM INotificationActivationCallback::Activate() callback to handle action/reply. However, the toast XML uses activationType="foreground" for all action elements.

MSIX-packaged apps: COM activation is declared in AppxManifest.xml. Windows invokes the COM activator for all activation types, so the early return in the WinRT handler works correctly — the COM callback fires and delivers the event.

Unpackaged apps (Squirrel, NSIS, etc.): For activationType="foreground", Windows fires only the WinRT in-process Activated event. No COM callback fires. The WinRT handler drops the event. Result: action and reply are permanently lost.

I have been deep in the weeds debugging this with Claude and I am no Windows API expert (I use a Mac!) but I have a context window full of Windows docs and Electron source :-) it suggests: 

Option A (minimal): In ToastEventHandler::Invoke, call HandleToastActivation() directly for structured args received via the WinRT Activated event, rather than returning early. This handles the foreground activation path used by unpackaged apps and is a no-op for MSIX apps where the COM callback will also fire (one path would just win the race).

Option B (correct Windows semantics): Change the generated toast XML to use activationType="background" for action/reply elements. This explicitly tells Windows to use the COM activation path, which works for both packaged and unpackaged apps (given setToastActivatorCLSID is called and the shortcut is correctly written). This also has the user-experience benefit of not foregrounding the app window for background actions like "Mark as Read".

author: nikwen
title: Add ability to stop heap profiling
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()` allows the app developer to start the [heap profiling supervisor](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/heap_profiling/multi_process/supervisor.h;drc=83d6a18bb1a14348c1050905353aad9ba559d3be). Any traces recorded afterward will include heap dumps. However, after the trace is recorded, memory allocations will continue to be intercepted until the app is restarted.

It would be awesome to have a way to stop that.

Unfortunately, upstream doesn't support stopping heap profiling / the heap profiling supervisor yet (which is why this functionality wasn't included in #50826). In Chrome, once enabled, memory allocations will be recorded until the app is restarted.

Deepak had great suggestions in https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50826#discussion_r3078384865:

> The heap profile supervisor process once started remains a process wide singleton, and will continue to intercept memory allocations from new and existing clients post the tracing. Could we get a change in upstream to make this start/stop on demand ? The other option would be to have our own supervisor that controls the lifetime of the heapprofilingservice but that would duplicate a lot of code with upstream, we can pursue that if addition of stop api is not possible in upstream.

### Proposed Solution

Two options:

1. Add a function `contentTracing.disableHeapProfiling()`
2. Refactor the API more broadly:
   - Remove `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()`
   - Add heap profiling options to the `contentTracing.startRecording()` `TraceConfig` instead, e.g.:
     ```js
     contentTracing.startRecording({
       heapProfiling: {
         mode: 'all',
         samplingRate: 100000,
         stackMode: 'native',
       }
     })
     ```
   - When heap profiling options are passed to `contentTracing.startRecording()`:
     - First start the heap profiling supervisor
     - Once the heap profiling supervisor has started, start the recording
   - When `contentTracing.stopRecording()` is called:
     - Stop the trace
     - Stop the heap profiling supervisor again

Option 2 has a cleaner API. (We marked `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()` as experimental to allow for exactly this kind of refactoring.)

Option 1 can work with:
- `--trace-startup=disabled-by-default-memory-infra --trace-startup-format=json --trace-startup-file=/path/to/trace.json` command line parameters to start profiling as early as possible
- [Chrome DevTools Protocol tracing](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Tracing/) (untested but I think it's likely to work)

This is a trade-off between having a nicer API or supporting more functionality.

### Alternatives Considered

See above. :)

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Operating System Version

Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-110-generic)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

In the `select-serial-port` IPC event, `portList[n].portName` should be the **full device node path**: `/dev/ttyUSB0` (or `/dev/ttyACM0`, `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` on macOS, etc.).

### Actual Behavior

`portName` contains the **device basename** (e.g. `ttyUSB0`) instead of the full device node path (`/dev/ttyUSB0`). Chromium uses this stored path when `port.open()` is subsequently called, so it attempts to open the file `ttyUSB0` relative to the working directory, which fails with `ENOENT` → `NetworkError: Failed to open serial port`.

The user is a member of `dialout`, the device exists at `/dev/ttyUSB0`, and the same Web Serial code works correctly in Chrome and Chromium browsers.

author: gdavidkov
title: Frameless BrowserWindow.getBounds() inflates by resize-hit insets after setResizable(true → false) on Windows (regression in 41.2.1 from #50863)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.2.1, 41.2.2, 43.0.0-nightly.20260421

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, scaleFactor 1.375

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

On a frameless BrowserWindow, calling setResizable(false) should not change the values returned by getBounds() / getContentBounds(). The window's logical rect should remain equal to the rect passed to setBounds().

### Actual Behavior

After setResizable(true → false) on a frameless window, getBounds() and getContentBounds() both report a rect inflated by the resize-hit insets introduced in #50863:
- x: -8
- width: +16 (8 left + 8 right)
- height: +9 (0 top + 9 bottom)

The inflation is steady-state (persists indefinitely). getContentBounds() equals getBounds() at this point, so the expanded hit-target rect is being reported as both the window rect and the content rect rather than kept as a hit-test-only extension outside the window.

Bisect (same harness, same machine, scaleFactor 1.375):

| Electron | t1 delta after `setBounds` | t2 delta after `setResizable(false)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 41.2.0 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` ✅ |
| 41.2.1 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |
| 41.2.2 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |
| 43.0.0-nightly.20260421 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |

The only change between 41.2.0 and 41.2.1 that touches this path is #50863.

Sample output (43.0.0-nightly.20260421):
```text
t1 - after setBounds(requested)
  requested  : {"x":200,"y":200,"width":400,"height":300}
  getBounds  : {"x":200,"y":200,"width":400,"height":301}
  delta      : {"x":0,"y":0,"w":0,"h":1}         <-- DPR rounding only

t2 - IMMEDIATELY after setResizable(false)
  requested  : {"x":200,"y":200,"width":400,"height":300}
  getBounds  : {"x":192,"y":200,"width":416,"height":309}
  getContent : {"x":192,"y":200,"width":416,"height":309}
  delta      : {"x":-8,"y":0,"w":16,"h":9}       <-- BUG

t3 - 50 ms later (inflation persists)
  delta      : {"x":-8,"y":0,"w":16,"h":9}
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/c833fe56f3159fcfce90853a64cb64cd

_No response_

author: mitchchn
title: Add API to get cursor position relative to the window
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

It's possible to get the position of the mouse cursor relative to the display with `screen.getCursorPoint()`.

On Wayland, this function inadvertently gave the cursor position relative to the active _window_ rather than the display. While this was the intended behaviour, it is still a useful capability which Electron should support.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `BaseWindow.getCursorPoint()` API which provides coordinates relative to the window. (So 0,0 is the top left corner of the window.)

### Alternatives Considered

Developers can get the cursor position relative to web content with a DOM event listener in the renderer, e.g. `mousemove` event. However this does not work well if you use multiple web content views, and of course it does not work outside the web content area for framed windows.

### Additional Information

Refs https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51153.

author: Aevarkan
title: [Documentation]: Emphasise platform differences still exist with cross-platform support
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Referring to Electron as cross-platform may cause developers to overlook how, even though one JavaScript codebase works for Windows, macOS, and Linux, performance characteristics aren't always the same for all platforms.

I filed an issue to address this for one case earlier:
- https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49727

There, the issue was the `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` API performing much worse on Linux, as compared to Windows and macOS. The performance disparity was caught as I was testing the application on Linux, in addition to the main developer testing on macOS and Windows.

While the API documentation states **platform availability**, such as an API only being available on macOS, it generally doesn't include whether **performance** might differ across platforms that are supported.

I believe this could mislead developers into thinking an Electron application performs the same across all platforms, and, as a result, overlook any platform specific issues that may come up.

### Proposed Solution

Add a section in [`Docs > Best Practices > Performance`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/performance) that emphasises the possibility for issues to only exist on one platform, even though Electron is a cross-platform framework.

I was thinking a section like:
> ## Platform Differences
> While Electron is a cross-platform framework, there may still be differences between platforms. An API, although it may support Windows, macOS, and Linux, is not guaranteed to **perform** the same across them.
>
> During development, be aware of the possibility that the performance of an Electron application running on your local device may not necessarily be identical performance-wise to the same application running on another platform. 

### Alternatives Considered

These performance differences could also be documented for each API.

I imagine this idea wouldn't be mutually exclusive with the first one.

### Additional Information

I'm making this issue primarily to get any others' thoughts on this, as I reckon this is a pretty big topic.

Happy to have a discussion 🙂

author: solome
title: [Feature Request]: Support per-corner radii in View.setBorderRadius()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

## Problem Description

`View.setBorderRadius(radius)` currently only accepts a single uniform radius.

I am building a browser-like UI in Electron with:

- a custom top navigation / toolbar area
- a webpage content area below it
- a composed surface that should look like a single rounded browser container

In this kind of layout, I often need different radii per corner instead of one radius for all four corners.

A common example is:

- top toolbar: rounded top-left / top-right corners, square bottom corners
- content area: square top corners, rounded bottom-left / bottom-right corners

With the current API, a uniform radius is not expressive enough for this kind of browser-style composition.

This is especially relevant when using `WebContentsView` for the page content and native `View`s for the surrounding shell UI. I can build the layout, but I cannot describe the corner geometry precisely enough with the current API shape.


### Proposed Solution

Extend `View.setBorderRadius()` to support per-corner radii in addition to the existing single-number form.

For example:

```js
view.setBorderRadius(12)

view.setBorderRadius({
  topLeft: 12,
  topRight: 12,
  bottomRight: 0,
  bottomLeft: 0
})
```

This would preserve backward compatibility while allowing browser-like shells and other composed native layouts to be expressed much more cleanly.

A per-corner object form also feels less error-prone and more self-documenting than a positional multi-argument overload.

## Why This Would Help

My use case is to simulate a browser interface where the custom top navigation bar and the webpage content area visually belong to the same rounded container.

Today, the lack of per-corner control makes this difficult:

- a single radius rounds corners that should remain square
- splitting the UI across multiple native views becomes visually awkward
- browser-like composition requires extra workarounds for something that is fundamentally a corner-geometry problem



### Alternatives Considered

- Applying CSS `border-radius` / `clip-path` inside the webpage.
  This is not a reliable substitute when the content is arbitrary web content, because page-controlled root backgrounds, loading skeletons, or transitions can make the result fragile.

- Building a more complex native wrapper around the content.
  This is possible, but it is a much heavier solution than simply allowing per-corner radii on the existing API.


### Additional Information

I am not asking this API to change the current clipping or hit-testing model of `setBorderRadius()`.

This request is specifically about allowing asymmetric / per-corner radii so Electron apps can build browser-like native layouts more precisely.

I wrote it to push the strongest argument for your real use case. If you want, I can also rewrite this into a version that explicitly asks for the 4-argument signature `setBorderRadius(topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft)`.

author: anishmoncivarghese
title: MAS-sandboxed Electron 41.3.0 crashes at startup on macOS 26.x with `EXC_BREAKPOINT brk 0` deep in V8 (`ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0` thread)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0 (also reproducible on 36.9.5)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253) — also reported on 26.3.1 (25D2128)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None confirmed. The shipping build that crashes was Electron 36.9.5; bumping to 41.3.0 produces a similar crash with slightly different V8 frames, suggesting the bug spans the 36 → 41 range under macOS 26 + MAS sandbox.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A correctly-signed, MAS-sandboxed Electron app should launch normally on macOS 26.x when delivered through TestFlight or the Mac App Store.

### Actual Behavior

App crashes at startup with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` / `brk 0` on a thread named `ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0`. Crash occurs ~2 seconds after launch on Electron 36, ~13 seconds on Electron 41 — gets further in initialization on the newer version but dies in the same place. No window is ever shown.

The crash signature has two consistent characteristics:
1. Triggered thread is always `ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0` (a Chromium worker for blocking foreground work).
2. A parallel `ThreadPoolForegroundWorker` thread is mid-`dns_configuration_copy` (or similar resolver work via `_dns_open_sys_config_notify` / `res_9_vinit`) when the crash happens.
3. A second worker thread frequently shows `(Instruction Abort) Translation fault` with `pc == far` — the CPU tried to execute code at a non-executable address, which strongly suggests JIT-page permission failure.

The `brk 0` on the triggered thread looks like V8's downstream `IMMEDIATE_CRASH` after the JIT-slot bookkeeping invariant breaks.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Crash signature — Electron 41.3.0 (build 10, TestFlight)

```
Process:             Lekhanam [1542]
Identifier:          com.lekhanam.app
Version:             1.3.2 (10)
Beta:                YES
Code Type:           ARM-64 (Native)
OS Version:          macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)
Hardware Model:      MacBookAir10,1
Triggered by Thread: 22  ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0
Exception Type:      EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Exception Codes:     0x0000000000000001, 0x0000000114ddbef0
```

Crashed thread (frames listed by nearest exported symbol; huge offsets are inlined / unsymbolicated functions):
```
Thread 22 Crashed:: ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0
0   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3408620
1   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3408424
2   Electron Framework  v8::Script::GetCompileHintsCollector() const + 25856
3   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3615324
4   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3615348
5   Electron Framework  xml_ffi$cxxbridge1$194$try_get_last_event_position + 234160
6   Electron Framework  xml_ffi$cxxbridge1$194$try_get_last_event_position + 233432
7   Electron Framework  v8::Object::ObjectProtoToString + 87044
8   Electron Framework  _v8_internal_Node_Print + 11342316
9   Electron Framework  rust_png$cxxbridge1$194$ResultOfStreamWriter$unwrap + 22548
10  Electron Framework  temporal_rs_PlainTime_second + 1620
11  Electron Framework  v8::ArrayBuffer::GetBackingStore() + 32000
12  Electron Framework  v8::ArrayBuffer::GetBackingStore() + 28764
13  Electron Framework  v8::ArrayBuffer::GetBackingStore() + 24300
14  Electron Framework  v8::ArrayBuffer::GetBackingStore() + 22764

16  Electron Framework  v8::ArrayBuffer::GetBackingStore() + 22148
17  Electron Framework  v8::Context::SetAlignedPointerInEmbedderData + 5904
18  libsystem_pthread.dylib  _pthread_start + 136
19  libsystem_pthread.dylib  thread_start + 8
```

Parallel `ThreadPoolForegroundWorker` (Thread 10) deep in libresolv init showing `(Instruction Abort) Translation fault` with `pc == far`:
```
Thread 10:
0   libresolv.9.dylib   _dns_open_sys_config_notify + 0
1   libresolv.9.dylib   res_9_vinit + 144
2   Electron Framework  v8::CpuProfile::GetSamplesCount() const + 1887772
3   Electron Framework  v8::CpuProfile::GetSamplesCount() const + 1887660
4   Electron Framework  v8::CpuProfile::GetSamplesCount() const + 1836124
5   Electron Framework  v8::CpuProfile::GetSamplesCount() const + 1829136

pc == far == 6934817064
```

The PC equaling FAR on this thread is the CPU's "tried to execute code at an unmapped/non-executable address." This is what JIT-page permission failure looks like at the CPU level.

## Crash signature — Electron 36.9.5 (build 7, currently shipping on App Store)

Same triggered-thread name, same DNS-related context, slightly different V8 frames (V8 was rewritten between Chromium 136 and 138):

```
Thread 21 Crashed:: ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0
0   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3279708
1   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3279508
2   Electron Framework  v8::internal::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor() + 11400
3   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3489000
4   Electron Framework  ares_dns_rr_get_ttl + 3489024
5   Electron Framework  v8::Object::GetConstructorName() + 228128
6   Electron Framework  v8::Object::GetConstructorName() + 227384
7   Electron Framework  v8::metrics::Recorder::GetContext + 306404
8   Electron Framework  _v8_internal_Node_Print + 10522428
9   Electron Framework  node::PrincipalRealm::wasm_streaming_object_constructor() const + 11464
10  Electron Framework  0x10a8b61b8 + 25016
11  Electron Framework  v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation + 84540
12  Electron Framework  v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation + 77700
13  Electron Framework  v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation + 74892
14  Electron Framework  v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation + 86344
15  Electron Framework  v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation + 73928
```

The Electron 36 stack explicitly shows `v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::RegisterJitAllocation`. The Electron 41 stack does not (V8 refactored the JIT allocator) but the failure mode (worker thread, brk 0, parallel CPU instruction abort on a different worker) is consistent.

## To Reproduce

I do not have a public minimal repro yet, but the failure conditions are tightly specified:

1. Electron app distributed via Mac App Store (MAS sandbox enabled).
2. Hardened runtime enabled (`CS_RUNTIME` set on every Mach-O — verified via `codesign -dvv` showing `flags=0x10000(runtime)` on main + helpers).
3. Entitlements include `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`, `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (with or without `cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` — tested both, no difference).
4. Running on macOS 26.x (confirmed on 26.3.1 and 26.4.1).
5. Apple Silicon (arm64).
6. Delivered through the App Store / TestFlight channel (so the bundle has a valid `_MASReceipt`; sideloaded MAS-signed bundles do not launch on modern macOS regardless of correctness — that's a separate AMFI gate, not this bug).

I'm happy to build a minimal Electron-Forge / electron-quick-start MAS-signed sample and upload it via TestFlight if that would help. Please let me know what would be most useful.

## Things tried that did NOT fix it

These are documented to save the next person's time:

1. **Bumped Electron 36.9.5 → 41.3.0.** Crash signature changed slightly (V8 was rewritten) but failure mode identical.
2. **Re-signed with Apple's `codesign` instead of `rcodesign`.** Signing pipeline became cleaner but the runtime crash was unaffected — both signers were producing valid signatures all along.
3. **Added `app.commandLine.appendSwitch('no-proxy-server')` to the main process** before `app.whenReady()`. Hypothesis: Chromium's PAC V8 isolate on a worker thread was the crash site. Crash unchanged.
4. **Removed `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`** from entitlements (it's deprecated on macOS 14+ and theoretically conflicts with `cs.allow-jit`). Crash unchanged.
5. **Verified TestFlight delivery channel.** App was installed via TestFlight (visible in crash reports as `Beta: YES`, `is_beta: 1`, `entitledBeta: true`), confirming we're past every signing/profile/entitlement validation gate. The crash is purely runtime.

## Hypothesis

V8's JIT-page handling on worker threads (specifically the `ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0` thread that handles DNS / network-resolver work in Chromium) is hitting a MAP_JIT lifecycle issue on macOS 26 under the MAS sandbox. macOS 26 tightened MAP_JIT enforcement: pages need explicit `pthread_jit_write_protect_np()` toggles, and worker threads in Chromium's network/resolver subsystem appear to lose RX permission before V8 attempts to execute. Under hardened runtime + sandbox, the resulting fault is fatal.

The pattern of "DNS-blocking thread + V8 frames + parallel worker hitting Instruction Abort with `pc == far`" is consistent across both Electron 36 and 41, which is why I think this is at the V8/Chromium layer rather than something specific to either Electron release.

## Build / sign details

- Build pipeline: `electron-builder` (no signing) → custom shell script using Apple's `codesign` (inside-out: dylibs/.node files → frameworks → helpers → main bundle) → `productbuild`.
- Signing identity: `3rd Party Mac Developer Application: Anish Varghese (65UF42MSBU)`.
- Provisioning profile: STORE distribution, valid until 2027.
- Hardened runtime: enabled on every Mach-O (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`).
- DER entitlements: present (verified via `codesign -d --entitlements -`).
- Native modules in bundle: `node-llama-cpp` and `nodejs-whisper` (both inert at runtime under MAS via `process.mas` guards), `@reflink/reflink-darwin-arm64` (active).

## Additional Information

The same app:
- Runs fine in `npm run dev` (unsandboxed Electron 41.3.0) on the same macOS 26.4.1 machine.
- Runs fine on macOS 15.x with the MAS-signed build.
- Is currently shipping on the App Store at version 1.3.1 (build 7, Electron 36.9.5) and crashing for all macOS 26 users.

author: aaddrick
title: Linux: matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)') returns false while other WCO signals report active
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Nobara 43 (Fedora-based), KDE Plasma 6, kernel 6.19.10. I reproduced it under both X11 and Wayland sessions.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None within the currently-supported window. I tested the same repro against Electron 38.8.6 (Chromium 140), 39.8.9 (Chromium 142), 40.9.2 (Chromium 144), and 41.3.0 (Chromium 146); the matchMedia mismatch reproduces identically on every one of them, with the other three signals reporting WCO active and the same `804 × 40` rect each time. So this isn't a regression within the supported window. Either the bridge has always been wrong on Linux or it regressed before Electron 38, which is already EOL.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a `BrowserWindow` is created with `frame: false`, `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, and a populated `titleBarOverlay` object, all four standard Window-Controls-Overlay entry points should agree that WCO is active:

1. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` → `true`
2. `windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()` → non-zero rect
3. `env(titlebar-area-width / -height / -x / -y)` → populated CSS env values
4. `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches` → `true`

That's the agreement pages rely on for WCO-aware layout. The [Window Controls Overlay explainer](https://github.com/WICG/window-controls-overlay/blob/main/explainer.md) and the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Controls_Overlay_API) both document the media query as the recommended CSS detection point.

### Actual Behavior

Three of the four signals correctly report WCO is active. **Only the `matchMedia` query disagrees and returns `matches: false`.**

Probe output from the attached repro running on Electron 41.3.0 (Wayland session, but X11 produces the same result; identical output verified on 38.8.6, 39.8.9, 40.9.2 — see *Last Known Working Electron version* above):

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 804 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 804px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

The titlebar-area rect (804 × 40) matches the configured `titleBarOverlay.height: 40`, which confirms Chromium has applied WCO at the layout level. The CSS `env()` values come from the same source. But pages following the W3C-recommended detection pattern (`matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` and the corresponding `@media` rule) see WCO as inactive and skip whatever WCO-specific layout they would have rendered.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/aaddrick/90a16bf22da070e07ff382c7a89ae3d8

### Additional Information

**Issue tracker searches** (extending the Preflight checkbox above). I searched for `windowControlsOverlay`, `WCO`, `titleBarOverlay`, `display-mode window-controls-overlay`, and `matchMedia display-mode`. No existing match. The closest neighbors are #34947 (BrowserView WCO support, separate concern) and #51000 / #45798 (Linux WCO button order / native context menu, different surfaces).

**Sibling repo with the Chromium PWA companion test.** I also published the same Electron Fiddle files alongside a Chromium-side PWA repro at https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch. The Electron repro lives at the repo root (it mirrors the gist linked above), and the Chromium-side test is under [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa). Either source works. I included the gist to satisfy the standard testcase-gist convention, and the repo carries the additional Chromium investigation that doesn't fit a flat gist.

**AI disclosure** (per the Electron governance AI policy): I drafted the repro and this report with assistance from Anthropic's Opus 4.7 via Claude Code. I then ran the repro locally on Electron 41.3.0 (Nobara 43 / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland), empirically verified the four-signal mismatch, and reviewed this body line-by-line before submission. I'm responsible for the contents and can answer follow-up questions.

**Chromium activation paths I tried on Linux.** I tried three separate paths to reproduce against Google Chrome 147.0.7727.55 on the same Linux box. None of them activate the WCO API surface in plain Chromium on Linux:

1. **Install as a PWA.** I packaged an equivalent app (manifest with `"display_override": ["window-controls-overlay"]`, served over `http://localhost`, installed via the omnibox install icon). Chrome parses the manifest and the registrar resolves the display mode to `window-controls-overlay`, but the per-app boolean `window_controls_overlay_enabled` stays `false` and there's no UI control to flip it on Linux. From `chrome://web-app-internals` for the installed app:

   ```
   "display_override": ["window-controls-overlay"],
   "registrar_evaluated_fields": { "display_mode": "window-controls-overlay", … },
   "window_controls_overlay_enabled": false,
   "user_display_mode": "kStandalone"
   ```

   The PWA opens in `display: standalone`. All four signals report inactive.

2. **`chrome://flags`.** The historical `enable-desktop-pwas-window-controls-overlay` flag from the original [Intent to Experiment](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/HNHbpxvrECA) isn't in Chrome 147 anymore. The feature shipped stable in Chrome 102 and the flag was retired. Adjacent flags (`enable-desktop-pwas-borderless`, `enable-desktop-pwas-additional-windowing-controls`, `enable-desktop-pwas-tab-strip*`) are unrelated to WCO activation.

3. **DevTools Application → Manifest → "Emulate the Window Controls Overlay".** The checkbox draws OS-style window-control buttons over the page area, but it doesn't plumb any of the four API signals. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` stays `false`, `getTitlebarAreaRect()` returns `0×0`, `env(titlebar-area-*)` is empty, and `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` returns `false`. The emulation is visual-only on Linux Chrome 147. This contradicts [devtoolstips.org's description of the feature](https://devtoolstips.org/tips/en/simulate-pwa-wco/), which says the env values should activate. In my test on Linux they did not.

So there's no path to observe Chromium-side WCO API behaviour on Linux today, and therefore no upstream baseline I could produce locally. There is, however, prior-art evidence that upstream Chromium handles this correctly elsewhere: [microsoft/vscode#160696](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/160696) explicitly documents that Chromium *does* match `(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` from `matchMedia` when WCO is active for installed PWAs. That places the divergence on Electron's `titleBarOverlay` activation path, not on upstream Blink — Electron's path activates the visible / rect / env signals on Linux (as shown in *Actual Behavior* above) but the `matchMedia` evaluator stays detached from that activation. If a maintainer knows of a way to force `window_controls_overlay_enabled: true` on Linux Chrome (a custom build, a LevelDB patch, a CDP method I missed), I'm happy to re-test. The Chromium PWA repro itself lives at [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa) in the sibling repo linked above.

**How I ran into this.** It surfaced during [aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian#538](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/pull/538). I was packaging an Electron-based web app for Linux and trying to match the Windows / macOS topbar layout. The bundled web app uses `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` to decide whether to render its WCO-aware topbar. On Electron Linux that returns `false` even though WCO is active, so the topbar silently doesn't render and the Linux build can't match the Windows layout despite the BrowserWindow being configured identically. Side-by-side, with the same app and identical `titleBarOverlay` config:

Windows:

![Windows: single-bar topbar with hamburger / sidebar / search / back-forward / ghost icons inline with the window controls](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/raw/master/docs/screenshots/windows-titlebar.png)

Linux (best achievable with the current workaround):

![Linux: stacked layout — DE-drawn titlebar on top, in-app topbar below, no inline window controls](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/raw/master/docs/screenshots/linux-titlebar.png)

The full investigation chain, including two adjacent Linux WCO observations that turned out to already be tracked at #34947 and #37789, is in [`docs/learnings/linux-topbar-shim.md`](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/blob/experiment/linux-topbar-wco/docs/learnings/linux-topbar-shim.md). Our current workaround is a preload shim that overrides `matchMedia` (and a couple of adjacent surfaces). A fix here would let us drop the `matchMedia` portion of that shim.

**Why I think it's worth filing despite Linux WCO being a moving target.** The mismatch is internal to Electron's own WCO surface. Three of four entry points agree the feature is active; only the documented detection point disagrees. That contradiction is independent of whether WCO behaves correctly elsewhere on Linux, and it silently breaks any web app that does feature detection the W3C-recommended way (`matchMedia` / `@media (display-mode: window-controls-overlay)`). The activation-paths investigation above also implies this is reachable only via Electron on Linux today, since plain Chromium-Linux doesn't expose a path to activate WCO for installed PWAs.

**Concrete impact.** Pages whose conditional WCO layout relies on the `@media` rule render their non-WCO layout while WCO is active, which leads to visual collisions with the overlay area. Pages that detect via `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` work correctly. Most JS-side detection examples in the wild use one or both, and any that use only the `@media` route are silently broken on Electron Linux today.

body:

### Electron Version

41.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Reproduced on Nobara 43 (Fedora-based, KDE Plasma 6, kernel 6.19.10) under both X11 and Wayland sessions, and on Windows 11 (23H2) in a VM today.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None within the currently-supported window. The same probe reproduces identically on 38.8.6 (Chromium 140), 39.8.9 (Chromium 142), 40.9.2 (Chromium 144), and 41.3.0 (Chromium 146) on Linux, and on 41.3.0 on Windows 11. Either this has always been wrong or it regressed before 38, which is EOL.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When a `BrowserWindow` is created with `frame: false`, `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, and a populated `titleBarOverlay` object, all four standard WCO entry points should agree:

1. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` → `true`
2. `windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()` → non-zero rect
3. `env(titlebar-area-width / -height / -x / -y)` → populated CSS env values
4. `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches` → `true`

The W3C [Window Controls Overlay explainer](https://github.com/WICG/window-controls-overlay/blob/main/explainer.md) and the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Controls_Overlay_API) both name the media query as the recommended CSS detection point.

### Actual Behavior

Three of four signals report WCO active. **Only `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` disagrees and returns `matches: false`.** The same mismatch reproduces on Linux and on Windows 11.

Probe output, Electron 41.3.0, Linux (Wayland; X11 identical):

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 804 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 804px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

Probe output, Electron 41.3.0, Windows 11:

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 763 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 763px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

The titlebar-area rect matches the configured `titleBarOverlay.height: 40` on both platforms, which confirms Chromium has applied WCO at the layout level. The CSS `env()` values share that source. But pages following the W3C-recommended detection pattern see WCO as inactive and skip the WCO-specific layout they would have rendered.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/aaddrick/90a16bf22da070e07ff382c7a89ae3d8

### Additional Information

**Relationship to #51389.** I filed [#51389](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51389) earlier today framing this as Linux-specific. After source investigation and a Windows 11 reproduction, that framing was wrong. I withdrew #51389 and am refiling here with the corrected scope. The probe output, gist, and sibling repo are unchanged; only the platform list and the root-cause section are new.

**Root cause.** Electron's `WebContents` (`shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.h:124-125`) inherits from `content::WebContentsDelegate` and overrides ~50 methods. It does not override `GetDisplayMode()`. A full grep of the tree confirms zero references to `display_mode` outside two unrelated header includes. Without an override, Chromium's default returns `blink::mojom::DisplayMode::kBrowser`, which gets baked into `WebPreferences::display_mode` in `RenderViewHostImpl::ComputeWebPreferences()` and shipped to Blink. The matchMedia evaluator for `(display-mode: …)` reads from there, so it always evaluates against `kBrowser` regardless of how the BrowserWindow was configured.

The other three signals work because they take a separate mojo path: `NativeWindow::NotifyLayoutWindowControlsOverlay()` → `BrowserWindow::UpdateWindowControlsOverlay()` (`electron_api_browser_window.cc:205`) → `web_contents()->UpdateWindowControlsOverlay(rect)`. That path never touches the `display_mode` web preference, so it stays at `kBrowser` and the four signals diverge.

**Fix.** I have a 16-line patch on a local branch that overrides `GetDisplayMode()` on Electron's `WebContents` and routes the answer through the same `IsWindowControlsOverlayEnabled()` gate (`native_window.h:390-398`) the other three signals already use. Same input, same answer; the four signals agree by construction. The override also returns `kFullscreen` for fullscreen windows and `kStandalone` for frameless windows without titleBarOverlay, which matches Chromium's PWA semantics so existing `isStandalone()`-style checks (e.g., the one in microsoft/vscode#160696) keep working. With the patch applied on Linux, the probe table reads `matches: true` and all four signals agree. PR coming separately.

**Sibling repo with the Chromium PWA companion test.** I published the same Electron Fiddle files alongside a Chromium-side PWA repro at https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch. The Electron repro lives at the repo root (mirrors the gist). The Chromium-side test is under [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa). Either source works.

**AI disclosure** (per the Electron governance AI policy): I drafted the repro and this report with assistance from Anthropic's Opus 4.7 via Claude Code. I ran the repro locally on Electron 41.3.0 (Nobara 43 / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland) and on a Windows 11 VM, empirically verified the four-signal mismatch on both, and reviewed this body line-by-line before submission. I'm responsible for the contents and can answer follow-up questions.

**How I ran into this.** It surfaced during [aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian#538](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/pull/538), packaging an Electron-based web app for Linux. The bundled web app uses `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` to decide whether to render its WCO-aware topbar. On Electron Linux that returns `false` even though WCO is active, so the topbar silently doesn't render. I assumed it was Linux-only because that's where I first saw it; the Windows VM repro disproved that.

**Concrete impact.** Pages whose conditional WCO layout relies on the `@media (display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` rule render their non-WCO layout while WCO is active, which causes visual collisions with the overlay area on every Electron platform. Pages that detect via `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` work correctly. Most JS-side detection examples in the wild use one or both, and any that use only the `@media` route are silently broken.

author: JamesHabben
title: Custom protocol via protocol.handle() not compatible with Chromium media playback
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

15.7.4

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A `<video>` element should be able to play a local MP4 file when served via `protocol.handle()` using a custom scheme, provided that:

- The response includes a valid `Content-Type` (e.g., `video/mp4`)
- Proper range request handling is implemented (`206 Partial Content`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, etc.)
- The response body contains the correct byte ranges from the file

This should behave equivalently to other Electron-supported methods of serving local media, including:

- `file://` URLs  
- HTTP (`http://127.0.0.1`)  

`protocol.handle()` should support media playback use cases in parity with other mechanisms for local file access.

### Actual Behavior

In the attached repro, the videos play correctly via `file://`, HTTP, and blob URL methods, but fail when served through `protocol.handle()` with a manually constructed `Response` (Buffer or stream), even when headers and range handling appear correct. Video1 plays with a `net.fetch`, but video2 fails. Both fail with buffer and stream inside `handle()`. Both also fail with the deprecated `registerFileProtocol`.

### Testcase Gist URL

body:

### Electron Version

41.5.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

In the Gist is a fiddle which sets a `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` handler to intercept the WebSocket connection which is made in `renderer.js`.

The Electron main process logs should show these logs:

```
Proxying WebSocket from wss://echo.websocket.org/ to local server
New WebSocket connection: ......
[client→server]Ping!
[server→client]Ping!
```

The first log line is from when we setup the interception.

The second is when the renderer connects through the WebSocket proxy.

The third and fourth are from the messages sent through the proxy.

Inside the Renderer you should see these messages on the screen to show what happened with the WebSocket connection:

```
[ws/open]
[ws/message] Request served by XXXXXXXX
[ws/message] Ping!
```

### Actual Behavior

The logs in the Electron main process are just:

```
Proxying WebSocket from wss://echo.websocket.org/ to local server
```

This indicates that the `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` handler is being called correctly, but as no other logs follow the WebSocket connection is not being correctly redirected to the proxy.

The logs inside the renderer are correct. Showing it is connecting to and communicating with the echo server.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/fede254f6a62f0c95abc18c990abc122

### Additional Information

It seems to me like the `ProxyingWebSocket::ContinueToHeadersReceived` method is not correctly handling `redirect_url_`: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/99117903fe94b9959f4c26a3b04d3e773749ae7d/shell/browser/net/proxying_websocket.cc#L95-L115

I beleive the code for standard requests is here: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/99117903fe94b9959f4c26a3b04d3e773749ae7d/shell/browser/net/proxying_url_loader_factory.cc#L509-L512

Related issue which was close due to lack of reproduction: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/31191

author: dgsratiu
title: [Bug]: SysDragImage top-level window leaked on Windows when drag completes in another application
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Whatever ships with Discord 1.0.9236 (binary doesn't expose it cleanly in version metadata; see "Notes" below).

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home, 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — I haven't bisected. Behaviour observed in current shipping Discord client.

### Expected Behavior

When a drag operation initiated by an Electron application ends — regardless of whether the drop target is the same Electron window, a different window in the same process, a different application entirely, or `Esc`/cancel — the `SysDragImage` top-level window created by `IDragSourceHelper::InitializeFromBitmap` (or its `SetDragImage` cousin) should be destroyed.

### Actual Behavior

When the drag is consumed by a drop target in **another process** (in my repro: Chrome rendering claude.ai's file uploader), the `SysDragImage` window owned by the originating Electron process is **not destroyed**. It persists indefinitely as an orphan top-level window with the following Win32 styles:

- `WS_EX_TOPMOST` — sits over every other window
- `WS_EX_LAYERED` — alpha-composited
- `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` — passes mouse input through (so it can't be dismissed by clicking)
- `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW` — invisible to Alt-Tab
- Class name: `SysDragImage`
- Window title: `Drag`
- Size: matches the drag-image bitmap (in my repro: 390×130 px at the position where the cursor was on drop)

Visually it appears as a stuck rectangle (white in my case, presumably whatever the failed-to-render drag-image bitmap was) floating on top of the desktop, surviving:

- The drop completing successfully in the receiving application.
- Closing the receiving application.
- Restarting `explorer.exe`.
- Pressing `Esc`, alt-tabbing, switching virtual desktops.

The only ways to clear it I have found:

1. Quit the originating Electron application (Discord), or
2. Surgically `PostMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0)` to the orphan HWND from a separate tool. The Electron process continues to run normally afterward — no functional regression observed.

### Testcase Gist URL

I do not have a minimal Electron testcase yet. The repro path requires whatever drag-source registration Discord performs. Happy to bisect / build a minimal Electron app that calls `webContents.startDrag` (or whatever Discord uses) if a maintainer thinks that would help isolate it from Discord-specific code.

### Additional Information

**Reproduction (Windows 11):**

1. Have Discord (1.0.9236) running with the main window visible. (The bug doesn't seem to require Discord to be focused.)
2. In Chrome, open https://claude.ai/ and start a chat (the file-upload drop target there triggers the bug; presumably any Chromium-rendered drop target in another process does).
3. From Windows File Explorer, drag any file into the claude.ai chat window. The drop succeeds — the file uploads normally.
4. Observe: a translucent rectangle, sized to the drag preview, remains painted on top of every window. Discord still works.

**Forensic evidence (PowerShell `EnumWindows` enumeration after the bug occurs):**

```
HWND=0x164140A  PID=8704 (Discord)
  Class:    SysDragImage
  Title:    Drag
  Size:     390x130 @ 947,587
  ExStyles: TopMost=True, Layered=True, Transparent=True, ToolWindow=True
```

PID 8704 was the Discord main process. Posting `WM_CLOSE` to that HWND alone clears the artefact and leaves Discord running:

```powershell
[W]::PostMessage(0x164140A, 0x0010, 0, 0)  # WM_CLOSE
# Window destroyed; Discord unaffected.
```

**Hypothesis on root cause:**

Chromium's drag-source code on Windows uses `IDragSourceHelper::InitializeFromBitmap` to register a drag image with the Windows shell. The shell creates the `SysDragImage` top-level window to render the bitmap and follows the cursor through the drag. Cleanup is supposed to occur when the drag completes (in `IDropSource::QueryContinueDrag` returning `DRAGDROP_S_DROP`/`DRAGDROP_S_CANCEL`, or via the shell's own teardown when the drag-drop session ends).

The leak appears to be specific to drops that occur in a **different OS-level drop target** than the source. When source and target are both inside the same Chromium/Electron app, cleanup happens. When the target is an external HWND owned by another process (Chrome.exe in this case, presumably any non-Electron drop target), the source's drag-end callback either doesn't fire or doesn't reach the cleanup path that destroys the `SysDragImage` HWND.

This is consistent with similar drag-source lifecycle bugs that have surfaced in adjacent contexts:

- Vencord/Vesktop#541 — Linux: Vesktop's input handling breaks until relaunch after a cross-app drag. Different OS surface, plausibly the same lifecycle bug.
- electron/electron#39839 — Drag-and-drop spawning a phantom Electron window plus a save dialog in 27.0.0-beta.1.
- swaywm/wlroots#2889 — Drag image freezes in Chromium/Electron on X11/Wayland.

I do not have a Chromium repro outside Discord — happy to build one if useful.

### Notes

- I am reporting this against `electron/electron` rather than Chromium upstream because (a) Electron is the actually-shipping surface where this manifests, (b) the Electron team triages to Chromium when appropriate, and (c) public Chromium bug filing has friction. Feel free to redirect to crbug.com if that's the cleaner home.
- Discord ships its Electron build without exposing the version through standard binary metadata (`Discord.exe` advertises `ProductName=Discord, Description=Discord` only). I can't tell you the exact Electron version without invasive inspection.
- The originating drag may have been a OneDrive-virtualised file (the source folder was OneDrive-synced), which involves the OneDrive shell extension hydrating the file via `dllhost.exe`. I cannot rule out that this is a contributing factor — i.e. the leak might only occur when the drag-source data object involves shell-extension hydration. Worth checking with a non-OneDrive source.

When typing Chinese (using IME input methods such as Pinyin) inside a textarea in an Electron application on macOS, the IME candidate window should:

* Display correctly under or near the text cursor
* Show full candidate list (not only pre-edit text / pinyin)
* Follow the caret position accurately during typing
* Behave consistently with native applications and Chrome browser

### Actual Behavior

On macOS (26.3 / Tahoe), when using Electron (tested with Electron 31 - Electron 35) with a minimal reproduction project:

* IME input still works (pinyin composition is visible)
* However, the candidate window does not display correctly
    * In some cases, only the pinyin/pre-edit text is shown
    * Candidate list is missing or not rendered
    * Candidate window may appear empty or not attached to the input field
* The issue persists even in a minimal Electron application with a single <textarea> and no custom CSS or layout
* The same input method works correctly in Google Chrome on the same system

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

* Reproducible in a minimal Electron application with only a single textarea element (no frameworks, no custom CSS, no layout complexity).
* Issue persists after testing multiple Electron versions (Electron 31 - Electron 35).
* Disabling CSS entirely (removing all styles) does not resolve the issue.
* Disabling GPU acceleration, changing backgroundThrottling, and other webPreferences flags do not affect the behavior.
* Same IME input method works correctly in:
    * Google Chrome (latest version on macOS)
    * Native macOS applications
* Suggests issue is specific to Electron/Chromium rendering path on macOS IME integration layer rather than application code or styling.
* Input composition (pre-edit text / pinyin) is correctly received, indicating IME is functional; only candidate window rendering/attachment is affected.
* Likely related to macOS IME candidate window attachment behavior in Electron’s Chromium-based web input pipeline under macOS 26.x (Tahoe).

title: setDisplayMediaRequestHandler useSystemPicker crashes after custom handler capture on macOS
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

39.8.10

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4 / Darwin 25.4.0

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Expected Behavior

An app should be able to use a custom `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(..., { useSystemPicker: false })` flow for one `getDisplayMedia()` request, stop all returned tracks, and then later switch to `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(..., { useSystemPicker: true })` for a subsequent `getDisplayMedia()` request without hanging or crashing.

### Actual Behavior

After a custom handler capture completes and all tracks are stopped, switching the same Electron session back to `useSystemPicker: true` can crash the process when a source is selected in the macOS system picker.

The crash is native and cannot be caught in JavaScript:

```text
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSGenericException', reason: '*** Collection <__NSArrayM: ...> was mutated while being enumerated.'
*** First throw call stack:
(
  0   CoreFoundation                      __exceptionPreprocess
  1   libobjc.A.dylib                     objc_exception_throw
  2   CoreFoundation                      -[__NSSingleObjectEnumerator description]
  3   ScreenCaptureKit                    -[SCContentSharingPicker contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  4   ReplayKit                           -[RPScreenRecorder contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  5   ReplayKit                           -[RPDaemonProxy contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  ...
)
Electron exited with signal SIGTRAP
```

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the gist below.
2. Run `npm install`.
3. Run `npm start`.
4. Click `1. Custom picker capture`.
5. In the in-app custom source list, select a window.
6. Wait for the local preview to start.
7. Click `2. Stop tracks`.
8. Click `3. System picker capture`.
9. In the macOS system picker, select the same window.
10. The app crashes with the native ScreenCaptureKit stack above.

Control behavior: if `3. System picker capture` is used first after app start, the system picker works.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/brainwith/5a2d084a43850998e27e6bfaff984b17

### Additional Information

The minimal repro does not use any app-specific code or WebRTC publishing. It only uses:

- `desktopCapturer.getSources()` for the custom source list
- `session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(handler, { useSystemPicker: false })`
- `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()`
- `MediaStreamTrack.stop()`
- then `session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(handler, { useSystemPicker: true })`
- then `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()` again

I also tested stronger cleanup before switching back to system picker, including clearing references and stopping tracks. The crash still occurs, suggesting the issue is in the same-session transition from a custom handler capture to the macOS system picker.

author: Rush
title: Crash (SIGSEGV) on right-click in -webkit-app-region: drag on macOS 26
body:
## Description Right-clicking on an element with `-webkit-app-region: drag` in a `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` window causes a SIGSEGV crash (null pointer dereference at address 0x0) on macOS 26 (Tahoe, build 25C56). The crash occurs inside `[ElectronNSWindow sendEvent:]` → `[super sendEvent:]` when processing `NSEventTypeRightMouseDown`. The `sendEvent` override temporarily disables draggable regions via `WebContents::SetDisableDraggableRegions(true)`, which makes `draggable_region()` return `nullptr`. Something in Chromium's event routing then dereferences this null pointer. ## Versions - Tested on Electron 42.0.1 (Chromium 148) and 43.0.0-alpha.1 (Chromium 149) — both crash - Electron 41.3.0 does NOT crash - macOS 26.2 (25C56), Apple Silicon (Mac16,6) ## Minimal Reproduction ```js // main.js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600, titleBarStyle: 'hidden', webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: false, contextIsolation: true } }); win.loadURL('data:text/html,
RIGHT CLICK HERE TO CRASH
Content area
'); }); ``` ```json // package.json {"name":"crash-test","version":"1.0.0","main":"main.js"} ``` Steps: 1. Run `npx electron .` 2. Right-click on the gray "RIGHT CLICK HERE TO CRASH" bar 3. App crashes with SIGSEGV ## Crash Report (key frames) ``` Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000 Thread 0 Crashed:: CrBrowserMain 0 Electron Framework 0x114526b88 ... 7 AppKit 0x190e3c860 -[NSApplication(NSEventRouting) sendEvent:] + 1276 8 Electron Framework 0x10e92a9bc ``` ## Analysis The crash path is in `shell/browser/ui/cocoa/electron_ns_window.mm` line 224-243. The `sendEvent:` override calls `SetDisableDraggableRegions(true)` before `[super sendEvent:event]`. This makes `WebContents::draggable_region()` return `nullptr` (line 2191 of `electron_api_web_contents.cc`). On macOS 26, the Chromium event handler inside `[super sendEvent:]` appears to dereference this null pointer. This did NOT crash on macOS 15 or Electron 41. ## Expected Behavior Right-clicking on a drag region should show a context menu (or do nothing), not crash.

author: YUCLing
title: Allow overriding MPRIS service name
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, [Chromium hardcodes MPRIS service name](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/system_media_controls/linux/system_media_controls_linux.cc;l=141;drc=c83b80f441edc1c50de8d3977fa3feeb0ae96bc3) as `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.chromium.instance<pid here>`, thus preventing the app from accessing MPRIS bus within Flatpak sandbox environment ([Flatpak only allows](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/sandbox-permissions.html#d-bus-access) `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.$FLATPAK_ID` service name).

As a result, `MediaSession` will not be able to work properly within Flatpak environment.

### Proposed Solution

Allow the app to set its custom MPRIS suffix, e.g. `app.setMPRISServiceName("abc")` sets service name to `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.abc`.

### Alternatives Considered

None as of now

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: HXS482
title: Transparent frameless window shows white corners on focus loss (DWM inactive frame)
body:
## Problem

On Windows 11, a transparent frameless window (`frame: false` + `transparent: true` + `roundedCorners: false`) with CSS `clipPath: inset(0 round 16px)` for rounded corners renders white rectangular blocks outside the CSS rounded corners when the window loses focus. This appears to be DWM rendering an inactive frame decoration over the transparent areas.

## Environment

- Electron 35.0.0
- Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- Node.js 24.14.1

## BrowserWindow options

```js
new BrowserWindow({
  frame: false,
  titleBarStyle: 'hidden',
  transparent: true,
  thickFrame: false,
  roundedCorners: false,
  backgroundMaterial: 'none',
  backgroundColor: '#00000000',
})
```

## What I've tried

1. **`setShape()`** — Prevents the white corners, but the rectangle-approximated rounded shape has visible aliasing/jagged edges. No `{ rect, radius }` format supported (TypeError).

2. **`DwmSetWindowAttribute` with `DWMWA_NCRENDERING_POLICY = DWMNCRP_DISABLED`** — Called via PowerShell P/Invoke before window shows. No HRESULT error, but white corners still appear on focus loss.

3. **`DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR = DWMWA_COLOR_NONE`** — Same result, no effect.

4. **`DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea` with `MARGINS = {-1,-1,-1,-1}`** — Same result, no effect.

5. **`show: false` + apply DWM fixes before `window.show()`** — Attempted to set DWM attributes before DWM's first render. Still no effect.

6. **Re-applying DWM fixes on `focus`/`blur` events** — No effect.

## Expected behavior

The white inactive-frame corners should not appear when the window loses focus, allowing CSS `clipPath`/`border-radius` to provide smooth rounded corners without `setShape()`.

## Question

Is there a way to prevent DWM from rendering the inactive frame on transparent frameless windows? Or is `setShape()` the only option, and if so, is there a plan to support rounded corner shapes (e.g. `{ rect, radius }` format)?

author: gdavidkov
title: [Breaking Change] 41.3 + 42: frameless+thickFrame HWND grows 16×8 DIP, no longer matches getBounds()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (verified on 10.0.22631 and 10.0.26200)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

For `BrowserWindow({ frame: false, thickFrame: true, resizable: true })` on Windows, the on-screen HWND rect (read via `user32!GetWindowRect`) equals `screen.dipToScreenRect(win.getBounds())`. `setBounds({ x, y, width: W, height: H })` produces a visible window of `W × H` DIP at `(x, y)`. This held through Electron `41.3.0`.

### Actual Behavior

Starting in `42.0.0`, the HWND extends outward from `getBounds()` by `SM_CXSIZEFRAME + SM_CXPADDEDBORDER` DIP on **left, right, and bottom**, and by `0` on **top**. `setBounds({ x, y, width: W, height: H })` produces a visible window of `(W + 16) × (H + 8)` DIP at `(x - 8, y)` at 100% DPI (scales with DPI). `getBounds()`, `getNormalBounds()`, and `getContentBounds()` continue to return the original logical (inset-subtracted) rect, so the `getBounds() ↔ HWND` identity is broken on this window class. No constructor option, runtime flag, or JS API to query the inset or restore 41 behavior.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/gdavidkov/c8c466109c009ff195f1abdcb68362a9

### Additional Information

### How the break looks in numbers

Same `BrowserWindow` options, same display, **measured locally** with the repro at the bottom of this issue:

| Observation | Electron 41.2.0 (last working) | Electron 41.3.0 / 42.1.0 (same input) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asymmetricInsetPhysical` @ 100% DPI | `{0, 0, 0, 0}` | `{left:8, top:0, right:8, bottom:8}` | new inset |
| `asymmetricInsetPhysical` @ 137.5% DPI | `{0, 0, 0, 0}` | `{left:12, top:0, right:12, bottom:11}` | new inset (scales with DPI) |
| Visible window width for `setBounds(w:500)` | 500 DIP | 516 DIP | **+16 DIP** |
| Visible window height for `setBounds(h:400)` | 400 DIP | 408 DIP | **+8 DIP** |
| `getBounds()` vs HWND rect | identical | HWND = bounds outset by `TLBR(0, T, T, T)` | identity broken |
| Center of `getBounds()` vs HWND center on Y | identical | logical center is `T/2` above HWND center | **−4 DIP** |
| `setBounds(display.workArea)` fills `workArea` | yes | overflows `workArea` by `T` DIP on L / R / B | window leaves work area |

### Source of the change

Introduced by **#50706** *"fix: external resize hit targets for frameless windows on Windows"* (shipped as #50864), with follow-up regression fix in **#51252 / #51296**. The relevant code in [`shell/browser/ui/views/win_frame_view.cc@v42.1.0`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.1.0/shell/browser/ui/views/win_frame_view.cc):

```cpp
gfx::Insets WinFrameView::RestoredFrameBorderInsets() const {
  if (window_->has_frame() || !window_->has_thick_frame() ||
      !window_->IsResizable())
    return {};

  const int thickness =
      display::win::GetScreenWin()->GetSystemMetricsInDIP(SM_CXSIZEFRAME) +
      display::win::GetScreenWin()->GetSystemMetricsInDIP(SM_CXPADDEDBORDER);
  return gfx::Insets::TLBR(0, thickness, thickness, thickness);
}
```

### Related

- [#40505](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/40505) — original Win11 frameless-resize bug
- [#50706](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50706) — the fix on `main`
- [#50863](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50863) — backport to `41-x-y` (shipped in `41.3.0`)
- [#50864](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50864) — backport to `42-x-y` (shipped in `42.0.0`)
- [#51244](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51244) — regression introduced by #50706
- [#51252](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51252) — regression fix on `main`
- [#51296](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51296) — regression-fix backport
- [#51287](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51287) — `fix: remove insets on fullscreen windows on Windows` (related follow-up)

### Electron Version

40.10.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Since the overlay is visually transparent and passes mouse events through, the underlying window is both visible and interactive. Its document.visibilityState should stay 'visible', no background throttling should apply, and clicks/animations should remain fully responsive.

### Actual Behavior

The underlying window's document.visibilityState becomes 'hidden' as soon as the transparent overlay covers it. Background throttling activates. Clicks (delivered through the overlay's pass-through) reach the main window but respond with noticeable latency; animations stutter.
Briefly dragging the underlying window restores 'visible', but it returns to 'hidden' once the drag ends and the overlay covers it again.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When a transparent: true BrowserWindow with mouse events set to pass through (setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)) is positioned on top of another BrowserWindow on macOS Sequoia, the underlying window's document.visibilityState flips to 'hidden' and background throttling kicks in — even though the underlying content is fully visible and interactive to the user through the overlay. 

Affected versions

Electron: 40.9.0 and later. Confirmed in 40.10.0, 41 . Confirmed not present in 40.8.5.
macOS: 15.x (Sequoia). Not reproducible on macOS 26.

Related PRs

#50579 — the change after which this regression appears. Fixes #45776 (a different occlusion scenario — windows created hidden and shown later) and incidentally removes the previous global disable that had been masking this bug.
#50712, #50713, #50715 — backports of #50579 to 42-x-y / 40-x-y / 41-x-y release branches.

author: gesou
title: Windows: resize hit-test area extends into client area with titleBarStyle "hidden"
body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 21h2-25h2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior The native resize hit-test area should be limited to the actual outer edge of the window. When `titleBarStyle` is changed from `"default"` to `"hidden"`, the resize border should not move inward into the visible client/content area. A pointer position that is treated as normal client content with `titleBarStyle: "default"` should remain normal client content with `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` if it is visually inside the window and not on the outer border. ### Actual Behavior With `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` on Windows, the native resize hit-test area extends into the visible client/content area. The mouse cursor changes to a horizontal resize cursor while the pointer is still visually inside the application window, not on the actual outer border. The same visual pointer position does not trigger resize behavior when using `titleBarStyle: "default"`. This happens without any custom CSS drag regions or custom titlebar implementation, so the issue appears to be in Electron's Windows native hit-testing / non-client area calculation for hidden-titlebar windows. ### `titleBarStyle: "default"` The cursor remains a normal pointer while it is visually inside the client/content area. ### `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` At approximately the same visual position, the cursor becomes a horizontal resize cursor while still visually inside the client/content area. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information I attached screenshots comparing `titleBarStyle: "default"` and `titleBarStyle: "hidden"`. The issue is visible without interacting with any DOM element: the cursor changes to the native horizontal resize cursor while it is still visually inside the application window.
