- If async encryption truly isn't available, calling `encryptStringAsync` / `decryptStringAsync` should reject the returned promise not crash the process.


### Actual Behavior


- `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` returns `false` from a minimal repro
- Calling `encryptStringAsync()` SIGSEGVs the process with the V8 HandleScope error above.

Notably, the same `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` call returns `true` in a larger codebase on the same machine and Electron build.

```js
// safeStorageTest.js
import { app, safeStorage } from 'electron'

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  console.log({
    isEncryptionAvailable: safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable(),
    isAsyncEncryptionAvailable: await safeStorage.isAsyncEncryptionAvailable(),
  })
  // Crashes with V8 HandleScope error:
  await safeStorage.encryptStringAsync('secret')
  app.quit()
})
```

Run with `npx electron safeStorageTest.js`.

Output:

```
{ isEncryptionAvailable: true, isAsyncEncryptionAvailable: false }
[ERROR:electron/shell/common/node_bindings.cc:171] Fatal error in V8:
  v8::HandleScope::CreateHandle() Cannot create a handle without a HandleScope
Electron exited with signal SIGSEGV
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Notably, the same `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` call returns `true` in another codebase on the same machine using the same Electron build. I've tried the steps below to make the repro above work:

- Calling `safeStorage.encryptString(...)` (sync) first (works fine, but async still reports unavailable)
- Creating a hidden `new BrowserWindow({ show: false })` before the probe
- Setting `app.setName('Test')` before `whenReady`

A workaround that **does work** is an arbitrary 2 second delay. So this seems to be an initialization issue.

author: moonyoulove
title: [Bug] Electron apps crash with exit_code=-2147483645 (GPU process sandbox crash) when zombie SIDs exist in DACL
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should launch normally even if the directory contains unparseable or orphaned zombie SIDs, or gracefully handle the permission validation error without crashing the entire GPU process.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process crashes on startup with exit_code=-2147483645 and outputs "FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc: GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye."

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**TL;DR:** Electron apps crash with exit_code=-2147483645 because the folder's DACL contains orphaned zombie SIDs (S-1-15...). Granting permissions to `S-1-15-2-2` (ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES) or running `icacls /reset` fixes the crash. This is closely related to the LPAC sandbox requirement discussed in #49143.

## Description

Recently, on my Windows PC, many Electron-based desktop applications (such as Discord, Bitwarden, LM Studio, Postman, VS Code, etc.) crash frequently, making them completely unusable. The error messages are as follows:

```
[33240:0524/193721.652:ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:999] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[33240:0524/193721.652:FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

After searching online, I found that other users have reported the same error recently:

- liliMozi/openhanako#1083
- anthropics/claude-code#61372
- postmanlabs/postman-app-support#14149

Currently, the only temporary solution is to add the `--disable-gpu-sandbox` parameter at startup. However, this requires doing it manually every time and is not a permanent solution.

## Hypothesis

After repeated troubleshooting and verification with AI, we ruled out hardware and driver issues. (During this time, I tried reinstalling drivers, reinstalling software, reinstalling Windows, adjusting Core Isolation and HAGS, updating BIOS, etc., but nothing worked.)

Finally, the AI identified the possible cause: an issue with the security permission list (DACL) of the application folder, which contains an unresolvable "zombie SID" (shown as "Unknown Account" in the Windows interface). This conclusion can be consistently reproduced using the following steps.

## Reproduction Steps

Please create a clean Electron project then package, or use an existing Electron application folder directly (the following example uses VS Code with PowerShell):

1. Add a zombie SID to the application folder:

```PowerShell
icacls "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code" /grant "*S-1-15-2-999-999-999:(OI)(CI)(F)"
```

2. Run the application:

```PowerShell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe" --verbose
```

**Expected Result**: The application will crash immediately during GPU initialization and output the following error logs:

```
[37568:0524/201836.841:ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:999] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[37568:0524/201836.841:FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

3. Run the following command to reset permissions and remove the zombie SID. After that, the application will work normally again:

```PowerShell
icacls "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code" /reset
```

## Additional Context

Before submitting this issue, I researched related past reports and noticed:

* #49143

It mentions that enabling the network sandbox in newer versions might cause permission issues, requiring the following command to grant permissions:

```PowerShell
icacls <install dir> /grant *S-1-15-2-2:(OI)(CI)(RX)
```

Following this clue, I did a cross-test and made a new discovery: if both the unknown zombie SID and the `S-1-15-2-2` permission exist at the same time, the application can start successfully without crashing.

author: ElRochito
title: [Bug] Helper app lookup uses hardcoded "Electron Helper" name — fatal crash when app is renamed by packager (macOS 26, arm64)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — not yet tested on macOS 15 or earlier. The issue may be specific to macOS 26.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

A packaged Electron app whose product name differs from "Electron" (i.e. every real-world app) should launch correctly on macOS 26 arm64.

The helper app path should be resolved at runtime using the main bundle's name — for example, by reading `CFBundleName` from `Info.plist` — so that standard packager behavior (renaming `Electron Helper.app` to `MyApp Helper.app`) works without requiring binary patching.


### Actual Behavior


The app crashes immediately on launch with exit code **133 (SIGTRAP)** and no output.

Running the binary directly from the terminal reveals the fatal error:

```
[FATAL:electron/shell/app/electron_main_delegate_mac.mm:66] Unable to find helper app
```

The Electron binary appears to resolve its helper processes using a name fixed at compile time (`Electron Helper`) rather than derived at runtime from the app bundle's `CFBundleName`. When a packager renames the helper bundles to match the product name (standard practice), the binary can no longer find them.

This was confirmed by the following test:

```bash
# Start from the unmodified node_modules Electron.app
cp -R node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app /tmp/TestApp.app

# Simulate what electron-builder does: rename helpers
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper.app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper.app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (GPU).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (GPU).app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (Plugin).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (Plugin).app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (Renderer).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (Renderer).app"

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /tmp/TestApp.app

/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
# → [FATAL] Unable to find helper app  (exit 133)
```

Restoring helpers to their original `Electron Helper*.app` names makes the app launch correctly.

Additionally, the packaged binary is **byte-for-byte identical** to the original from the npm package (same SHA-256 hash), confirming it was never patched:

```bash
shasum -a 256 "dist/mac-arm64/MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp"
# c86c2701f15ca66ba460f4cdcd7ebcab0b5133a4cc299295f02108b3754e9eed

shasum -a 256 "node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron"
# c86c2701f15ca66ba460f4cdcd7ebcab0b5133a4cc299295f02108b3754e9eed
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/ElRochito/f251a4231213679f31a6c97d5b8ab625

### Additional Information


**Workaround** (in electron-builder): add an `afterPack` hook that renames the helpers back to their original `Electron Helper*.app` names after packaging. See companion issue filed against [electron-builder](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder).

**What did NOT help:**
- Setting `hardenedRuntime: false` in electron-builder config
- Setting `identity: null` to skip code signing
- Removing the quarantine attribute (`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`)
- Re-signing the bundle with `codesign --force --deep -s -`
- All FUSE flags are identical between working and failing binaries (`EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` is disabled in both)

**Suggested fix:** In `electron/shell/app/electron_main_delegate_mac.mm` around line 66, derive the helper name from `[NSBundle.mainBundle objectForInfoDictionaryKey:@"CFBundleName"]` at runtime rather than using a compile-time constant, e.g.:

```objc
NSString *bundleName = [NSBundle.mainBundle objectForInfoDictionaryKey:@"CFBundleName"];
NSString *helperName = [NSString stringWithFormat:@"%@ Helper", bundleName];
```

This would make the helper resolution robust to any product name without requiring binary patching.

author: Classic298
title: Child processes crash at launch in base::i18n::InitializeICUFromDataFile (ICU init CHECK fails), exit 0x80000003, Windows 11 26200
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.8.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200.8457)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown / not bisected

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron child processes (GPU, renderer, utility) initialize and the app launches normally, as it does for Chromium/Chrome and for older-Electron apps on the same machine.

### Actual Behavior

On this machine, every Electron child process aborts at the very first step of startup — before GPU init, sandbox lockdown, or logging — inside ICU initialization. The browser process is fine; only child processes die.

Symbolized stack (cdb / WinDbg, child-process following, Electron's public symbol server, exact electron.exe.pdb match):

    electron!base::i18n::InitializeICUFromDataFile     <- CHECK fails
    electron!base::i18n::InitializeICU
    electron!content::ContentMainRunnerImpl::Initialize
    electron!content::RunContentProcess
    electron!content::ContentMain
    electron!wWinMain

So `CHECK(InitializeICU())` trips -> base::ImmediateCrash -> the child exits 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT). The app's own log (no debugger) confirms the same code:

    child-process-gone { type: 'GPU', reason: 'crashed', exitCode: -2147483645 }   // = 0x80000003

Because the abort is this early, the child writes no log and no crash dump. The browser only sees the child vanish, counts it as a GPU crash, exhausts GPU fallback modes, and aborts via content::IntentionallyCrashBrowserForUnusableGpuProcess ("GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye."). That is why it superficially looks like a GPU problem, but the GPU is never reached.

Result: the app shows a blank window or quits on launch. Reproduces with multiple Electron 40 apps (Proton Mail 1.13.0 = Electron 40.8.5; GitHub Desktop 3.5.10 shows the identical instant-vanish, no-dump fingerprint).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This needs no special app code to reproduce — any recent-Electron app crashes the same way on this machine, so a Fiddle would just be a default app. Happy to produce one if useful.

Evidence it is ICU init, not the GPU/driver:
- icudtl.dat is present and valid (10,822,192 bytes, correct ICU header) and the **browser** process loads that same file fine; only **child** processes fail.
- dxdiag: AMD RX 7900 XTX healthy, Direct3D feature level 12_2.
- Ruled out: HVCI off; all Exploit Protection / process mitigations NOTSET (MicrosoftSignedOnly, ProhibitDynamicCode, DisallowWin32k, etc.); no AppInit_DLLs / AppCertDlls; no AV/EDR/anti-cheat; clean DDU + several AMD driver versions; a full clean Windows reinstall.
- Scope: Chrome/Brave (Chromium) and an older-Electron app (Signal) are unaffected on this exact machine; only recent Electron (40.x) fails. So the failure is specific to Electron's child-process ICU initialization on this Windows build (26200), not core Chromium.

Versions: Electron 40.8.5, Chromium 144.0.7559.236, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 build 26200.8457, x64, AMD RX 7900 XTX driver 32.0.31007.5012.

Method caveat: the symbolized stack was captured under a debugger, but it matches the non-debugger exit code (0x80000003) and the pre-logging/pre-dump behaviour exactly, so it is the real fault.

Originally surfaced as Chromium issue 516312113 (filed under a GPU/AMD-driver premise that turned out to be a red herring). Crash logs, full symbolized stack, dxdiag, and a symbol-matched dump available on request.

author: MarshallOfSound
title: macos-arm64 BrowserWindow tests time out on main (since 2026-05-24)
body:
## Summary
Every `macos-arm64 / test` job (darwin + mas) has been failing on `main` since 2026-05-24. ~30 `BrowserWindow` window-management tests in `spec/api-browser-window-spec.ts` fail, all with `Timeout of 30000ms exceeded` (×3 retries): show/hide, focus/blur/z-order, minimize/maximize bounds, `visibilityState`, content protection, capturePage. The expected window event never fires — this looks like a broken window-server session in the runner, not a logic bug.

## When it started
- ✅ green — `chore: bump chromium to 150.0.7849.0 (#51733)`, run `26301533643` (05-22)
- ❌ red — `ci: unpin homebrew version (#51757)`, run `26368726651` (05-24)

## Likely cause
Two things changed between those runs:

| | green | red |
|---|---|---|
| runner image | `macos-15-arm64/20260427` | `macos-15-arm64/20260520` |
| macOS | 15.7.4 | 15.7.7 |
| Homebrew pin | present | removed (#51757) |

The **macOS 15.7.4 → 15.7.7 runner-image bump** is the likely trigger (window-server / screen-recording TCC / modal-dialog behavior). The Homebrew unpin is probably *not* the cause: the test job runs prebuilt artifacts and never invokes `brew` for anything GUI-related.

author: wehos
title: [Wayland] setIgnoreMouseEvents input region not applied without a frame submission (follow-up to #51769)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`BrowserWindow.setIgnoreMouseEvents()` on **native Wayland** applies asynchronously and unreliably. Even after the API call returns and the JS-side state flips, the Wayland compositor may continue delivering pointer events to the surface for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds — and in some sequences it never applies at all until an unrelated event happens. This is the underlying problem #51769 worked around with `compositor()->ScheduleFullRedraw()`, but that workaround is not sufficient in two reproducible cases:

1. **Race during the "passthrough turning on" window.** If the user (or any pointer event) hits the surface in the gap between `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` returning and the input region actually committing, the surface gets "stuck" in non-passthrough — the new region never lands.
2. **`setIgnoreMouseEvents(false)` while focused.** On a focused, idle, transparent overlay (frame:false, transparent:true), turning passthrough OFF often does nothing — the prior empty input region stays committed indefinitely until some other event jolts the compositor.

Root cause is upstream Chromium behavior, **not** Electron-side, and exists in current `main` (verified against `chromium/main` at the time of filing). See the linked Chromium issue.

### Proposed Solution

Once the linked Chromium issue is resolved, Electron inherits the fix automatically. In the meantime, two interim options for Electron to consider:

1. **Cherry-pick / carry a Chromium patch** in `patches/chromium/` that either (a) exposes `CommitNow()` on `WaylandToplevelExtension`, or (b) makes `WaylandSurface::set_input_region` flush directly when `apply_state_immediately_` is false. Either makes `setIgnoreMouseEvents` (and any other path that touches the input region without a frame cycle) work reliably without waiting on a buffer commit.
2. **No-op damage trick** at the Electron layer: after `UpdateFrameHints()` in `ElectronDesktopWindowTreeHostLinux::SetIgnoreMouseEvents`, mark a 1-pixel damage region on the compositor's root layer to force the next frame to actually submit. Less invasive but hacky.

### Alternatives Considered

- The current `compositor()->ScheduleFullRedraw()` in #51769. Helps the common case (idle overlay, ~1.3 s → near-instant under load) but does **not** fix the two cases above because Chromium can still skip submitting a frame if the surface content is visually unchanged.
- Polling `setShape()` (the original N.E.K.O. workaround). Works but is a per-frame timer-driven hack.
- Switching to X11 / XWayland. Not acceptable for native-Wayland use cases.

### Additional Information

**Context:** Originally surfaced as a follow-up to #51769 ("fix: implement setIgnoreMouseEvents on Wayland"). The PR itself works correctly; this issue is about the residual unreliability that #51769 cannot fully address inside Electron alone.

**Root-cause analysis** (Chromium 150.0.7849.0, verified identical in `chromium/src` `main`):

- `ui/ozone/platform/wayland/host/wayland_surface.cc` `WaylandSurface::set_input_region()` only forwards directly to `wl_surface_set_input_region` when `apply_state_immediately_` is `true`. Otherwise it stores the region in `pending_state_` and waits for `ApplyPendingState()` to be called.
- `apply_state_immediately_` is only ever set to `true` from one place: `ui/ozone/platform/wayland/gpu/gl_surface_wayland.cc` — i.e., only the GL-surface path.
- `ApplyPendingState()` is invoked solely from `WaylandFrameManager` on frame submission. With no GL surface and no visual change, the compositor (or Chromium itself) may skip the frame and the input region change never lands.
- `compositor()->ScheduleFullRedraw()` schedules a paint but does not guarantee a buffer commit; if the surface is visually identical to the prior frame, the request is effectively dropped.

**Repro environment used to verify:**

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel `6.17.0-1013-azure` |
| Desktop | GNOME Shell 46.0, Mutter, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=ubuntu:GNOME` |
| Session | Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`) |
| Electron | `44.0.0-nightly.20260525` built from #51769 |
| Chromium | 150.0.7849.0 |
| GPU | None (Azure VM, `drmGetDevices2()` returns no devices, software rendering) — exposes the underlying race on the non-GL path |
| Repro app | Frameless transparent `BrowserWindow` (`frame: false, transparent: true, alwaysOnTop: true`) toggling `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` |
| Launch | `--no-sandbox --ozone-platform=wayland` |

**Linked Chromium issue:** _(to be added once filed — the Chromium tracker doesn't have a CLI, so it'll be posted manually shortly after this issue.)_

**Linked PR:** #51769

---

_Investigation and writeup assisted by Claude (Anthropic), reviewed and posted by [@wehos](https://github.com/wehos)._

42.3.0

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 23H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

NAN should handle the v8::External API change in V8 13.x, as it has
handled previous V8 API changes, so addons using NAN compile against
Electron 42 / Node 24 without modification.

### Actual Behavior

## Description
Building any NAN-based native addon against Electron 42 (V8 13.x) headers 
fails due to breaking changes in `v8::External` API:

- `v8::External::Value()` now requires a `v8::Isolate*` parameter
- `v8::External::New()` signature changed

The errors originate inside NAN's own files:
- `nan_callbacks_12_inl.h`
- `nan_implementation_12_inl.h`

## Error Output
```
nan_callbacks_12_inl.h(213,46): error C2660:
'v8::External::Value': function does not take 0 arguments
nan_implementation_12_inl.h(79,24): error C2660:
'v8::External::New': function does not take 2 arguments
```


## Minimal Reproduction

**binding.gyp**
```json
{
  "targets": [{
    "target_name": "hello",
    "sources": [ "hello.cc" ],
    "include_dirs": [ "<!(node -e \"require('nan')\")" ]
  }]
}
```

**hello.cc**
```cpp
#include <nan.h>

NAN_METHOD(Hello) {
    info.GetReturnValue().Set(
        Nan::New("hello world").ToLocalChecked()
    );
}

NAN_MODULE_INIT(Init) {
    NAN_EXPORT(target, Hello);
}

NODE_MODULE(hello, Init)
```

**package.json**
```json
{
  "name": "nan-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "nan": "2.27.0" },
  "scripts": { "build": "node-gyp rebuild" }
}
```

**Steps to reproduce:**

```bash
npm install
# Download Electron 42 headers
npx node-gyp rebuild --target=42.3.0 --dist-url=https://electronjs.org/headers
```

title: Dirent.parentPath is missing from fs.glob/globSync withFileTypes under asar
body:
### Preflight Checklist

### Electron Version

42.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Ventura 13.5 (arm64), Windows 11 25H2 (x64)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`fs.glob` or `fs.globSync` with `options.withFileTypes` expect to return `fs.Dirent[]` under asar packaged or not. And the `fs.Dirent` should include a `parentPath` property.

```ts
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })
/*
[
  Dirent {
    name: 'index.js',
    parentPath: '/path/to/project/dist',
    Symbol(type): 1
  }
]
*/
```

### Actual Behavior

`Dirent.parentPath` property is existing under dev runtime `npx electron .` or build `asar: false`, but it's missing under asar packaged.

```ts
// under asar packaged app
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { dialog } from 'electron'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })

// Use showErrorBox to print value after build app.
dialog.showErrorBox('', JSON.stringify(direntList, null, 2))
/*
[
  {
    "name": "index.js"
    // parentPath is missing
  }
]
*/
```

Dirent.parentPath is a relatively new property. It's marked stable in node.js `v24.0.0` and `v22.17.0`. Maybe hasn't been implemented yet in electron asar mode.
https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#direntparentpath

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The following steps can be used to reproduce the result. Using node.js `v24.15.0` same with electron's node.js version.

1. Create a new npm project directory and enter it
```bash
$ mkdir electron-test
$ cd electron-test
$ npm init --y
```

2. Install dependencies
```bash
$ npm install -D electron@42.2.0 electron-builder@26.8.1
```

3. Edit electron-builder config in package.json
```jsonc
// package.json
{
  // ...
  // add the following
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "type": "module",
  "build": {
    "appId": "some.app.id",
    "compression": "store",
    "asar": true,
    "directories": {
      "output": "release"
    }
  }
}
```

4. Add `dist/index.js`
```js
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { app, dialog } from 'electron'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })

// print value
console.log(direntList)
dialog.showErrorBox('', JSON.stringify(direntList, null, 2))

app.exit()
```

5. Run `npx electron .` the Dirent.parentPath exists
6. Run `npx electron-builder` to build app with asar
7. Click to launch the packaged app, we can see the `Dirent.parentPath` is missing in the dialog

author: RossSmyth
title: Distro Packaging and `process.argv` (and others)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Packaging Electron applications in distros is a bit weird. We want the packages to be as close to the experience of it being from the upstream application repo as possible, while also getting regular security updates.

The way that distos (Arch and Nixpkgs at least) generally do this is the following:
1. Package supported Electron versions
2. Package the application `resources` directory (primarily the `.asar`, but also sometimes other files)
3. Add a wrapper than does something like `/bin/electron41 /share/CoolElectronApplication/resources/app.asar`

This works decently well. It decouples the Electron from the application so it can be updated separately. But there are a few snags.

* Doing this naively, Electron considers itself "unpackaged" and so `app.isPackaged` is false

This primarily results in logging being output by applications. Disto wrapping solves this with the magic `ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED`. Set this to true, and now `app.isPackaged` returns true. 

Great! Now dev logging isn't output. But at what cost? This does break applications, subtlety. This breaks `process.argv`. The only thing the above environment variable changes is the output of `app.isPackaged` outputting true. It does not change the order of `process.argv` to be the "packaged" format. This is NOT changed if `app.isPackaged` returns true, but when `app.getPath('exe')` returns something that isn't `electron`. 

A common pattern in applications is doing something like:
```js
  if (app.isPackaged) {
    process.argv.unshift(null)
  }
```
or something similar (`process.argv.slice(app.isPackaged ? 1 : 2)` is also common). When `ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED` is set, this is incorrect! The format is not the "packaged" argv, so CLI arguments become incorrect. 

We noticed this in Nixpkgs, and attempted to work around it with a shim that attempts to setup all the paths correctly.
https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/487711#issuecomment-4594210912

This almost works! `process.argv` is correct, `app.getPath('exe')` is correct, `app.isPackaged` is true, and `resourcesPath` is correct. Testing this shim, what fails is `app.relaunch`. 
https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat.Electron/blob/3c89e81c7bc41ba742178d3f84070817e6e05f25/src/app/main/app.ts#L85

Unfortunate. I tried some other solution, like making a symlink of `Electron` to see if that changed the way it considers itself "packaged," but it does not. So we are pack to the original status quo. This *mostly* works because most Electron apps don't take CLI args, so breakage is not common. 

### Proposed Solution

Some way to tell Electron "hey this is packaged!" without needing to jump thru hoops with an imperfect shim that lies to Electron about what's running, and duplicates Electron logic. I do not know exactly what. I know users want:

1. The application name to appear in `top` (this currently does not happen)
2. Dev logging not to output
3. Don't bloat package size (aka don't copy Electron into every every Electron application)

And then use distro maintainers would like:

1. Something low maintenance (not duplicating Electron processing logic)

### Alternatives Considered

Status-quo. Currently things work *fine*. Not perfect, but fine. 

### Additional Information

https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/electron42/-/blob/main/electron-launcher.sh

Nixpkg's wrapper (they are currently ad-hoc, trying to fix that) look something like:
```bash
export ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED=1
exec /nix/store/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-electron/bin/electron /nix/store/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa1-application/share/resources/application/resources/app.asar "$@"
```

author: shrinktofit
title: Removing a shadow-hosted iframe with nodeIntegrationInSubFrames can throw "illegal access" when setImmediate is pending
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched for an existing issue that matches this behavior.
- [x] I have included a minimal reproduction repository.

### Electron Version

39.1.0

### What operating system are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

Removing a DOM node that hosts an iframe in its shadow root should not throw synchronously. In the reproduction, `document.body.removeChild(host)` should succeed regardless of whether a `setImmediate` callback is pending in the parent renderer.

### Actual Behavior

When `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` is enabled and the iframe has loaded with Node/Electron runtime available, removing the shadow host while a `setImmediate` callback is pending throws:

```text
removeChild threw: illegal access
```

The same DOM removal succeeds when `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` is disabled.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/shrinktofit/electron-iframe-repro

### Additional Information

The minimal trigger appears to be:

1. Create a `BrowserWindow` with `nodeIntegration: true`, `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: true`, `contextIsolation: false`, and `sandbox: false`.
2. In the main frame, create a host element and attach an open shadow root.
3. Append an iframe inside that shadow root and load a local HTML file that uses `require('electron')`.
4. Wait for the iframe `load` event.
5. Queue a parent-frame `setImmediate(() => {})` callback.
6. Immediately call `document.body.removeChild(host)`.

Observed comparison from the repro:

- With `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: true`: iframe reports `require=function`, and `removeChild` throws `illegal access`.
- With `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false`: iframe reports `require=undefined`, and `removeChild` succeeds.

A pending `setTimeout(..., 0)` or Promise microtask did not reproduce the exception in the same test shape; the failure seems specific to pending `setImmediate` while detaching a node-enabled subframe hosted inside shadow DOM.

author: thiagomsoares
title: [Bug]: Buffer.byteLength/Buffer.from compute wrong UTF-8 size for large strings with non-ASCII chars; fs.writeFileSync aborts
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon (M1 Max)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — standalone Node 24.10.0 (V8 13.6) behaves correctly, so this looks like a regression in the V8 shipped with Electron 42 (14.8.178.28-electron.0).

### Expected Behavior

`Buffer.byteLength(s, 'utf8')` returns the correct UTF-8 byte count, `Buffer.from(s, 'utf8')` round-trips, and `fs.writeFileSync(path, s, 'utf-8')` writes the file.

### Actual Behavior

For large strings containing a non-ASCII character, the UTF-8 size is computed wrong, `Buffer.from` silently produces a truncated/corrupted buffer, and `fs.writeFileSync` hard-aborts the whole process with an uncatchable C++ CHECK:

```
Assertion failed: (length + 1) <= (capacity())
void node::MaybeStackBuffer<char>::SetLengthAndZeroTerminate(size_t) [T = char, kStackStorageSize = 1024]
  at ../../third_party/electron_node/src/util.h:454
```

Repro (run with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, also reproduces in the main process):

```js
const s = 'a'.repeat(200000) + 'ç' + 'a'.repeat(199999)

console.log(s.length)                      // 400000
console.log(Buffer.byteLength(s, 'utf8'))  // 399999 — wrong, should be 400001

const b = Buffer.from(s, 'utf8')           // 399999 bytes, silently corrupted
console.log(b.toString('utf8') === s)      // false (round-trips to length 399998)

require('fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/x', s, 'utf-8')  // aborts the process (SIGTRAP)
```

On Electron 42.3.2 (Node 24.15.0, V8 14.8.178.28-electron.0) all three are broken as above. On standalone Node 24.10.0 (V8 13.6.233.10-node.28) all three behave correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I hit this in production: my app persists a JSON stats file that had grown to ~600 KB and contained a couple of `ç`/`ã` characters. Every save aborted the main process a few seconds after launch (uncatchable CHECK), which is how I found it.

A few data points from bisecting:

- Pure-ASCII strings of any size are fine; at least one non-ASCII char is needed.
- A non-ASCII char within the last few code units of the string does not trigger it.
- The length dependence is non-monotonic, which suggests sensitivity to the string's internal representation rather than plain size — with a single `ç` in the middle: len 131072 OK, 200000 crash, 262144 OK, 262146 crash, 300000 OK, 400000 crash.
- It also reproduces with a flat string read via `fs.readFileSync` (not only concatenated/cons strings).

The silent `Buffer.from` corruption seems worse than the abort — anything encoding large user strings to UTF-8 can write truncated data with no error at all.

author: jerem
title: [Bug]: globalShortcut on Wayland never calls the host `Registry.Register` portal handshake, so `register()` fails on xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.20 (GNOME 50)
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [x] I have searched for existing issues. Closest are #49873, #48391, #45607, #49806 — all closed/fixed and present in the versions tested below; none cover the `Registry.Register` requirement. ### Electron Version(s) Reproduced on **40.6.1, 41.5.0, 41.7.1, and 42.3.3** (latest). All identical. ### What operating system(s) are you using? Linux (Fedora 44, Wayland) ### Operating System Version Fedora 44 Workstation, GNOME Shell 50.2, **xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.2**, xdg-desktop-portal-gnome 50.0 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown on this portal version. The related accelerator/app-id fixes (#49988 → backported to `41-x-y` via #50051) are present in all versions tested here, but do not resolve this. ### Expected Behavior With `--enable-features=GlobalShortcutsPortal` and `--ozone-platform=wayland`, `globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Space', cb)` should register a global shortcut via the XDG GlobalShortcuts portal and fire `cb` regardless of which window is focused. ### Actual Behavior `globalShortcut.register(...)` returns **`false`** and `isRegistered(...)` is **`false`**. A full session-bus trace shows the renderer **never contacts `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts`** (no `CreateSession`, no `BindShortcuts`) and **never calls `org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry.Register`**. The shortcut effectively degrades to focus-bound. Toggling the feature on/off makes **no difference** on Wayland; the same MRE returns `true` on `--ozone-platform=x11`: | ozone backend | `GlobalShortcutsPortal` flag | `register()` | portal `CreateSession` calls | |---|---|---|---| | wayland | enabled | `false` | 0 | | wayland | default (no flag) | `false` | 0 | | wayland | disabled | `false` | 0 | | x11 (XWayland) | enabled | `true` | 0 (X11 grab) | ### Root cause (diagnosed) xdg-desktop-portal **1.20+** requires a non-sandboxed ("host") app to declare its identity by calling **`org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry.Register(app_id, options)`** before app-id-gated portals will serve it. Chromium's `GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux` still relies on the legacy systemd-scope app-id derivation: in a bus trace it creates `app-electron-.scope` but never calls `Registry.Register`. On xdg-desktop-portal 1.21 the legacy path no longer yields an app id for host apps, so: ``` $ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop \ --object-path /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop \ --method org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts.CreateSession "{...}" Error: org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed: An app id is required ``` **Proof the portal itself is fully functional** — a minimal Python client that performs the missing `Registry.Register` call (with a reverse-DNS app id backed by a `.desktop` file) drives the whole flow successfully and receives `Activated` from an unfocused window: ``` Registry.Register('com.example.GsPortalProof') OK CreateSession OK -> .../session/1_7016/session1 BindShortcuts OK -> id='open-quick-entry' trigger='Press space' *** ACTIVATED *** id='open-quick-entry' (press #1) *** ACTIVATED *** id='open-quick-entry' (press #2) ``` Secondary note: GNOME's backend additionally rejects app ids that are not reverse-DNS and backed by an installed `.desktop` file (`gnome-control-center-global-shortcuts-provider: Discarded shortcut bind request from application with an invalid app_id >gsportalproof<`). Electron's default app id (the executable name, e.g. `electron`) would likely also fail this even once `Registry.Register` is wired up — so both the `Registry.Register` handshake **and** a valid `.desktop`-backed reverse-DNS app id are needed. ### Testcase **Electron MRE** (`register()` returns `false`): ```js const { app, globalShortcut, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { new BrowserWindow({ width: 320, height: 120 }); const acc = 'CommandOrControl+Alt+Space'; const ok = globalShortcut.register(acc, () => console.log('FIRED')); console.log('register returned', ok, 'isRegistered', globalShortcut.isRegistered(acc)); }); // run: electron --ozone-platform=wayland --enable-features=GlobalShortcutsPortal . ```
Python client proving the portal works once Registry.Register is called Run wrapped in a matching systemd app scope + `.desktop` file: ``` # ~/.local/share/applications/com.example.GsPortalProof.desktop with # Name=GS Portal Proof, Exec=python3 .../gs_portal_proof.py systemd-run --user --scope -u app-com.example.GsPortalProof.scope \ python3 gs_portal_proof.py ``` ```python import dbus from dbus.mainloop.glib import DBusGMainLoop from gi.repository import GLib PORTAL, OBJ = "org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop", "/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop" GS = "org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts" REG = "org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry" APP_ID = "com.example.GsPortalProof" DBusGMainLoop(set_as_default=True) bus = dbus.SessionBus() portal = bus.get_object(PORTAL, OBJ) sender = bus.get_unique_name()[1:].replace(".", "_") # THE MISSING STEP: declare the host app id on this connection. dbus.Interface(portal, REG).Register(APP_ID, {}) def req(tok): return f"{OBJ}/request/{sender}/{tok}" def on_created(code, res): sh = res["session_handle"] def on_bound(c, r): print("BindShortcuts code", int(c)) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda c, r: on_bound(c, r), signal_name="Response", dbus_interface="org.freedesktop.portal.Request", path=req("bind1")) shortcuts = dbus.Array([dbus.Struct(("open-quick-entry", dbus.Dictionary( {"description": dbus.String("demo"), "preferred_trigger": dbus.String("CTRL+ALT+space")}, signature="sv")), signature="sa{sv}")], signature="(sa{sv})") dbus.Interface(portal, GS).BindShortcuts(sh, shortcuts, "", {"handle_token": "bind1"}) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda c, r: on_created(int(c), r), signal_name="Response", dbus_interface="org.freedesktop.portal.Request", path=req("create1")) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda *a: print("*** ACTIVATED ***", a[1]), signal_name="Activated", dbus_interface=GS) dbus.Interface(portal, GS).CreateSession( {"handle_token": "create1", "session_handle_token": "sess1"}) GLib.MainLoop().run() ```
### Additional Information - The portal advertises `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` version 1 and `org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry` with `Register(sa{sv})`. - Likely fundamentally a Chromium bug in `ui/base/accelerators/global_accelerator_listener/global_accelerator_listener_linux.cc` (the listener should perform the host `Registry.Register` handshake on xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.20), surfacing through Electron's `globalShortcut`. Happy to file/cross-reference upstream in the Chromium tracker if preferred.

author: olivaresf
title: [Bug]: Notification 'click' never emitted on macOS for banners presented while the app is frontmost
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the contributing guide and searched existing issues: no macOS report of this exists (the post-migration notification regressions on file are Windows-only, e.g. #51147, #51650).

### Electron Version

42.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.1 (any 41.x — the pre-UNUserNotificationCenter backend)

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a notification banner emits `click` on the `Notification` instance regardless of whether the app is frontmost. This was the behavior of the `NSUserNotification` backend, whose delegate fired `didActivateNotification` on `ContentsClicked` independent of focus (and presented foreground notifications via `shouldPresentNotification: YES`).

### Actual Behavior

Since the migration to `UNUserNotificationCenter` (#47817, shipped in 42), a banner presented while the app is frontmost (via `willPresentNotification` → `Banner | List | Sound` in `shell/browser/notifications/mac/notification_center_delegate.mm`) just dismisses when clicked: macOS never invokes `didReceiveNotificationResponse` for it, so `NotificationClicked()` never runs and no `click` is emitted.

Clicking the same notification while the app is backgrounded or minimized works (the normal delivered-notification activation path).

Ruled out: this is not the garbage-collection issue (#16922) — references are retained — and not the unsigned-build case (the app is code-signed and notifications display and emit `show` normally).

### Testcase Gist URL

Not reproducible in Fiddle: since 42, macOS notification events require a code-signed app. Steps with a signed build:

1. On 42.1.0, while the app window is focused, `new Notification({title: 'x'}).show()` (delayed a few seconds behind a timer) with a `click` listener attached and the reference retained.
2. Click the banner → no `click` event.
3. Same steps with the app unfocused or minimized → `click` fires.
4. Same steps on 41.x → `click` fires in all cases.

### Additional Information

We hit this in production (Basecamp Desktop): users reported notification clicks "doing nothing", exactly and only when the window was active. Downgrading to 41.7.1 restored the old behavior, which is our current mitigation.

Reading the 42-x-y delegate code, the dispatch itself looks correct (`UNNotificationDefaultActionIdentifier` → `NotificationClicked()`, identifier lookup intact) — the response callback simply never arrives from macOS for foreground-presented banners. If that's an OS-level contract of `UNUserNotificationCenter`, it would be worth documenting as a breaking change of the migration; if there's a way to opt foreground banners back into response delivery, even better.

🤖 Drafted with AI assistance; the analysis above was verified against the `42-x-y` sources.

### Expected Behavior
Calling `app.dock.bounce('critical')` once while the app is in the background should bounce the dock icon continuously until the app becomes active or the request is cancelled.

The dock icon bounces continuously for ~1 minute, then visibly drops to ~2 bounces per minute even though the app has not been activated and no focus events fire. Other apps have reported related bouncing issues (Signal Desktop #652, Mattermost Desktop #693) but report a complete stop rather than throttling — possibly because they do not restart the bounce on an interval as we do.

author: rconde01
title: EventTarget.dispatchEvent() silently invokes zero listeners in a renderer when it coincides with a Debugger.pause (breakpoint) transition
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2 x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

A `"message"` event dispatched via `EventTarget.dispatchEvent()` should always invoke its registered listeners.

### Actual Behavior

In a renderer with `nodeIntegration: true`, when `dispatchEvent()` is called **from a Node.js `net` socket `'data'` callback** and the call **coincides with the V8 inspector transitioning into a paused state** (a breakpoint being hit, or `Debugger.pause` via DevTools / the DevTools Protocol), `dispatchEvent()`:

- returns `true` (i.e. runs to completion), but
- **invokes none of the registered listeners** — even listeners that are never removed,

while a **plain function call on the very next line still executes**. So the JS thread is not frozen; specifically the *listener-invocation* step inside `dispatchEvent` is skipped.

Observed log (the anomaly always lands immediately after a pause is issued):

```
[main] Debugger.pause #857
[renderer] *** ANOMALY *** msg-17032: dispatchEvent returned notCanceled=true, but EventTarget listeners did NOT run (internal=false, external=false); plain callback ran=true. [message #17032]
```

- `notCanceled=true` — the dispatch algorithm completed normally.
- `internal=false external=false` — neither registered `"message"` listener ran (no `removeEventListener` is ever called; tracked listener count stays at 2).
- `plain callback ran=true` — the direct `onMessage(msg)` call on the next line executed.

This was originally hit in a real app where protobuf messages arriving over a socket were decoded and "dispatched" but the registered handlers never ran — **only while debugging with breakpoints**. It is intermittent: the drop happens only when a `dispatchEvent` call lands on a pause transition (observed anywhere from ~40 to ~860 pauses into a run).


### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/rconde01/electron-intermittent-dispatch-event-bug

### Additional Information

### How to run

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

The app opens a hidden renderer (`nodeIntegration: true`, `contextIsolation: false`) running a `MessageSocket extends EventTarget` pipe **server**; the main process streams length-prefixed messages to it and repeatedly issues `Debugger.pause`/`Debugger.resume` via `webContents.debugger`. For each message the renderer dispatches a `CustomEvent` and also calls a plain callback, then reports an `*** ANOMALY ***` if `dispatchEvent` returned but the listeners didn't run. It exits `0` and prints `REPRODUCED: …` on the first anomaly, or exits `1` after the timeout.

It is timing-sensitive — **if a run times out, run it again** (a clean run does not mean the bug is absent). Tunables are at the top of `main.js`.

## Additional Information

### It is not a V8/Node bug — it requires Blink

A pure-Node control (`node-only/` in the testcase) runs the identical logic — a `net` server, `class … extends EventTarget`, `dispatchEvent` per message — with a Worker thread driving the V8 inspector against the main thread (`inspector.Session.connectToMainThread()` + `Debugger.pause`/`resume`). Run under Electron's own bundled Node via `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` — i.e. **the same V8 build (14.8) as the failing renderer, without Blink** — it does **not** reproduce:

| Configuration | V8 | Real main-thread pauses | Anomalies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Electron renderer (Blink) | 14.8 (Electron 42.3.3) | hit at pause #857 | **reproduces** |
| Pure Node, same V8, no Blink (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`) | 14.8 | ~1,900 across two 5-min runs | **0** |

Node's `EventTarget` invokes listeners as plain JS calls, and a V8 inspector pause suspends the isolate at a safepoint without skipping that invocation. The skip appears specific to **Blink's** DOM event-dispatch path — presumably a guard that refuses to enter a fresh listener callframe while the isolate is transitioning into the inspector-paused state — so `dispatchEvent` returns having invoked no listeners while the already-running caller frame continues.

To run the control:

```sh
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 npx electron node-only/repro.js   # same V8 as renderer, no Blink
# or any system Node:
node node-only/repro.js
```

### Versions reproduced on

| Electron | Chromium | V8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 42.3.3 (latest stable) | 148.0.7778.218 | 14.8.178.28 |
| 41.x | 146.0.7680.72 | 14.6.202.11 |

(Exact build versions print as the `[env]` line at the top of every run.)

### Workaround

Do not route socket data through `EventTarget`/`dispatchEvent`. A plain callback (or any direct function call) is unaffected — note `plain callback ran=true` on the very message where the listeners were skipped. Replacing the `dispatchEvent("message")` hop with a direct callback fully resolved the dropped messages in the original application.

author: snandy-ts
title: Support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

[Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)](https://blog.google/security/protecting-cookies-with-device-bound-session-credentials/) is a Chromium feature that binds session cookies to a device-specific cryptographic key, mitigating cookie theft. DBSC shipped as enabled-by-default in Chromium 150, and works correctly in Chrome Dev (currently Chromium 151).

However, DBSC does not appear to function in Electron 43.0.0-beta.1 (which bundles Chromium 150). When a server responds with a `Secure-Session-Registration` header, Electron never initiates the DBSC registration flow; i.e., no request is made to the server's registration endpoint. The "Device bound sessions" panel present in Chrome Dev's DevTools (Application tab) is also absent in Electron's DevTools. The feature appears to be entirely non-functional.

I've tested both with and without explicit feature flags (`--enable-features=DeviceBoundSessions,DeviceBoundSessionsDevTools,EnableBoundSessionCredentialsSoftwareKeysForManualTesting,PersistDeviceBoundSessions`) with no change in behavior. The same server setup works correctly in Chrome Dev, where the registration endpoint is called and the session is bound as expected.

Environment:
- Electron 43.0.0-beta.1
- macOS Tahoe 26.5

### Proposed Solution

Enable DBSC support in Electron, matching the behavior of Chromium 150+. Specifically:
- Honor `Secure-Session-Registration` and `Secure-Session-Challenge` response headers to initiate the registration and refresh flows.
- Create and manage device-bound keys via the platform's secure key storage (Secure Enclave on macOS, TPM on Windows).
- Include `Sec-Secure-Session-Id` and `Secure-Session-Response` headers on subsequent requests for bound sessions.

Ideally this would work out of the box, as it does in Chrome, without requiring feature flags.

### Alternatives Considered

- Enabling via Chromium feature flags: Attempted with both Electron 42 and 43 using various combinations of `--enable-features flags`. No effect.
- Implementing session binding at the application level: This would require managing cryptographic keys and intercepting network requests manually, defeating the purpose of a browser-native solution and losing the security guarantees of platform-level key storage.

### Additional Information

- DBSC is particularly relevant for Electron apps that handle sensitive authenticated sessions, as it provides protection against cookie theft/exfiltration attacks.
- It's unclear whether DBSC is intentionally excluded from Electron's Chromium build or unintentionally non-functional. Any guidance on status or planned support would be appreciated.

author: Shieldxx
title: BrowserWindow 'ready-to-show' never emitted when webContents.setZoomFactor() is called on a hidden window before first paint (regression in 40.x)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.0 (also reproduces on 41.7.2 and 40.10.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.8.10

### Expected Behavior

A `BrowserWindow` created with `show: false` emits `ready-to-show` after the renderer's first paint, even if `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on the still-hidden window shortly after `did-finish-load` — this worked on Electron ≤ 39.

### Actual Behavior

When `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on a hidden (`show: false`) window in the gap between `did-finish-load` and the window's first paint, **`ready-to-show` is never emitted** — the window stays invisible forever. This happens **even when the new zoom factor is identical to the current one** (i.e. a semantic no-op call; in our case the same value that was already passed as `webPreferences.zoomFactor`).

Observed state while stuck:

- `did-finish-load` fires normally
- `webContents.isLoading()` → `false`, `isCrashed()` → `false`, page title set, renderer fully interactive
- `win.isVisible()` → `false`, `ready-to-show` listener never invoked (verified registered before `loadFile`)
- Calling `win.show()` manually works fine and shows correct content

Version matrix (identical app code, only the Electron binary swapped):

| Electron | ready-to-show | window visible |
|---|---|---|
| 39.8.10 | emitted | yes |
| 40.10.3 | never | **no** |
| 41.7.2 | never | **no** |
| 42.4.0 | never | **no** |

So the regression was introduced in 40.x.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_ — the suppression is timing-sensitive: in a bare `main.js` with a trivial or even artificially heavy page, calling `setZoomFactor()` synchronously in `did-finish-load` or via `setTimeout(0–200ms)` did **not** reproduce; the real-world trigger is a renderer that calls a zoom IPC during its framework boot (the call lands after `did-finish-load` but before the hidden window's first compositor frame). A reliable public reproduction with exact steps is below; happy to help narrow this down to a Fiddle.

### Additional Information

Reliable reproduction with a small open-source app (MIT):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher
cd SimLauncher
git checkout v0.9.10          # last release before our workaround; package.json pins electron ^39
npm install
npm run build
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 39: window appears
npm install -D electron@42.4.0
npx install-electron
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 42: window NEVER appears
```

The trigger inside the app: the renderer's boot calls a `set-zoom` IPC whose handler runs `webContents.setZoomFactor(factor)` on the still-hidden window ([`src/main/ipc/config.ts`, `set-zoom` handler](https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/blob/v0.9.10/src/main/ipc/config.ts)). The factor equals the construction-time `webPreferences.zoomFactor` (both read the same persisted store), so the call is a no-op value-wise. Commenting out that single `setZoomFactor` line makes `ready-to-show` fire normally on 40–42; restoring it suppresses the event again — bisected via env-flag toggles of individual boot steps, this one line is the sole trigger.

Workaround we shipped (works): skip same-value `setZoomFactor` calls, plus a `did-finish-load` + timeout fallback that shows the window if `ready-to-show` never arrives — https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/pull/487.

User impact before the workaround: app "starts minimized"/invisible reports from production users, since the standard anti-flash pattern (`show: false` + show on `ready-to-show`) never shows the window.

body:

### Electron Version

42.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Debian, Wayland, Gnome

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When the keyring is locked (after auto login or after manually locking the keyring), an electron app should not prompt to unlock the keyring until it is needed, such as after using the safeStorage API.

This was the previous behavior in electron <= 41.7.2 (tested in Electron Fiddle default app).

### Actual Behavior

title: Attempting to show a message box segfaults when using Qt backend
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux (X11, KDE Plasma 6)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Showing a message box should work with both GTK and Qt backends.

### Actual Behavior

When Electron/Chromium is built with `use_qt6=true` ([as Arch Linux does](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/electron42/-/blob/42.3.0-1/PKGBUILD?ref_type=tags#L613)), attempting to show a message box in Electron segfaults when Chromium uses its Qt backend, which it does by default on KDE. Forcing the GTK backend with `--ui-toolkit=gtk` works around the issue. This does not affect upstream binaries as Electron [defaults to](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/build/args/all.gn#L50-L52) `use_qt5 = false` and `use_qt6 = false`.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The issue can be reproduced with the following code:
```js
const { dialog } = require("electron");
dialog.showMessageBox({ message: "test" });
```

I believe it is caused by [this cast](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L47) in `GetGtkUiPlatform`  which assumes `linux_ui` always points to a `GtkUi` instance. The function then calls `GtkUi::GetPlatform` on that object to get `GtkUiPlatform* platform`. I have determined with gdb that the segfault happens on [this line](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/148.0.7778.180/ui/gtk/gtk_util.cc#L214) in Chromium's `gtk::SetGtkTransientForAura` ([called here](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L121-L122) in the `GtkMessageBox` constructor) when it tries to call `platform->SetGtkWidgetTransientFor`. Since `platform` is not actually a `GtkUiPlatform` pointer, this tries to jump to an invalid address leading to a segfault.

title: requestSingleInstanceLock(additionalData): second instance gets the lock and SIGKILLs the first when additionalData.argv has ≥9 elements
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A second app instance that calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock(additionalData)
should always return false, exit, and cause the first (already-running) instance
to receive the 'second-instance' event, regardless of how many elements
additionalData.argv contains. The first instance should keep running.


### Actual Behavior

When additionalData carries an argv array with 9 or more elements:

- The SECOND instance gets `requestSingleInstanceLock() === true` so both
  instances believe they hold the lock.
- The FIRST (running) instance is SIGKILLed. The events 'before-quit'/'will-quit'/'quit'
don't fire, and no crash report is generated.

The first instance logs:

  [ERROR:chrome/browser/process_singleton_posix.cc:779] additional_data_size exceeds payload length
  <electron path> exited with signal SIGKILL

With 8 or fewer argv elements everything works fine. But 9 or more causes this behavior.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Can't repro via Electron fiddle because repro requires 2 instances.

package.json
```
{ 
  "name": "esb", 
  "version": "1.0.0", 
  "main": "main.js" 
}
```

main.js
```
const { app } = require('electron')

const extra = process.argv.slice(2) // trailing CLI args -> additionalData.argv

const gotLock = app.requestSingleInstanceLock({ argv: extra })

console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] lock => ${gotLock} (additionalData.argv length = ${extra.length})`)

app.on('before-quit', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] before-quit`))

app.on('second-instance', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] second-instance (correct)`))

if (!gotLock) { 
  app.quit() 
}
else { 
  app.whenReady().then(() => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] primary ready`)); 
  setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30) 
}
```

author: Hedwig188
title: webContents.print() ignores the `duplexMode` and `printBackground` options (read under the wrong key) since v41.0.0; silent print also never inherits the printer's default duplex
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.0.0 through 42.4.1 (latest stable at time of filing). Also reproduces on v43.0.0-alpha.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Window 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5 (and the rest of the 40.x line) for the duplexMode / printBackground options. See the separate note below on default-duplex inheritance, which is longstanding.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

For `webContents.print()` (silent path):

- Passing `duplexMode: 'longEdge' | 'shortEdge' | 'simplex'` should take effect.
- Passing `printBackground: true` should print background graphics.
- This is how 40.x behaves.
- Also, omitting `duplexMode` should letting the printer/driver default duplex apply during silent printing


### Actual Behavior

Since 41.0.0, in `webContents.print()`:

1. An explicitly supplied `duplexMode` is **ignored** — the job always prints simplex.
2. An explicitly supplied `printBackground` is **ignored** — backgrounds are never printed.

(Both options still work in `printToPDF()`, which is a different, separately-normalized code path.)

3. `duplexMode` defaulting to simplex when no value is supplied. There is no way to request "use the printer's configured default."

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Root Cause

In `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc`, `WebContents::Print` reads several caller options out of the JS `options` dictionary using Chromium's internal **print-settings key constants** instead of the public JS option names.

The JS layer does not rename options: `WebContents.prototype.print` in `lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts` passes the caller's `options` object straight to the native `_print` binding (only `pageSize` is transformed into `mediaSize`). So native receives the public names, e.g. `duplexMode` and `printBackground`.

Most option reads survive only because the Chromium key string coincidentally equals the JS option name:

| JS option | native reads under | string value | matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `printing::kSettingColor` | `"color"` | yes |
| `landscape` | `printing::kSettingLandscape` | `"landscape"` | yes |
| `deviceName` | `printing::kSettingDeviceName` | `"deviceName"` | yes |
| `scaleFactor` | `printing::kSettingScaleFactor` | `"scaleFactor"` | yes |
| `pagesPerSheet` | `printing::kSettingPagesPerSheet` | `"pagesPerSheet"` | yes |
| `collate` | `printing::kSettingCollate` | `"collate"` | yes |
| `copies` | `printing::kSettingCopies` | `"copies"` | yes |
| **`duplexMode`** | `printing::kSettingDuplexMode` | **`"duplex"`** | **no** |
| **`printBackground`** | `printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds` | **`"shouldPrintBackgrounds"`** | **no** |

The string values are from Chromium `printing/print_job_constants.cc`.

Because the JS object never contains a `"duplex"` or `"shouldPrintBackgrounds"` key, those two reads never match and always return their fallbacks (`kSimplex` / `false`), which are then written into the settings.

### duplexMode

**40.8.5 (working):**

```cpp
// Duplex type user wants to use.
const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(
    "duplexMode", printing::mojom::DuplexMode::kSimplex);
settings.Set(printing::kSettingDuplexMode, static_cast<int>(duplex_mode));
```

**41.0.0+ (broken):**

```cpp
// Duplex type user wants to use.
const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(
    printing::kSettingDuplexMode, printing::mojom::DuplexMode::kSimplex);
settings.Set(printing::kSettingDuplexMode, static_cast<int>(duplex_mode));
```

`printing::kSettingDuplexMode` is `"duplex"`, not `"duplexMode"`.

### printBackground

**40.8.5 (working):**

```cpp
settings.Set(printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds,
             options.ValueOrDefault("printBackground", false));
```

**41.0.0+ (broken):**

```cpp
settings.Set(
    printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds,
    options.ValueOrDefault(printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds, false));
```

`printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds` is `"shouldPrintBackgrounds"`, not `"printBackground"`. (Note: v41 even defines a correct local constant `kPrintBackground = "printBackground"`, but the read does not use it.)

Both regressions were introduced by the 41.0.0 printing refactor that added `usePrinterDefaultPageSize` (#49812), which switched these reads to `kSetting*` constants. The other options were unaffected only by the coincidence above.

## Separate (longstanding) issue: cannot inherit the printer's default duplex

Independent of the regression: `WebContents::Print` *always* writes `kSettingDuplexMode`, defaulting to simplex when no value is supplied. This is true in 40.x as well. As a result, omitting `duplexMode` forces simplex rather than letting the printer/driver default duplex apply during silent printing — there is no way to request "use the printer's configured default."

Suggested handling: only set `kSettingDuplexMode` when the caller actually supplied a value, so an omitted `duplexMode` leaves the driver default intact.

author: robschi
title: `showSaveDialog`: directory-less `defaultPath` produces `current_folder="."` on Linux (portal) — unlike macOS/Windows
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.0 

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch (Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A directory-less `defaultPath` should set the suggested filename only and must not
produce a relative `current_folder` — matching the macOS and Windows behavior.

### Actual Behavior

The `SaveFile` options carry a valid `current_name` but a relative `current_folder`:

```
   array [
      dict entry(
         string "current_name"
         variant             string "test.jpeg"
      )
      dict entry(
         string "current_folder"
         variant             array of bytes "." + \0
      )
   ]
```

Real-world capture from the Flatpak Signal (`org.signal.Signal`, Electron 42.3.0):

```
... member=SaveFile
   string "org.signal.Signal"
   string "wayland:..."
   string "All Files"
   array [
      dict entry(
         string "current_name"
         variant             string "signal-2026-05-24-214530.jpeg"
      )
      dict entry(
         string "current_folder"
         variant             array of bytes "." + \0
      )
   ]
```

The dialog's location becomes `file:.` (an unusable relative path). With the LXQt
backend the filename field also comes up empty.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This is a problem I hit with the Flatpak version of Signal when saving files through
the Linux file-chooser portal — it looks like it can be fixed in Electron's Linux
dialog code (details below). Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend, but the
malformed request is sent regardless of backend.

This report was drafted with AI assistance; the `dbus-monitor` capture is from my
own machine and the code references point to the linked diffs, so it can all be
verified directly.

## Summary

On Linux, `dialog.showSaveDialog` / `dialog.showOpenDialog` with a **directory-less
`defaultPath`** (a bare filename — which the docs explicitly permit) sends
`current_folder="."` in the xdg-desktop-portal `SaveFile` request. The relative `.`
is not a usable directory: the dialog opens at a broken location (shown as
`file:.`), and on stricter portal backends the suggested filename is dropped too.
macOS and Windows handle the identical input correctly.

## Platform

- Linux, Wayland
- xdg-desktop-portal FileChooser interface v4
- Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend (empty filename **and** `file:.`). The
  malformed `current_folder="."` is produced by Electron/Chromium and sent to
  whichever backend is configured; how visible the breakage is depends on the
  backend (GTK tolerates the `.` and still prefills the name; LXQt does not).

## Steps to reproduce

Minimal main-process snippet:

```js
const { app, dialog } = require('electron')
app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  // bare filename, no directory — allowed per the docs
  await dialog.showSaveDialog({ defaultPath: 'test.jpeg' })
})
```

While the dialog is open, watch the portal call:

```
dbus-monitor --session "interface='org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser',member='SaveFile'"
```

## Root cause

`shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_linux.cc` forwards `settings.default_path` to
`SelectFile` unmodified whenever it is non-empty:

```cpp
base::FilePath default_path = settings.default_path.empty()
                                  ? electron::GetDefaultPath()
                                  : settings.default_path;
dialog_->SelectFile(..., default_path, ...);
```

A bare filename is non-empty, so it is passed straight through, and Chromium's
portal layer then derives `current_folder` from `DirName()` → `"."`.

macOS and Windows guard against exactly this:

- `file_dialog_mac.mm` — sets the directory only `if (default_path.IsAbsolute())`,
  otherwise uses `BaseName()` as the filename and leaves the directory unset.
- `file_dialog_win.cc` — `SetFileName(BaseName)` and only calls `SetDefaultFolder`
  `if (default_path.IsAbsolute())`.

The Linux path has no equivalent `IsAbsolute()` guard. The recent "default to
Downloads folder" PRs (#49441 → #49538 → #49868, targeting 43.0) only handle the
**empty** `defaultPath` case and leave this code path untouched.
