author: SchmelleDevCrea
title: [Bug]: Electron 44.0.0 Linux SIGTRAP: PartitionAlloc freelist corruption detected during Fontconfig startup
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble), Linux 7.0.0-30-generic, X11 via Xvfb

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

No reliable last-known-working Electron version. The failure is intermittent and has not been compared against a controlled older-Electron matrix.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Under the stated packaged-AppImage startup conditions, Electron should initialize Fontconfig, start the main process, and create the first BrowserWindow without terminating.

### Actual Behavior

The Electron browser/main process intermittently exits with SIGTRAP during application startup.

The failure has been observed in independent command-line startup cases that use valid debug-level options and valid diagnostic-log-directory options. The fully symbolicated instance occurred while a valid debug-level startup case was initializing; other instances occurred after internal service readiness while creating the first BrowserWindow.

This is a native SIGTRAP from Electron/Chromium PartitionAlloc, not a harness timeout, SIGTERM cleanup, OOM event, disk-full event, or GPU-process failure.

### Testcase Gist URL

No public testcase is currently available because the packaged application is closed source.  The failure is reproduced by repeatedly launching one retained Linux AppImage through the sequential startup matrix described in Additional Information. A matching Crashpad minidump, full symbolicated output, and a retained-binary reproduction environment are available privately on maintainer request.

### Additional Information

## Summary

This is an intermittent native `SIGTRAP` from Electron `44.0.0` on Ubuntu `24.04.4`.

Electron's matching public Linux x64 symbols resolve the crash to `partition_alloc::internal::FreelistCorruptionDetected`. Detection occurs when Fontconfig calls `strdup()` while parsing font XML configuration.

This identifies where Electron detected invalid allocator freelist metadata. It does **not** prove that Fontconfig, Pango, or Expat made the earlier invalid write or free.

## Environment

- Electron: `44.0.0`
- Electron public-symbol debug ID: `E798769358C1C954E22B4446B9C113EB0`
- OS: Ubuntu `24.04.4 LTS` (Noble)
- Kernel: `7.0.0-30-generic`
- Architecture: x64
- Display: X11 via Xvfb
- Virtualization: VirtualBox
- VM memory: 5 GiB
- Virtual GPU acceleration: disabled

Relevant Ubuntu packages:

- fontconfig: `2.15.0-1.1ubuntu2`
- libfontconfig1: `2.15.0-1.1ubuntu2`
- libpango-1.0-0: `1.52.1+ds-1build1`
- libpangoft2-1.0-0: `1.52.1+ds-1build1`
- libexpat1: `2.6.1-2ubuntu0.4`

## Controlled Reproduction Process

The product is a closed-source Linux AppImage. I do not yet have a standalone public reproducer.

The failure is captured using one retained AppImage, so no rebuild occurs between attempts:

1. Extract the AppImage once with `--appimage-extract`.
2. Run the extracted `AppRun` repeatedly.
3. Use one Xvfb display and one D-Bus session for a run.
4. Use a minimal Fontconfig configuration containing only system font directories, then run `fc-cache -f`.
5. Start only one application process at a time.
6. Give each launch a fresh temporary data directory, XDG cache/config/runtime directories, diagnostic directory, loopback ports, and process group.
7. Wait up to 120 seconds for the startup-ready record. On successful readiness, request orderly shutdown. Stop the stress run at the first `SIGTRAP`.

The fully symbolicated crash occurred during this valid startup invocation:

    AppRun --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage --disable-software-rasterizer -- --backend-debug info --frontend-debug off --profile-log <temporary-profile-path>

This invocation starts the application normally, applies valid command-line debug settings, and waits for the startup-ready record. It does not load user projects, measurement data, remote content, or application workflows.

The packaged Linux AppImage uses `--no-sandbox`. The following flags are CI-specific and have not yet been individually removed from the reproduction:

- `--disable-gpu`
- `--disable-dev-shm-usage`
- `--disable-software-rasterizer`

## Observed Frequency

The retained Electron 44 AppImage completed 99 complete sequential startup stress runs successfully. Attempt 100 then failed during another valid startup case using a diagnostic log-directory argument.

The following reduced observed frequency but did not eliminate the crash:

- increasing VM memory;
- reducing concurrent VM activity;
- serializing application launches;
- reusing one Xvfb/D-Bus session;
- using a minimal Fontconfig configuration;
- prewarming the Fontconfig cache.

An isolated Expat `2.8.3` build was also tested. `ldd` confirmed that Electron and Fontconfig loaded the replacement `libexpat.so.1`, but the same native `SIGTRAP` occurred. This rejects Expat replacement as a fix.

## Fully Symbolicated Crashing Thread

    partition_alloc::internal::FreelistCorruptionDetected
    partition_alloc::PartitionRoot::Alloc
    malloc
    libc.so.6!__GI___strdup
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcExprCreateString
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcParseFamily
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcEndElement
    libexpat.so.1
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcConfigParseAndLoadFromMemoryInternal

The Crashpad dump shows:

- process uptime: approximately 8 seconds;
- `SIGTRAP`, not `SIGSEGV`;
- crash in the Electron browser/main process, not a renderer or GPU subprocess;
- no OOM, disk-full, GPU, or test-harness-timeout event.

## Questions

1. Does this match a known Electron/Chromium Linux PartitionAlloc or allocator-shim issue involving system Fontconfig/Pango libraries?
2. Is packaged AppImage `--no-sandbox` behavior relevant to this allocation path?
3. Which supported Electron or Chromium diagnostics can identify the earlier allocation, free, or write that corrupted the freelist before `malloc()` detected it?
4. Is there a later Electron or Chromium branch with a relevant Linux allocator fix that should be tested?

## Potentially Related Report

This may be related at the environment and symptom level, but has not been proven to be the same root cause:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322185

## Evidence Availability

A matching Crashpad `.dmp`, complete symbolicated output, sanitized command line, and additional environment details are available through a private maintainer-requested channel.

I will not publish the raw minidump, system core, packaged binary, source code, or CI evidence directory publicly.

## Analysis Note

This report was heavily AI-assisted. The underlying evidence was independently captured and verified through retained-AppImage startup loops, Crashpad minidumps, systemd core metadata, official Electron 44 symbols, exact package versions, and the resolved native stack.

Please treat the causal interpretation as a diagnostic lead. Corrections, requests for non-sensitive evidence, and guidance toward a supported minimal reproducer are welcome.

author: codebytere
title: Tray icon missing on GNOME (Wayland) in 44.0.0 / 43.4.1+: StatusNotifierItem registration is rejected
body:
### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also 44.0.0-beta.6, 43.4.1, 43.4.2)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME with the default ubuntu-appindicators extension, Wayland and Xorg sessions

### What arch are you using?

x64, arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

44.0.0-beta.5 / 43.4.0 (icon registers; see #52674 for the separate menu problem those had), 42.x fully working

### Expected Behavior

`new Tray(image)` registers a StatusNotifierItem with `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and the icon shows in the GNOME top bar.

### Actual Behavior

Nothing is registered with the watcher (`busctl --user get-property org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher /StatusNotifierWatcher org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` never lists the app). On Wayland there is no tray icon at all; on Xorg the legacy XEmbed fallback icon appears instead.

The item calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem("org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1")`, i.e. the well-known name with the object path appended. GNOME's watcher treats an argument that does not start with `/` as a bus name, `GetNameOwner` fails on that string, and the registration is refused, after which the SNI implementation is torn down. This came in with the cherry-pick of https://crrev.com/c/8250459 in #52951 (44-x-y) and #52952 (43-x-y); upstream fixed it a week later in https://crrev.com/c/8272040 (in Chromium 154.0.8016.0, so `main` already has it), which registers the plain well-known name and exports the item at `/StatusNotifierItem` again.

### Testcase Gist URL

```js
const { app, Tray, Menu, nativeImage } = require('electron');
app.on('ready', () => {
  const t = new Tray(nativeImage.createFromPath('icon.png'));
  t.setContextMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate([{ label: 'Quit', role: 'quit' }]));
});
```

Per-version result against a watcher that resolves items the way the GNOME extension does:

| version | RegisterStatusNotifierItem argument | result |
|---|---|---|
| 42.10.0 | `:1.1` | ok |
| 43.4.0, 44.0.0-beta.5 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` | registered (menu issue is #52674) |
| 43.4.1, 44.0.0-beta.6, 44.0.0 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1` | `NameHasNoOwner`, registration refused |

Google Chrome 151.0.7922.173 in the **same** sandbox does not abort: `google-chrome-stable --version` prints the version, and `--headless=new --dump-dom about:blank` exits 0. Outside the sandbox, `electron --version` prints `v43.4.0` and exits 0. ### Testcase Gist URL No app code is required. Reproduction with the official binary: ```bash curl -fsSL -o electron.zip \ https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v43.4.0/electron-v43.4.0-linux-x64.zip unzip -q electron.zip ./electron --version # v43.4.0 # Codex (or any Linux sandbox that makes shutdown(2) return EPERM): codex sandbox -- ./electron --version # FATAL:content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc:41 Check failed: . shutdown: Operation not permitted (1) ``` A direct check that the sandbox returns EPERM for `shutdown`: ```bash codex sandbox -- python3 -c 'import socket,ctypes,ctypes.util a,b=socket.socketpair(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_SEQPACKET) libc=ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("c"), use_errno=True) r=libc.shutdown(a.fileno(), 0); print("ret", r, "errno", ctypes.get_errno())' # ret -1 errno 1 ``` ### Additional Information This showed up first as a Slack Desktop 4.51.191 coredump after `slack --version` was run from a Codex bubblewrap jail (`tmux-spawn` scope, root mounted `ro,nosuid,nodev`, `/tmp/.codex` present). Slack has no public desktop issue tracker, so this is filed against Electron. Vanilla Electron 43.4.0 reproduces it. `chrome-sandbox` on the Slack package is correctly `rwsr-xr-x` root. This is not the SUID-helper-misconfigured abort.
In-depth investigation

Chromium `content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc` `SandboxHostLinux::Init()` does: ```cpp CHECK(socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0, fds) == 0); PCHECK(0 == shutdown(child_socket_, SHUT_RD)) << "shutdown"; ``` The outer sandbox's seccomp filter returns `EPERM` for `shutdown(2)` (`man shutdown` does not list EPERM as a normal error). Chromium treats that as fatal and calls `ImmediateCrash()` (`int3; ud2`), which the kernel delivers as SIGTRAP. systemd-coredump for Slack PID 24324: signal 5 (TRAP), `si_code: SI_KERNEL`, command `/usr/lib/slack/slack --version`. RIP was `int3` / `ud2`. The core contained the FATAL line above. One main thread; died during Chromium sandbox-host init. Chrome 151 in the same Codex sandbox logs `setsockopt: Operation not permitted` from crashpad and continues. Electron 43.4.0 / Chromium 150 still takes the fatal PCHECK path on `--version`.

author: thomasbachem
title: setZoomLevel() / setZoomFactor() is silently ignored before the first navigation in the isolated and manual zoom modes
body:
### Electron Version

45.0.0-nightly.20260826 (current `main`, local build)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS 26 (arm64) – the code path is platform-independent browser-process logic

### Expected Behavior

A zoom level set before the first navigation commits is applied once the page loads, in the zoom
modes that are meant to persist (`isolated` and `manual`) – the same way
`webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated', zoomFactor: 1.5 }` already behaves.

### Actual Behavior

The call is silently dropped – no error, no return value, and `getZoomFactor()` stays at `1`:

```js
const w = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated' } })
w.webContents.setZoomFactor(1.5)        // silently dropped
await w.loadURL('https://example.com')
w.webContents.getZoomFactor()           // 1 (expected 1.5)
```

`WebContentsZoomController::SetZoomLevel()` bails out on `!IsRenderFrameLive()` (no frame is live
before the first navigation commits), and the JS binding discards its `bool` result, so nothing
surfaces to the app. Expressing the same intent through web preferences does work, so the two
spellings of one intent disagree.

Workaround: pass the initial factor via `webPreferences: { zoomFactor }` instead of calling the
setter before load.

I have a fix with regression specs ready, built and tested against `main` – PR to follow.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_ (the snippet above is the complete reproduction)

author: Llegion404
title: [Bug]: Linux safeStorage kwallet backend uses KWallet4-era D-Bus path on Plasma 6 and --password-store is ignored
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.8.1 (Chromium 148.0.7778.280) — as shipped in VS Code 1.133/1.134/1.135; all three reproduce.

### What operating system are you using?

Arch Linux x86_64, KDE Plasma 6.7.4 (Wayland), kwallet 6.29 (`kwalletd6`; no kwalletd5 present)

### What architecture are you using?

x64

### Last Working Electron Version

Unknown — this reproduces on every Electron-42-era build I tested. The documented `--password-store` workaroutes (e.g. `kwallet5`) reportedly worked on earlier Electron generations.

### Expected Behavior

On KDE Plasma 6, `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` should return `true`: kwalletd6 is running, enabled, the default wallet is open, and it serves the KWallet D-Bus API at `/modules/kwalletd5` and `/modules/kwalletd6` (and owns all three bus names `org.kde.kwalletd`, `org.kde.kwalletd5`, `org.kde.kwalletd6`).

`--password-store` should select the backend (per the Chromium `key_storage_util_linux.cc` contract and VS Code's documentation of this flag for Electron apps).

### Actual Behavior

Two distinct problems:

**1. The kwallet backend unconditionally uses the KWallet4-era service path.** OSCrypt probes `org.kde.KWallet.isEnabled` at **`/modules/kwalletd`**, which kwalletd6 does not export → `UnknownObject` → OSCrypt initializes no backend → `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` returns `false` and secrets fall back to the hardcoded-password "v11" encryption.

**2. `--password-store` has no effect on OSCrypt selection.** Tested as a fresh main process:

| `--password-store` | `Selected backend for OSCrypt` | object path probed |
|---|---|---|
| *(unset / detect)* | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `kwallet5` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `kwallet6` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `gnome-libsecret` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |

Setting `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE` and `KDE_SESSION_VERSION=6` explicitly does not change the outcome. Notably, the `Password storage detected desktop environment: ...` VLOG from `key_storage_util_linux.cc` (documented in VS Code's keychain troubleshooting) never appears at all — the whole detection/selection stage seems bypassed.

### Testcase Gist / Code To Reproduce

Any Electron 42 app on Plasma 6:

```js
// main.js
const { app, safeStorage } = require('electron');
app.whenReady().then(() => {
  console.log('isEncryptionAvailable:', safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable());
  console.log('getSelectedStorageBackend:', safeStorage.getSelectedStorageBackend());
  app.exit(0);
});
```

```sh
npx electron . --password-store=kwallet5 --enable-logging=stderr --vmodule="*/components/os_crypt/*=2"
```

stderr:

```
VERBOSE1:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:116] Selected backend for OSCrypt: KWALLET
WARNING:dbus/object_proxy.cc:570] Failed to call method: org.kde.KWallet.isEnabled: object_path= /modules/kwalletd: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownObject: No such object path '/modules/kwalletd'
ERROR:components/os_crypt/sync/kwallet_dbus.cc:113] Error contacting kwalletd (isEnabled)
ERROR:components/os_crypt/sync/kwallet_dbus.cc:82] Error contacting klauncher to start kwalletd
WARNING:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:189] OSCrypt tried KWallet but couldn't initialise.
VERBOSE1:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:135] OSCrypt did not initialize a backend.
```

Output: `isEncryptionAvailable: false`, `getSelectedStorageBackend: kwallet` — identical for every `--password-store` value.

### Additional Information

- Per the Chromium 148 source, `KWalletDBus::KWalletDBus(base::nix::DesktopEnvironment)` only picks the `kwalletd5`/`kwalletd6` constants for `DESKTOP_ENVIRONMENT_KDE5`/`KDE6`; everything else — including whatever value is being computed here — falls into the legacy `else` branch with the KWallet4 constants (`org.kde.kwalletd` + `/modules/kwalletd`).
- Consequence on disk: all app secrets stored with the `v11` prefix (hardcoded-password fallback) instead of `v10` (keyring).
- There is no way to work around this from the OS side: kwalletd6 owns `org.kde.kwalletd` and **exits with status 1** (`Failed to register name 'org.kde.kwalletd' with DBUS`) if it can't, so a proxy on the legacy bus name cannot coexist with it. Meanwhile kwalletd6 answers fine on `/modules/kwalletd5` and `/modules/kwalletd6`, so simply honoring the flag (or fixing the DE detection) would resolve it.
- Downstream impact tracked in microsoft/vscode#332559 (VS Code shows "You're running in a KDE environment but the OS keyring is not available for encryption…" on every secret write), with my full diagnosis at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332559#issuecomment-5441155367. VS Code's documented KDE 6 workaround (`--password-store=kwallet5`) no longer does anything because of problem 2.

author: claude
title: Tracking: documented APIs without spec test coverage (docs/api vs spec audit)
body:
An audit of the documented API surface in `docs/api/*.md` (main @ ffd19de9) against the test suite under `spec/`. Method: static cross-reference — every documented method/property/event/constructor/`<webview>` attribute heading was searched for references anywhere in `spec/` (dedicated `api-*-spec.ts`, any other spec, or `spec/ts-smoke` type tests).

Scope: 1,577 documented API items across 76 `docs/api` files. `docs/api/structures/` (110 files) plus `command-line-switches`, `environment-variables`, `corner-smoothing-css`, and `window-open` were excluded as non-testable surfaces.

## Overall numbers

| | items | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Referenced somewhere in `spec/` | 1,300 | 82% |
| Referenced **only** in `spec/ts-smoke` type tests | 40 | 3% |
| **No reference anywhere in `spec/`** | **237** | **15%** |

## Headline gaps

- **`pushNotifications`: 0/3 covered, no spec file at all** — the entire macOS APNS surface (`registerForAPNSNotifications`, `unregisterForAPNSNotifications`, `received-apns-notification`) is untested.
- **`BaseWindow` has no dedicated spec file** despite 187 documented items. Its coverage is almost entirely incidental via `BrowserWindow` tests; 30 items have no reference at all.
- **`unresponsive`/`responsive` events** (on both `BrowserWindow` and `WebContents`) have zero references anywhere in `spec/` — not even a string match — despite being the primary hang-detection API.
- **`Tray` interaction surface is essentially untested**: every interaction event (`click` variants, `mouse-*`, all `drag-*`/`drop-*`), `balloon-click`/`balloon-closed`, `getGUID`, `removeBalloon`.
- **All four `screen` DIP conversion methods** (`screenToDipPoint`, `dipToScreenPoint`, `screenToDipRect`, `dipToScreenRect`) are untested.

## Per-module task list (worst offenders)

Counts are uncovered/total documented items, where "uncovered" = no reference in `spec/` or ts-smoke-only. Item lists below name the most notable gaps, not all of them — full item-level detail is in the linked report.

- [ ] **pushNotifications — 3/3**: whole module (`registerForAPNSNotifications`, `unregisterForAPNSNotifications`, `received-apns-notification`); no spec file exists
- [ ] **webContents — 37/200**: `unresponsive`/`responsive`, device emulation (`enableDeviceEmulation`/`disableDeviceEmulation`), caret browsing (`setCaretBrowsingEnabled`/`isCaretBrowsingEnabled`), selection/scroll helpers (`centerSelection`, `unselect`, `scrollToTop`, `scrollToBottom`, `adjustSelection`), `copyImageAt`, `saveVideoFrameAs`, `isBeingCaptured`, `isWaitingForResponse`, `inspectSharedWorker`/`inspectServiceWorker`, `replaceMisspelling`, `input-event`, `cursor-changed`, `update-target-url`, `preferred-size-changed`
- [ ] **BrowserWindow — 35/204**: `unresponsive`/`responsive`, `will-resize`/`will-move`/`moved`, `query-session-end`/`session-end`, `app-command`, `flashFrame`, `hookWindowMessage` family, thumbar/thumbnail methods (`setThumbarButtons`, `setThumbnailClip`, `setThumbnailToolTip`), `setOverlayIcon`, `setBackgroundMaterial`, `isSnapped`/`snapped`, `focusOnWebView`/`blurWebView`
- [ ] **BaseWindow — 31/187**: no dedicated spec file; largely the same window-management gaps as BrowserWindow (`will-resize`/`will-move`/`moved`, `session-end` events, `hookWindowMessage` family, thumbar methods, `flashFrame`, `getContentView`, `isModal`, `isNormal`, `setBackgroundMaterial`)
- [ ] **session — 25/93**: `clearCodeCaches`, `clearHostResolverCache`, `setUSBProtectedClassesHandler`, `setBluetoothPairingHandler`, the spellchecker surface (`setSpellCheckerEnabled`, `isSpellCheckerEnabled`, `getSpellCheckerLanguages`, `availableSpellCheckerLanguages`, all four `spellcheck-dictionary-*` events), device add/remove events (`hid-*`, `serial-port-*`, `usb-device-*`), `getCacheSize`, `flushStorageData`, `closeAllConnections`
- [ ] **app — 24/114**: `will-quit`, `will-finish-launching`, `gpu-info-update`, macOS activity/Handoff surface (`continue-activity` family, `updateCurrentActivity`, `invalidateCurrentActivity`, `resignCurrentActivity`), `open-file`/`open-url`, `hasSingleInstanceLock`, `setAppUserModelId`, `moveToApplicationsFolder`, `toastActivatorCLSID`
- [ ] **Tray — 20/36**: every interaction event — `click` (behavioral), `right-click`, `double-click`, `middle-click`, `mouse-up`/`mouse-down`/`mouse-enter`/`mouse-leave`/`mouse-move`, `drag-enter`/`drag-leave`/`drag-end`, `drop`/`drop-files`/`drop-text` — plus `balloon-click`/`balloon-closed`, `removeBalloon`, `getGUID`
- [ ] **`<webview>` tag — 24/113**: mostly repeats of the webContents method gaps (`centerSelection`, `unselect`, scroll helpers, `adjustSelection`, `replaceMisspelling`, `inspect*Worker`, `isWaitingForResponse`) plus attributes `plugins`, `nodeintegrationinsubframes`, `enableblinkfeatures`/`disableblinkfeatures` and events `load-commit`, `update-target-url`
- [ ] **systemPreferences — 10/26**: macOS notification subscription surface (`postNotification`, `postLocalNotification`, all `unsubscribe*Notification`), `askForMediaAccess`, `accent-color-changed`, `isSwipeTrackingFromScrollEventsEnabled`
- [ ] **powerMonitor — 8/16**: `lock-screen`/`unlock-screen`, `thermal-state-change`, `speed-limit-change`, `user-did-become-active`/`user-did-resign-active` (`on-ac`/`on-battery` are ts-smoke-only)
- [ ] **screen — 7/12**: all four DIP conversion methods (`screenToDipPoint`, `dipToScreenPoint`, `screenToDipRect`, `dipToScreenRect`); `display-added`/`display-removed`/`display-metrics-changed` are ts-smoke-only
- [ ] **Notification — 5/30**: `reply` and `action` events, `handleActivation`, `urgency`, `timeoutType`
- [ ] **TouchBar item classes — 12 items** across `TouchBarScrubber` (4), `TouchBarColorPicker`, `TouchBarLabel`, `TouchBarSegmentedControl`, `TouchBarSlider`, `TouchBarButton` (2 each) — mostly instance properties never read/written in tests

## Platform split of the 237 unreferenced items

- 55 macOS-only
- 40 Windows-only
- 145 with no platform restriction — testable on the existing Linux CI path today

## Full report

Item-by-item breakdown (all 1,577 items, per-module tables, tier for each item): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/671ee4f0-4aef-4f61-b2b9-80cb5bc34f2a

## Caveats

- This is **static string matching**: an item counts as "covered" if its name is referenced anywhere in `spec/`. A reference is not a behavioral assertion — common short names (`show`, `focus`, `id`) inflate apparent coverage, so the real behavioral gap is larger than 15%.
- Conversely, some items may be exercised indirectly (e.g. via helpers) without a name match, though heading-level matching makes this rare.
- Many gaps are platform-bound (Tray interactions, thumbar, APNS) and genuinely hard to drive in CI — the task list is for triage, not an assertion that every item is automatable.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

author: marcdownie
title: Linux + useSharedTexture = black texture
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also reproduced on 42.3.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

CachyOS (Arch), kernel 7.1.3-1-cachyos, x86_64. KDE Plasma 6 / kwin_wayland, and separately a bare Xorg session on a spare VT.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

none on Linux (useSharedTexture working great on MacOS and Windows)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the dma-buf referenced by
`textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap` should contain the rendered page.

### Actual Behavior

The `paint` event fires, `textureInfo` is fully populated and plausible, and the dma-buf is a real,
importable allocation of exactly the expected size — but every byte of it is zero.

This is **not** #49247. There, `paint` never fires with a texture. Here the handle arrives and is
structurally correct; only its contents are missing. It also reproduces where
`supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport` is `true`, which is the configuration #49247 treats as working.

The clearest way to see it uses only Electron's own APIs — `sharedTexture.importSharedTexture`,
`sendSharedTexture`, and `VideoFrame.copyTo`. No native addon, no external consumer:

Under KDE Plasma / Wayland:

```
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=false  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=578d48a9-...
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

And on a bare Xorg session on a spare VT, where the flag is `true` — the configuration #49247
treats as working — the same script, unchanged:

```
session: tty  DISPLAY=:1  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=unset
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=true  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=14f9f92c-186a-4e2d-ac3a-07d73971ff53
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

The page under test is a solid, continuously animating background, so a correct buffer cannot be
zero. The A/B against Chromium's other output path, same URL, same switches, same machine, differing
only in `useSharedTexture`:

| offscreen mode | non-zero pixels |
| --- | --- |
| `useSharedTexture: false` (CPU bitmap) | 921600 / 921600 |
| `useSharedTexture: true` (dma-buf) | 0 / 921600 |

Chromium renders the page; only the shared-texture export is empty.

#### What has been ruled out

Four independent readers agree the memory is zero — Electron's own import + WebCodecs readback; a
`VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` import plus GPU copy; a CPU `mmap` with `DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC`; and
a third-party Vulkan consumer. The CPU mapping shares none of the Vulkan importers' assumptions
about modifier, stride, memory type or layout, and still reads zero. Zeros rather than garbage
argues the memory is genuinely zero rather than correct bytes read through a wrong layout.

Also ruled out:

- **Timing.** Reading 3 seconds after the paint, while still holding the lease, is unchanged.
- **Warm-up.** The 25th paint of a continuously animating page is unchanged.
- **First-frame effects.** Same at paint 1, 5, 10 and 25.
- **Content.** Same for a `data:` URL, a local app, and a fully loaded `https://youtube.com`.
- **Format.** Same for `argb` (stride 5120) and `rgbaf16` (stride 10240).
- **Electron version.** Same on 42.3.3 and 44.0.0.
- **Session type.** Same under Wayland and under a real Xorg session (not XWayland).
- **Vulkan/ANGLE coherence.** See below.

#### Interaction with #49247, and one caution

On Wayland, Chromium logs `Unable to initialize SkSurface` and delivers `paint` with no texture,
exactly as #49247 reports. Adding **`--use-angle=vulkan`** alongside `--enable-features=Vulkan`
clears that: ANGLE moves onto Vulkan (`ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.341, RTX 4090)`), the error stops,
and a real dma-buf is delivered. `--enable-features=Vulkan` on its own is not enough, and
`--ignore-gpu-blocklist` on its own is worse than neither, because it enables Vulkan while leaving
ANGLE on GL — which is also when Ozone reports Wayland and Vulkan to be incompatible.

That may be useful to #49247 on its own. But it does not fix the buffer, and neither does Xorg. On a
bare Xorg session `supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport` flips to `true` and all four readers still see
zero.

The caution: the "Ubuntu 24.04 Xorg — works fine" result in #49247 is evidenced by a `console.log`
of `textureInfo`, which is metadata. That is the same metadata this machine prints under Xorg,
`supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport: true` included. I could not find anywhere in that thread, or in the
shared-texture docs, where the *pixels* are read back and checked. So the two observations may not
conflict: the handle can be correct while the buffer behind it is never filled, and only a consumer
that samples it would notice. If someone with a known-good Linux setup can run the script below and
report a non-zero count, that would localise this to NVIDIA immediately.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/marcdownie/2938b49759c9516ff4612ade344d6f22

### Additional Information

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, proprietary driver 610.43.02. The machine also has an AMD Raphael
iGPU, but Chromium runs on the NVIDIA card throughout (confirmed via
`WEBGL_debug_renderer_info`); the AMD path could not be tested, because restricting the Vulkan ICD
to RADV prevents the GPU process from starting against this NVIDIA-driven display.

`--ozone-platform=x11` inside a Wayland session is XWayland and is not a substitute: the GPU process
dies with exit code 139, matching #49247. The Xorg results above are from a genuine X server started
on a spare VT.

author: Chaussetthe
title: [Bug]: linux-arm64 builds published since 2026-08-24 expose x86-64 fcntl constants (O_DIRECTORY / O_NOFOLLOW / O_DIRECT)
body:
## Preflight checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

## Electron version

44.0.0 (also 42.10.0, 42.10.1)

## What operating system(s) are you using?

Debian (forky/sid), aarch64

## Operating System Version

Linux aarch64, ext4

## What arch are you using?

arm64

## Last Known Working Electron version

43.4.1 (published 2026-08-19)

## Expected Behavior

On aarch64 Linux, `fs.constants` should carry the arm64 values defined in
`arch/arm64/include/uapi/asm/fcntl.h`:

| constant | aarch64 | generic / x86-64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `O_DIRECTORY` | 16384 (`040000`) | 65536 (`0200000`) |
| `O_NOFOLLOW` | 32768 (`0100000`) | 131072 (`0400000`) |
| `O_DIRECT` | 65536 (`0200000`) | 16384 (`040000`) |

arm64 is one of the architectures that override the `asm-generic` defaults, and it
swaps exactly these two pairs.

## Actual Behavior

Affected linux-arm64 builds report the **generic/x86-64** values. On arm64 those bit
patterns mean `O_DIRECT | O_LARGEFILE`, so any `open()` that asks for
`O_DIRECTORY` actually asks for `O_DIRECT`, and opening a directory with `O_DIRECT`
returns `EINVAL`.

```
$ unzip -q electron-v44.0.0-linux-arm64.zip -d x
$ cd x && ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ./electron ../repro.js
arch            : arm64
electron        : 44.0.0
node            : 24.18.1
O_DIRECTORY     : 65536 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 131072 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 16384 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : EINVAL   <-- the bug

$ node ../repro.js          # system Node, same machine, same kernel
arch            : arm64
electron        : undefined
node            : 24.20.0
O_DIRECTORY     : 16384 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 32768 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 65536 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK
```

## Testcase Gist URL / repro.js

```js
const fs = require('fs');
const c = fs.constants;
console.log('arch            :', process.arch);
console.log('electron        :', process.versions.electron);
console.log('node            :', process.versions.node);
console.log('O_DIRECTORY     :', c.O_DIRECTORY, '(aarch64 expects 16384)');
console.log('O_NOFOLLOW      :', c.O_NOFOLLOW, '(aarch64 expects 32768)');
console.log('O_DIRECT        :', c.O_DIRECT, '(aarch64 expects 65536)');
try {
  fs.closeSync(fs.openSync('/tmp', c.O_RDONLY | c.O_DIRECTORY | c.O_NOFOLLOW));
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK');
} catch (e) {
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) :', e.code, '<-- the bug');
}
```

## Additional Information

### This tracks the build date, not the branch or the Node version

I probed the official `electron-v<version>-linux-arm64.zip` release assets, one by one,
on the same aarch64 machine:

| published | version | `O_DIRECTORY` | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-06-30 | 43.0.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-07-21 | 43.2.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 42.8.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 43.3.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 42.9.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 43.4.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-15 | 42.9.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-16 | 42.9.2 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-18 | 42.9.3 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-19 | 43.4.1 | 16384 | correct — **last good** |
| 2026-08-24 | 42.10.0 | 65536 | **broken — first bad** |
| 2026-08-25 | 42.10.1 | 65536 | **broken** |
| 2026-08-25 | 44.0.0 | 65536 | **broken** |

Two points worth stressing:

1. The break spans **three different release branches** (`42-x-y` and `main`). The only
   thing the bad builds share is that they were produced after 2026-08-19.
2. **42.9.3 (good) and 42.10.0 (bad) ship the identical Node, 24.18.1.** So this is not
   a Node change — `node_constants.cc` picks these values up from the UAPI headers at
   compile time, which points at the linux-arm64 build environment (sysroot / header
   search path resolving `asm/fcntl.h` to the generic definitions instead of the arm64
   ones) rather than at anything in the Electron or Node source tree.

My guess is a sysroot or toolchain image update landing in that window, but I have no
visibility into the release infrastructure.

### Impact

This is quiet and nasty rather than loud:

- `open()` on a directory with `O_DIRECTORY` fails with `EINVAL` — the failure mode that
  led me here. Any app doing a durable-write / `fsync`-the-directory dance on arm64 is
  broken.
- **`O_NOFOLLOW` silently becomes `O_LARGEFILE`, which is a no-op on 64-bit.** Code that
  passes `O_NOFOLLOW` to defend against symlink swaps still opens successfully and gets
  no error — the protection is simply gone. That one has security consequences and
  produces no symptom at all.
- Conversely, `O_DIRECT` now means `O_DIRECTORY`.

I found this because a shipping Electron app (Claude Desktop 1.40609.0 arm64, on Electron
42.10.0) fails to write any of its state on Linux arm64: every private-directory write
throws `EINVAL`, so nothing is ever persisted. Filed separately with that vendor.

Not tested: `linux-armv7l`, which also overrides the generic fcntl values and may well be
affected the same way. `linux-x64` cannot show the bug, since there the generic values are
the correct ones.

author: LinusDierheimer
title: Expose window reference handles (from xdg_foreign, XID, etc)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Windowing systems allow to reference windows of other apps using some kind of platform specific tokens. For example wayland has the `xdg_foreign` protocol, X11 uses XIDs. I am not familiar with Windows or MacOS APIs, but i am sure they have something similar. Currently Electron has no way to get these for own windows, so they cannot be exported to other applications.

An example (and the motivation for this issue) are XDG Desktop portals. They describe the reasoning here: https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/window-identifiers.html. As of now, using portals from within an Electron application requires passing an empty string as the window identifier, so dialogs do not get placed correctly.

Internally, they are already detected and used by chromium and electron (via [`ExportWindowHandle`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/4ae8411d3e994ca1445c358a858f16fc9bdf40e2/ui/linux/linux_ui_delegate.h#L44)), so it shoud merely be a case of exposing them on a public API.

### Proposed Solution

Add a method to `BaseWindow` that returns the platform dependent window identifier handle.

### Alternatives Considered

Use `getNativeWindowHandle`, and write platform specific code that somehow talks witht the compositor itself.

### Additional Information

_No response_

author: sethwebster
title: [Bug]: webContents.debugger use-after-free: cppgc-managed Debugger never detaches its DevToolsAgentHostClient, crashing the browser process
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.5.0 (also reproduced on 43.4.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6.2

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — the affected code path was introduced with the cppgc/Oilpan migration of `electron::api::Debugger`

### Expected Behavior

Attaching `webContents.debugger` to a WebContents (in our case, `<webview>` guest contents), receiving CDP notifications, and later letting the WebContents be destroyed should never crash the browser process, regardless of GC timing.

### Actual Behavior

The browser process segfaults (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS / KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` at `0x10`/`0x18` — a null/dangling pointer plus member offset) on `CrBrowserMain`. We collected three crashes in one day across two Electron versions (41.5.0 and 43.4.1), in two distinct but related signatures.

**Signature A (2 of 3 crashes) — inbound CDP notification dispatched to a freed client** (symbolicated from macOS `.ips` via breakpad symbols, Electron 41.5.0):

```
0  content::DevToolsSession::DispatchProtocolNotification(...)
1  blink::mojom::DevToolsSessionHostStubDispatch::Accept(...)
2  mojo::InterfaceEndpointClient::HandleIncomingMessageThunk::Accept(mojo::Message*)
3  mojo::MessageDispatcher::Accept(mojo::Message*)
4  mojo::InterfaceEndpointClient::HandleIncomingMessage(mojo::Message*)
5  IPC::ChannelAssociatedGroupController::AcceptOnEndpointThread(...)
6  base::TaskAnnotator::RunTaskImpl(base::PendingTask&)
7  base::sequence_manager::internal::ThreadControllerWithMessagePumpImpl::DoWork()
8  base::MessagePumpCFRunLoopBase::RunWorkSource(void*)
   ... CFRunLoop / NSApplication run loop ...
```

On 43.4.1 the same crash appears with frame 0 in `content::DevToolsSession::DispatchProtocolResponseOrNotification(content::DevToolsAgentHostClient*, ...)`.

**Signature B (1 of 3) — WebContents teardown force-detaches sessions into a freed client** (Electron 41.5.0):

```
0  content::DevToolsAgentHostImpl::ForceDetachAllSessionsImpl()
1  content::RenderFrameDevToolsAgentHost::DestroyOnRenderFrameGone()
2  content::RenderFrameDevToolsAgentHost::FrameDeleted(...)
3  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsObserverList::NotifyObservers(...)
4  content::WebContentsImpl::OnFrameTreeNodeDestroyed(content::FrameTreeNode*)
5  content::FrameTree::Shutdown()
6  content::WebContentsImpl::~WebContentsImpl()
7  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::DestroyOwnedInnerWebContents(...)
8  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::DetachInnerWebContents(...)
9  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::OnFrameTreeNodeDestroyed(...)
10 content::FrameTreeNode::~FrameTreeNode()
11 content::RenderFrameHostImpl::ResetChildren()
12 content::FrameTree::Shutdown()
13 content::WebContentsImpl::~WebContentsImpl()
14 electron::InspectableWebContents::~InspectableWebContents()
15 electron::api::WebContents::~WebContents()
16 electron::api::WebContents::DeleteThisIfAlive()
17 base::TaskAnnotator::RunTaskImpl(base::PendingTask&)
   ... message pump ...
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Root-cause analysis** (from reading the v41.5.0 / main sources; we do not have a minimal repro yet — the crash depends on GC timing, which matches its "random, tens of minutes apart" occurrence in production):

`electron::api::Debugger` is now a cppgc/Oilpan-managed `gin::Wrappable`, but it registers itself with content as a **raw** `content::DevToolsAgentHostClient*` via `agent_host_->AttachClient(this)`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L119

Its destructor never detaches that client:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L35

```cc
Debugger::~Debugger() = default;
```

`DetachClient` is only called from the explicit JS-facing `Debugger::Detach()`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L126-L131

The only strong root keeping an attached `Debugger` alive is the owning `api::WebContents`'s member:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.h#L783

```cc
cppgc::Persistent<api::Debugger> debugger_;
```

So once the `api::WebContents` wrapper goes away (e.g. `<webview>` guest destruction via the posted `DeleteThisIfAlive()` task, as in Signature B), nothing on the content side owns or pins the still-attached client. When cppgc sweeps the `Debugger` while `DevToolsSession`/`DevToolsAgentHost` still hold the raw client pointer:

- the next CDP notification from the renderer dispatches into freed memory (**Signature A** — easy to hit with chatty domains like `Network.enable` / `Log.enable` / `Page.startScreencast`), or
- a later WebContents-tree teardown reaches `ForceDetachAllSessionsImpl()`, which invokes `client->AgentHostClosed()` on freed memory (**Signature B**). Sweep order between the `api::WebContents` and its `Debugger` in the same GC cycle is unspecified, so the Debugger can be gone by the time the WebContents teardown runs.

The bug is still present on `main` — `Debugger::~Debugger() = default;`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L36

Before the cppgc migration this was masked because the wrappable's deterministic destruction paths differed; with Oilpan, destruction is decoupled from the last use, so the raw client pointer in content outlives the object.

**Suggested fix**: ensure the client is detached before the object can be reclaimed — e.g. call `agent_host_->DetachClient(this)` in `~Debugger()` (mirroring `Detach()`), and/or detach in a `WebContentsDestroyed()` observer hook so the session never survives its client.

**Context in which we hit this**: our app attaches `webContents.debugger.attach("1.3")` to `<webview>` guest WebContents and enables `Runtime`/`Network`/`Log`/`Accessibility` (constant notification stream). Guests are routinely destroyed and recreated. Crashes appear minutes to tens of minutes later, aligned with GC pressure rather than any user action. Happy to provide the full `.ips` reports or symbolicated dumps on request.

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 26100.9106 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Electron's ipcRenderer API is not subject to a maximum number of IPC messages sent in a single launch of the process ### Actual Behavior Currently the 2²⁸th message sent from a renderer to main will result in an application crash. I have confirmed this on both MacOS and Windows hosts, and have no reason to believe that Linux would behave differently either ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/weiblen-sh/89de25a5585da083ff86079d299eb92a ### Additional Information This was previously reported under https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/52343 but closed / dismissed as AI slop. From what I was able to gather [this change](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48212/changes/5584e1b10af05fac2758021798e86f46a0267241#diff-d27518b40a822c334189d42f115d0362994d91abfa64ab49daf11093cbdf3623) introduced the bug and was fixing build failures caused by the persistent `rfh_templ` due to enabling the `-Wexit-time-destructors` build flag. I used the supplied repro and left it running until the 29-bit BitField space was exhausted with the MSVC debugger attached and sure enough this crash manifests at precisely the 2²⁹th instantiated `ObjectTemplate`: I wish I had a faster way to repro this for you but ~80k IPC messages / sec was the peak I could reach which takes ~1 hour to crash.

author: appdevopts
title: [Bug] Native addons deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` abort during GC on Node 24.19.0 / 24.20.0
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.11.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3.1 

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.10.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A native addon deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` should not abort the process when its wrapped JS object is garbage collected.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading to 42.11.0 the main process aborts with SIGABRT from inside a V8 first-pass weak callback. The crash happens on a `worker_threads` thread of the main process. Symbolized frames from the minidump:

```
libsystem_kernel      __pthread_kill
libsystem_c           abort
Electron Framework    node::Assert(node::AssertionInfo const&)                        node_errors.cc
Electron Framework    node::RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(v8::Isolate*, void (*)(void*), void*) + 220
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 312
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 12
Electron Framework    v8::internal::GlobalHandles::InvokeFirstPassWeakCallbacks()
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Heap::CollectGarbage(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::CollectGarbageAndRetryAllocation(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawSlowPath(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration(...)
                      [JS frames]
Electron Framework    node::worker::MessagePort::OnMessage(...)
Electron Framework    node::worker::Worker::StartThread(...)
```

The addon is a fork of better-sqlite3; its `Statement` class derives from `node::ObjectWrap`. The destructor itself contains no Node API calls — the call to `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` comes from the inlined `node::ObjectWrap::~ObjectWrap()`.

We have not captured the process stderr, so we do not have the printed assertion text. In Node v24.19.0 the only CHECK in `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` is `CHECK_NOT_NULL(env)` at `src/api/hooks.cc:142`.

**Root cause**

42.11.0 updated Node.js to v24.19.0 (#52634).

v24.19.0 backported nodejs/node#63642 (`4b5eb7b72d`, "src: add cleanup hooks to `node::ObjectWrap`"), which makes the `node::ObjectWrap` constructor and destructor call `AddEnvironmentCleanupHook` / `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook`. `ObjectWrap` is header-only, so this call is compiled into any addon built against these headers.

v24.19.0 does not include nodejs/node#63985 (`1723773d41`, "src: keep global list of addon-provided cleanup hooks"), which reworks `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` to resolve the hook through a global registry instead of the current `Environment`. From that commit message:

> This occasionally breaks down when `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook()` is called during garbage collection -- which would be an expected use case of the functionality, but one that has not been covered through our tests before 215027c8eded2e.

In v24.19.0 and v24.20.0, `src/api/hooks.cc` still has:

```cpp
void RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(Isolate* isolate,
                                  CleanupHook fun,
                                  void* arg) {
  Environment* env = Environment::GetCurrent(isolate);
  CHECK_NOT_NULL(env);
  env->RemoveCleanupHook(fun, arg);
}
```

and `Environment::GetCurrent(v8::Isolate*)` in `src/env-inl.h` returns `nullptr` when `isolate->InContext()` is false, which is the case while V8 invokes first-pass weak callbacks.

**Affected branches**

From `DEPS`: `main`, `45-x-y`, `44-x-y` and `43-x-y` are on Node v24.20.0; `42-x-y` is on v24.19.0. Both Node versions contain #63642 without #63985.

**Upstream status (checked 2026-09-02)**

- nodejs/node#65042, the `[v24.x backport]` of #63985, is open and labelled `blocked`. Last activity 2026-08-13.
- It is blocked on nodejs/node#65195 / #65630, a use-after-free in `CleanupHookThunkRun` arising from the interaction of #63642 and #63985. #65630 is still open.
- nodejs/node#65446 tracks the 24.19.0 side of this.

So #63985 does not appear to be independently applicable: nodejs/node#65195 reports that it is what introduces the use-after-free that #65630 fixes.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Filing this for visibility. Whether and how to address it before Node ships a fixed v24.x is entirely up to the Electron maintainers.

The crashing class derives from `node::ObjectWrap`, so the trigger is the `ObjectWrap` destructor path rather than anything specific to this addon — any addon rebuilt against 24.19.0+ headers should be affected.

author: robin24
title: Backport Chromium fix for wrong macOS AX line number / line range (crbug 423048796) to 42-x-y and 43-x-y
body:
### What is being requested

Please backport Chromium commit 36ac8f31796a392340f7914d1018c3a885fc183f
("Fix wrong line number and range when using macOS Accessibility in text fields/areas",
https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8092671, https://crbug.com/423048796)
to the 42-x-y and 43-x-y release lines. It first shipped in Chromium 152 (Electron 44).

### Why

This is the bug reported in #47393 (closed as upstream in June 2025; the reporter then filed
crbug 423048796, which is now fixed). On macOS, `AXLineForIndex` returns the next line's number
unless the caret is at the start of a line, and the legacy `AXRangeForLine` handler returns nil for
every line except the first. VoiceOver uses these to put the current line on a Braille display, so
in every Electron app with a multi-line text field (native `<textarea>` included) Braille users see
the wrong line, a stale line, or nothing. Blind developers are currently unable to use VS Code
(Electron 42) with a Braille display on macOS for this reason (microsoft/vscode#319725,
microsoft/vscode#316018).

### Evidence

Same test page, same VoiceOver, same Braille display:
- Chrome 152.0.7977.66 (fixed): six differently built multi-line fields all track lines correctly.
- Electron 42.8.1 / Chromium 148 (VS Code 1.135, page loaded in its Simple Browser): all six fail.
- Neither `patches/chromium/.patches` on 42-x-y nor on 43-x-y currently carries this fix.

### The change

Small and self-contained, in `ui/accessibility/platform/browser_accessibility_cocoa.mm`
(`accessibilityLineForIndex:` uses `upper_bound` with bounds checks instead of `lower_bound`) and
`ui/accessibility/platform/ax_platform_node_cocoa.mm` (`AXRangeForLine:` forwards every line index
instead of only 0), plus a test.

author: riurisniti
title: Renderer crashes with CHECK in DidCreateScriptContext after same-process window.open (regression in 42.10.0)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.11.2 (also reproduced on 42.10.0, 42.10.1, 42.11.0, 42.11.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.9.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Opening a same-process child window with `window.open('')` from a renderer (contextIsolation: false, sandbox: false) should not crash the renderer.

### Actual Behavior

After the app calls `window.open('', anyName)` (same-process child window; the returned handle can even be discarded), the renderer process crashes silently — exit code `0x80000003` (STATUS_BREAKPOINT), no JS error, no FATAL log line:

- if the child window is **hidden** (`show: false` / 1px off-screen), the renderer dies **~0.5s after the open**, with no further app activity;
- if the child window is **visible**, the renderer stays alive until the **next user interaction** (click / SPA route change) in the opener, then dies.

All same-process windows die together and the app enters a crash-reload loop. 100% reproducible in our production app (8x8 Work — large React SPA); we have not managed to reproduce it in a standalone fiddle despite extensive attempts (details below), which points at a renderer-state-dependent race.

The crash is `CHECK(!environments_.contains(render_frame))` in `ElectronRendererClient::DidCreateScriptContext` (electron_renderer_client.cc:138), reached via lazy `blink::LocalWindowProxy::Initialize` — full symbolicated stacks below. Bisected to 42.10.0; introduced by #53042.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/riurisniti/a881f20a9cfca62d3e3738d9f13f5c71

### Additional Information

Appologies for the AI generated info dump - not everyday I encouter such esoteric Electron errors so I had to make do.

Note: the gist is a faithful *environment*, not a crashing one - it replays the exact arming step and both detonation choreographies that crash our app 100% of the time, but survives standalone; see the investigation below for why.

## AI Agent result

The regression bisects cleanly to **42.10.0** and is still present in **42.11.2**. 42.9.3 is the last good version. Since #53042 was also backported to 43.x/44.x (#53040), we expect those lines to be affected as well — this currently blocks us from upgrading past 42.9.x on any line.

Renderer configuration: `contextIsolation: false`, `sandbox: false`, `nodeIntegration: false`, preload on the opener window, `webSecurity: false`.

Happy to share minidumps privately and to run instrumented builds / patches against our app, which reproduces this within seconds on every launch.

<details>
<summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

### Symbolicated crash stack

Identical stack shape (same stack-offset layout) in minidumps from **42.11.1** (`electron.exe.pdb` debug id `7097E67EA20201714C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38bcf67`) and **42.11.2** (debug id `37048362CA69C9374C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38d6d67`), symbolicated against symbols.electronjs.org:

```
v8::Object::Get -> v8::internal::Runtime::GetObjectProperty     (a property read)
-> blink::LocalWindowProxy::Initialize()                        (lazy context init)
-> v8::Isolate::InstallConditionalFeatures
-> content::RenderFrameImpl::DidInstallConditionalFeatures
-> electron::ElectronRenderFrameObserver::DidInstallConditionalFeatures (+0xB2 into fn)
-> ElectronRendererClient::DidCreateScriptContext
-> CHECK(!environments_.contains(render_frame))                 (line 138)
```

I.e. a **lazily initialized script context** (created on first property access through a window proxy, not by a navigation — our frame-lifecycle tracing shows zero navigations/frame creations in the ~1.4s before death) hits a RenderFrame that already has an entry in `environments_`.

### Suspected mechanism

#53042 added the per-RenderFrame `environments_` map. `WillReleaseScriptContext` erases an entry only when `env->context() == context`. `window.open('')` gives the child frame an initial-empty-document context (env registered), then commits the real about:blank document in the same RenderFrame. If the first context's release doesn't match the erase condition (or hasn't happened) by the time the committed document's context is **lazily** created on first proxy access, the CHECK fires. The visibility dependence (hidden child → dies in ~0.5s; visible child → dies on next opener interaction) suggests the fatal lazy init is driven by occlusion/backgrounding work in the hidden case and by interaction-driven work in the visible case.

### Reduction results (in our app, each verified by A/B launches)

- **Trigger is fully generic**: one bare `window.open('', name)` suffices. Reproduced with our production window name/features, with a featureless 8-char name, and with a plain non-portal name. Return value discarded.
- **Child preload irrelevant**: crashes both when the child inherits the opener preload and when it is stripped (`webPreferences: { preload: '' }` override — child provably has no preload; browser logs "preload script must have absolute path" and drops it).
- **DevTools ruled out**: crashes with devtools fully disabled (no DevTools webContents exist).
- Our overlay/portal management (hide/setBounds IPC), a meetings iframe subsystem, and everything else app-specific were individually disabled — the crash persists through all of them.
- The crash also reproduces when the `window.open` is **delayed 20s** until the app is fully settled/idle — it is armed by the child window's existence, not by a boot-time race.
- The `0xC0000005` (illegal access) crashes sometimes seen ~0.3s into the post-crash reload appear to be a secondary cascade — possibly the class of bug #53042 aimed to fix.

### Standalone reproduction attempts (all survived)

15+ fiddle/harness scenarios reconstructing the app's conditions: exact webPreferences (contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, webSecurity:false, preload), file:// and http origins, our full chromium switch set, same-name double-opens and open/close churn, continuous and single-shot delayed property polling of live and stale window handles, iframe srcdoc/data navigation churn, child hide/show/1px choreography with synthetic input events, visible+focused opener, our real ~500KB preload bundle, and app-scale heap replication (~650MB live objects, 8GB --max-old-space-size, GC pressure). None crash. Whatever completes the race appears to be a structural property of a large real-world renderer's heap/object graph.

### Environment notes

- App: 8x8 Work desktop (large React SPA, several same-process `window.open` overlay windows).
- Also reproduced with `--v8-cache-options=none` (ruling out #52988) and with small IPC payloads only (ruling out #53019). 42.11.1's #53329 contextBridge fix did not help.

</details>

title: Builtin spellchecker never marks text typed into a CodeMirror 6 editor — plain contenteditable works; same page fully checked in plain Chrome 152
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu Linux x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not bisected

### Expected Behavior

With the builtin spellchecker enabled (`spellcheck: true` webPreference, `session.setSpellCheckerLanguages(['en-US'])`), any `contenteditable` editing host with `spellcheck="true" lang="en-US"` gets the red squiggle and `context-menu` `params.misspelledWord`/suggestions for misspelled typed text — including one driven by CodeMirror 6.

### Actual Behavior

On a page with three such editables — (1) a plain `contenteditable`, (2) a bare unmodified CodeMirror 6 `EditorView` at top level, (3) the same nested inside another editable — typing `recieve here` into each marks only (1). The CM-driven hosts (2)/(3) are never underlined and the context menu reports no misspelled word.

The marker is never created, as opposed to created-then-wiped: replacing a text node/line **after** typing leaves an existing marker intact. And since only genuinely typed text is marked (attribute toggles / blur-refocus never trigger a re-check), the miss never recovers.

**Why this looks Electron-side, not Blink or CodeMirror:** the identical repro page opened in plain Google Chrome 152.0.7977.82 (Linux, fresh `en-US` profile) spellchecks **all three** boxes, including both CodeMirror editors. The CodeMirror maintainer also could not reproduce on Chromium 152 (Linux): https://discuss.codemirror.net/t/9886. Same Chromium 152 engine, divergent outcomes — the difference is Electron's spellchecker integration.

A plain contenteditable that mimics CM's per-keystroke DOM work (replacing the edited text node or the whole line, re-asserting the selection, synchronously or on rAF) is still checked fine — so it is specifically the live CodeMirror 6 editing host that Electron's after-typing marking pass never services.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mauriciolongo/daeff5511fdc9ea402506a917f1a83e5

### Additional Information

The gist is standalone HTML with no application code (unmodified `@codemirror/view` 6.43.1 bundled inline). Load it in a `BrowserWindow` with the builtin spellchecker enabled and type `recieve here` in each box: the plain box squiggles, both CodeMirror boxes stay clean. The same file opened in plain Chrome 152 squiggles all three.

### Expected Behavior

Signal Desktop (and other Electron apps) should start normally with a visible window and working renderer.

### Actual Behavior

Signal silently crashes at startup with no window shown. The GPU subprocess exits with `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` (`0x80000003` / exit code `-2147483645`). This is a related but distinct variant from the original reports in #32440 which showed `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (`0xC0000005`).

Windows Application Event Log (Event ID 1000):
```text
Faulting application: Signal.exe
Exception code: 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT)
Fault offset: 0x0000000006fefb69  ← identical across every crash attempt
```

Running with `--disable-gpu` surfaces the GPU subprocess crash explicitly:
```text
[ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc:1108] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:416] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

**Secondary issue:** Even after working around the startup crash with `--in-process-gpu`, newly spawned renderer processes (e.g. Help → About window) crash with the same exit code:
```text
Render process is gone
Error: Reason: crashed, Exit Code: -2147483645
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Hardware
- GPU: Intel® Iris® Xe Graphics — Tiger Lake (`PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_9A49`, HP subsystem `87FE103C`)
- Drivers tested: `31.0.101.5186` (Jan 2024) and `32.0.101.7088` (Jun 2026) — both affected

### Diagnostics Ruled Out
- Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS): not enabled
- Hardware Shadow Stack / CET (`UserShadowStack`): NOTSET  
- No third-party AV or EDR (Windows Defender only)
- Fault offset `0x06fefb69` is deterministic across all crash attempts

### Workaround
`--in-process-gpu` flag allows the app to start. `--disable-gpu` alone does **not** fix it (GPU subprocess still crashes).

### Related Issues
- electron/electron#32440 (closed — original report, different exit code `0xC0000005`)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#5721 (open — Intel integrated graphics requiring GPU flags)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#7828 (open — renderer crash on Windows 11)

author: Zeus-Deus
title: [Bug]: new BrowserWindow() never returns under --ozone-platform=headless, then the process segfaults
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.10.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-2, Wayland session (also reproduces with the display environment variables unset)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not determined — only 40.10.2 was available to test on this machine.

### Expected Behavior

With `--ozone-platform=headless`, `new BrowserWindow()` should return and the window should load, as it does under `--headless=new`, `--ozone-platform=x11`, and `--ozone-platform=wayland`.

### Actual Behavior

Under `--ozone-platform=headless`, `app.whenReady()` resolves normally but **`new BrowserWindow()` never returns**. The constructor blocks for roughly 60 seconds, then the process dies with SIGSEGV. No window is ever created and no renderer is spawned.

Instrumenting the main process shows exactly where it stops:

```
# --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+14ms  whenReady resolved
        <- hangs here ~60s, then SIGSEGV (exit 139, core dumped)

# --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+56ms  whenReady resolved
+74ms  BrowserWindow constructed
+133ms did-finish-load
+134ms quit 0
```

Reproduces independently of GPU and sandbox flags:

| flags | result |
|---|---|
| `--ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless` (sandbox on, GPU on) | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=x11 --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=wayland --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |

Possibly relevant: in the runs where the GPU is not disabled, the headless process still emits an **X11/GLX** error before dying, which is unexpected for a platform that should not be talking to X at all:

```
X Error of failed request:  BadMatch (invalid parameter attributes)
  Major opcode of failed request:  150 (GLX)
  Minor opcode of failed request:  5 (X_GLXMakeCurrent)
```

The core dump's crashing thread could not be symbolized (no debug symbols for the release binary), so I can only report the observable behavior, not the faulting frame.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Zeus-Deus/1797bbc852e232e83501db1b35f294a4

### Additional Information

Full reproduction — a `package.json` with `"main": "main.js"` plus the gist file:

```bash
electron . --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-a   # hang, then SIGSEGV
electron . --headless=new            --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-b   # works
```

Impact: `--ozone-platform=headless` is a common way to run Electron apps in
automated/CI-style environments without a display server. On this version it
fails in a way that is easy to misread — the app dumps core on every launch,
which on desktops that surface core dumps looks like an application crash
rather than an unsupported flag. `--headless=new` is a working substitute.

body:

### Problem Description

The Windows windowing system was built with GDI, so it creates a default GDI canvas for every window. This canvas uses 3 bytes per pixel, about 6 MB for a 1080p screen. For self-rendering apps like Electron, this canvas is unnecessary. Since the memory is not allocated by the application itself but by the DWM, there is no simple way to accurately measure and test it. The only way to disable it is to pass WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP to CreateWindowEx. Electron Apps should use this optimization.

Background:
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/20655
https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/issues/11523

### Proposed Solution

Update the document native-code-and-electron-cpp-win32.md

none

title: WebRTC audio call fails with "codec collision" (payload_type 111, stereo/non-stereo Opus) — works fine in Chromium-based Edge on the same system
body:

### Electron Version

39.8.10,43.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Manjaro Linux, kernel 6.18.49-1-MANJARO, Wayland session (KDE Plasma), PipeWire audio.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A WebRTC audio call (Google Chat / Google Meet) negotiates a valid SDP and connects, as it does in a real Chromium-based browser (Microsoft Edge stable) on the exact same machine, same OS session, same audio devices.

### Actual Behavior

The call fails to connect. Chromium's WebRTC stack logs a codec collision and the call layer reports a disconnect:

\`\`\`
[ERROR:third_party/webrtc/pc/sdp_offer_answer.cc:575] A BUNDLE group contains a codec collision between
{payload_type: 111, codec: {mime_type: audio/opus, clock_rate: 48000, num_channels: 2, parameters: {minptime: 10, stereo: 1, useinbandfec: 1}}}
and
{payload_type: 111, codec: {mime_type: audio/opus, clock_rate: 48000, num_channels: 2, parameters: {minptime: 10, useinbandfec: 1}}}.
All codecs must share the same type, encoding name, clock rate and parameters. (INVALID_PARAMETER)
\`\`\`

Two Opus codec entries for the same payload type (111) are generated — one advertising `stereo=1`, one without it — which is an invalid/self-contradictory SDP. The calling web app (Google Chat/Meet) then reports the peer connection as disconnected (`DisconnectedError`, various `EndCause`/`StartupCode` combinations depending on how far initialization got).


### Testcase Gist URL

No minimal repro gist yet — this only reproduces against a live Google Chat/Meet call (a real-world WebRTC service doing its own SDP munging), not a synthetic getUserMedia+RTCPeerConnection testcase. Happy to help build one if a maintainer can point to what would be useful (e.g. a two-peer local repro that forces a `stereo=1`/no-`stereo` transceiver pair on the same m-line).

### Additional Information

- Confirmed NOT reproducible in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based, not Electron) on the exact same machine, same session, same audio devices, same call — rules out a system/PipeWire/audio-device-specific cause.
- Confirmed independent of which audio input device is selected (tested with two different physical microphones — same collision both times).
- Possibly related to Electron's Linux builds not shipping with the same PipeWire integration as stock Chromium/Chrome/Edge builds (see #29115) — mentioning in case that's a relevant lead for maintainers, though that issue was specifically about screen-share, not general audio/call codec negotiation.
- Audio setup: PipeWire, one active USB microphone tested at a time (Logitech A50 USB headset in `mono-fallback` PipeWire profile, and separately a Creative Live! Cam webcam mic in `analog-stereo` profile) — both trigger the identical collision.

title: [Bug]: macOS globalShortcut.register returns true for the same shortcut in two applications
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.8.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 15.5 (24F74) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown; no Electron regression range established ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? Yes ### Expected Behavior If application A has registered Command+Shift+A and remains running, application B should receive a conflict result when registering the same accelerator, as described in the [globalShortcut.register documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/global-shortcut#globalshortcutregisteraccelerator-callback). If shared registration is intentional on macOS, please document the platform difference and provide a supported way to request exclusive registration or detect this kind of conflict. ### Actual Behavior Two separately installed builds of our Electron application, with separate application names and user-data directories, were running on the same Mac. Both used globalShortcut.register('Command+Shift+A', callback), and both calls returned true. The application's success log is emitted only when register() returns true. These are the relevant log messages, with the application identities replaced by A and B: ```text App A, 16:00:56.784: Successfully registered screenshot shortcut: Command+Shift+A App B, 16:01:33.877: Successfully registered screenshot shortcut: Command+Shift+A ``` Both settings pages displayed the shortcut without a conflict warning. The settings query uses !globalShortcut.isRegistered(shortcut); the raw isRegistered() results were not separately logged. We understand that isRegistered() describes registration by the current application, not a system-wide registry. On Windows, the same application logic reports a conflict for the equivalent Control+Shift+A shortcut. No macOS Electron regression range has been established. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information The observation above is from the application builds. This reduced example has not been independently run on macOS. A current supported Electron release has not yet been retested. ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, globalShortcut } = require('electron'); let window; app.whenReady().then(() => { window = new BrowserWindow({ width: 480, height: 240 }); window.loadURL('data:text/html,

Global shortcut check

'); const shortcut = 'Command+Shift+A'; const registered = globalShortcut.register(shortcut, () => { console.log('shortcut fired', process.pid); }); console.log({ pid: process.pid, shortcut, registered, isRegistered: globalShortcut.isRegistered(shortcut) }); }); app.on('will-quit', () => globalShortcut.unregisterAll()); ``` Run two independent processes without a single-instance lock.
